title: Agent Operating Contract
text:
**This is the #1 rule. Violating it has repeatedly taken WSL down and forced a
full Windows reboot.**

- Root cause (confirmed 2026-07-09): the Windows `C:` drive (`/mnt/c`) is **100%
  full** (≈1.3 GB free). A heavy `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy` spikes
  RAM + IO, WSL fails to allocate buffers (`No buffer space available`), and the
  WSL VM dies. `target/` living on `/dev/sdd` (plenty free) does **not** save you.
- **Forbidden in an interactive agent session on this machine:** `cargo build`,
  `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` on `builder_app`/`builder_main` (or the whole
  workspace), `npm run verify`, `npm run check`, `cargo test --workspace`. Any of
  these can crash the host.
- **Do instead:** make code + doc edits only; delegate ALL compilation/tests to
  **Codex or CI**, not this session. Reason about correctness by reading code, not
  by building. If a build is truly unavoidable, ask the maintainer to run it (or
  run it themselves via `!<cmd>`), and only after `/mnt/c` has been freed below
  ~90%.
- If you think "just one quick `cargo check`" — **stop.** That is exactly the
  thought that crashed the machine. There is no safe heavy cargo command here
  until `/mnt/c` free space is restored.


This is a permanent repository contract, not a recommendation tied only to the
2026-07-09 incident. All Cargo compilation/test/lint execution must use the
sanctioned Docker wrappers on every developer machine and in CI. There is no
host-Cargo fallback when disk space or RAM appears healthy.

Run cargo **inside a memory-capped container** so a heavy build can never
exhaust host RAM. A helper wraps this:

```bash
scripts/dbuild.sh test  -p builder_app orch -- --nocapture
scripts/dbuild.sh clippy -p builder_domain -p builder_app --all-targets -- -D warnings
scripts/dbuild.sh build --workspace
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_main
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/nverify.ps1
```

Cargo validation wrappers run `rust:1.96-bookworm` with at most
`--memory 4g --cpus 2`; the dedicated image-building BuildKit wrapper has a
separate 6 GiB memory/equal-swap ceiling with the same 2 CPU limit. They mount
only the repo as source and keep target/Cargo/temp writes on an admitted safe
root (Linux/WSL) or named Docker volumes (Windows). A build that
would blow up OOM-kills **inside the container**, not on the host. Tune with
`DBUILD_MEM` / `DBUILD_CPUS` / `DBUILD_IMAGE`. The durable fix is still to free
`/mnt/c`; Docker containment remains mandatory after space is restored. The
normative runbook is `docs/BUILD_SAFETY.md`.

Native Windows Git Bash is a supported interactive path. `npm run check` keeps
its existing `check:docker` contract, and `scripts/dbuild-image.sh` delegates to
the capped `dbuild-image.ps1` runner on MSYS/MINGW. WSL is not required for that
image-build and interactive-TUI flow.


A `PreToolUse(Bash)` hook (`.claude/hooks/block-heavy-cargo.sh`, wired in
`.claude/settings.json`) **denies** any host `cargo build|test|clippy|run|check`
and `npm run verify|check` before it runs. Commands routed through `docker`
(including `scripts/dbuild.sh`) are allowed. jq-free on purpose — jq is not
installed here, and a hook that depends on a missing tool gives no protection.
If a session started before the hook existed, open `/hooks` once or restart to
activate it.

## Command Contracts

- Do not change `npm run check` without explicit maintainer approval.
- `npm run check` must build the Docker image and launch the interactive TUI path through `npm run check:docker`.
- Keep `npm run verify` itself lightweight and Node-only. Interactive agents on
  this machine must still invoke that contract through `nverify`/`dverify`, not
  run the host npm command directly.
- Keep behavior-preserving refactor validation on `npm run refactor:stability`.


- Do not add AI assistant names, tool names, or co-author trailers to commits.
- Use the configured maintainer git identity and the stored `gh` authentication


- A release is complete only when the same patch version is present on all five
  public surfaces: the release commit on `origin/main`, the GitHub release and
  native binary asset, the npm package, the versioned plus `latest` Docker Hub
  image tags, and the matching public GHCR image tags.
- `scripts/release-all.sh` must finish by running
  `scripts/verify-release-set.sh`. Do not report release success unless that
  verifier confirms the five surfaces, the executable version, and matching
  private GitHub/public GitHub/Docker Hub/GHCR binary SHA-256 values.
- Release orchestration must reject every non-`main` branch and any tracked or
  untracked worktree change before creating a version commit or external
  release. The final npm check must include `builderReleaseTag`, not only the
  package version and `latest` dist-tag.
- The npm launcher must not execute a managed `vendor/builder` merely because
  the file exists. Its manifest must match the current package repository,
  release tag, and asset; otherwise reinstall or fail clearly.


- Refactors must preserve current behavior unless the maintainer explicitly approves a behavior change.
- Do not treat a refactor as complete until affected tests and stability gates pass.


- After completing any implementation, refactoring, or feature task, agents must **always by default** execute a rigorous QA and audit pipeline before considering the task complete.
- **Mandatory QA Steps**:
  1. **Focused Verification via Capped Docker**: Run targeted unit and integration tests for all modified crates using the sanctioned Docker wrappers (`scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p <crates>` on Windows or `scripts/dbuild.sh` on Linux/WSL).
  2. **End-to-End Architectural Audit**: Verify producer-to-consumer data flow, edge-case plumbing, and invariant preservation. Ensure no unhandled error paths, unindexed edge cases, or leaked abstractions.
  3. **Refactoring & Clean Code Polish**: Conduct a thorough self-review and refactoring to guarantee clean, idiomatic, robust, and maintainable code adhering to all repository standards.
  4. **Regression & Resource Safety Check**: Confirm that all related subsystems remain stable, memory and concurrency contracts are preserved, and no unapproved behavior changes are introduced.


- **절대 성급한 가정이나 호언장담 금지 (Zero Premature Assertions)**:
  - "완벽하게 고쳤다", "모든 문제가 해결되었다"는 식의 주관적이거나 근거 없는 호언장담을 엄격히 금지한다.
  - 모든 상태 보고와 완료 주장은 반드시 **실제 명령어 실행 로그, 실패/통과 테스트 출력, 실측된 수치(라인 수, 바이트 크기, 종료 코드 0)**라는 명백한 물리적 증적(Evidence)을 첨부하여 증명해야 한다.
- **철저한 실측 기반 검증 파이프라인 (Empirical Verification Only)**:
  - 코드를 수정한 후에는 관련된 단위 테스트, PTY 스모크 테스트, `nverify`/`dbuild` 격리 검증을 실제로 실행하여 성공함을 직접 확인한 뒤에만 보고한다.
  - 메인테이너가 작업 중이거나 명령을 실행 중일 때는 백그라운드에서 임의로 중복 빌드를 돌려 리소스 락(`lock_busy`) 충돌을 유발하지 않는다.
- **사이드 이펙트 및 누락 방지 전수 점검 (Zero-Omission Comprehensive Audit)**:
  - 단편적인 부분 수정에 그치지 않고, 연관된 모든 상위/하위 모듈(포매터, 어댑터, 렌더러, CLI/TUI 상호작용 등)의 호출부와 엣지 케이스를 단 하나의 누락도 없이 꼼꼼하게 전수 점검해야 한다.
  - 미사용 import, 미사용 함수/상수(`unused warnings`), 대소문자 단언, 터미널 뷰포트 침범 등 잠재적 결함 요소를 사전에 100% 식별하고 정리한다.
- **잠재적 위험 및 데이터 손실 원천 방어 (Zero Data Loss & Deep Defensive Architecture)**:
  - 겉으로 보이는 단순 임시방편(Quick Fix / Hardcoded Patch) 수정을 엄격히 금지하며, 문제의 근본 원인을 데이터 모델 및 아키텍처 레벨에서 분석하고 해결해야 한다.
  - 버퍼 상태 전이, 모달 격리 및 복원(Replay State Drain/Restore), 활성 턴 인터럽트 등 모든 엣지 시나리오에서 사용자 입력 및 원본 데이터가 0.001%도 유실되거나 변형되지 않도록 무손실 원천 방어 설계를 적용한다.
  - 모든 잠재적 위험 요소와 사각지대(Edge Cases, Race Conditions, Mutex Poisoning, 제어문자 오프셋 불일치 등)를 선제적으로 식별하고, 이에 대응하는 견고한 회귀 방어 테스트를 반드시 추가하여 불변식을 영구 고정한다.
- **플럼빙 체크 전수조사 기본 원칙 (Mandatory Comprehensive Plumbing Audit)**:
  - 코드를 수정하거나 기능을 변경/제거할 때는 단순 국소 부위 수정에 머물지 않고, 생산자(Producer)부터 중간 버퍼(Queue/State), 최종 소비자(Consumer/Renderer/Model)까지 이어지는 **데이터 배선(Plumbing) 전체를 반드시 전수 추적하고 검증**해야 한다.
  - 레거시나 불필요한 코드를 정리할 때도 안전하게 제거 가능한 대상인지 사전에 꼼꼼히 확인하고, 제거 후에는 연관된 모든 상/하위 인터페이스의 배선을 안전하고 깔끔하게 정리해야 한다. 이는 모든 작업의 기본이자 절대 원칙이다.
- **일관성, 유지보수성 및 쓰기 정리 비용 완결 원칙 (Consistency, Maintainability & Write Cleanup Cost)**:
  - 코드, 설정, 문서에 쓰기(Write/Creation/Modification)가 발생하면 반드시 그에 상응하는 **정리 및 전사적 정합성 동기화 비용(Cleanup & Alignment Cost)**을 끝까지 책임지고 완수해야 한다.
  - 단편적인 한 줄 수정으로 끝내지 않고, 상하위 크레이트 간 상수 일치(`DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS`, `DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY`, `DEFAULT_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN`), 패키지 메타데이터(`Cargo.toml` vs `package.json`), 에이전트 마크다운 명세(`agents/*.md`), 도움말 및 TUI 팔레트까지 프로젝트 전역의 일관성을 100% 동기화하고 정리한다.
  - 미사용 코드, 데드 코드(`dead_code`), 불필요한 레거시 함수/필드가 단 하나도 남지 않도록 모든 쓰기 작업 직후 전수 정리를 필수적으로 수행한다.
- **명시적 승인 없는 커밋/푸시 절대 금지 (Explicit Approval Required for Commit/Push)**:
  - 메인테이너(사용자)가 명시적으로 "커밋해라", "푸시해라", "배포해라"고 지시하기 전에는 어떠한 커밋이나 원격 푸시도 자의적으로 수행하지 않는다.


This section records the July 8 implementation state; it is not current runtime
authority. The July 10 lightweight-boundary continuation and the July 15
attention-brief continuation below supersede it. In particular, the former
Explore strategy, traversal advisor, mission-control frontier note, `/frontier`
command, status-row frontier plumbing, and `advisor.rs` were later removed and
must not be restored.

At that time, the repo had a locally validated implementation of the July 8 CTF
frontier exploration plan:

- Plan files:
  - `docs/plans/2026/07/08/PLAN_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md`
  - `docs/plans/2026/07/08/DECISION_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md`
- Implemented pieces include:
  - Default-off `[exploration]` config flag and `ExecutionStrategyKind::Explore` selection for CTF/investigation-shaped runs.
  - `EvidenceKind::Lead`-backed frontier persistence, `Frontier` fold, caps, depth limit, dead-probe pivot, and pure traversal advisor.
  - `explore` tool ops for `add_lead`, `dispatch`, `dead_probe`, `solve`, `block`, and `frontier`.
  - Dispatch enrichment through the existing delegation path: broad clone, category focus overlay, parent finding seed digest, and conservative child-result promotion.
  - Mission-control frontier/advisor note, `/frontier` command, status-row frontier segment plumbing, README/ARCHITECTURE/public mirror documentation updates.
  - New files: `crates/builder_app/src/orch/exploration/advisor.rs`, `dispatcher.rs`, and `merge.rs`.
  - Phase 10 lightweight executable contract: `crates/builder_app/src/orch_spec/exploration_e2e.rs`.
  - Frontier cap eviction policy: when the frontier is full, a higher-scoring new lead exhausts the lowest-scoring open node; lower/equal scoring leads are rejected.
- Most recent focused checks that passed:
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh check -p builder_app -p builder_main -p builder_ratatui`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_app orch::exploration -- --nocapture`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_app orch_spec::exploration_e2e -- --nocapture`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_main ui_turn::tests::test_frontier_status_from_explore_dispatch_result -- --nocapture`
- Full gates passed on 2026-07-09 with heavy commands run sequentially and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` where applicable:
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh build --workspace`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh test --workspace`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_config --test schema`
  - `npm run verify`
  - `npm run refactor:stability`
  - `git diff --check`
- Additional 30-point frontier implementation/documentation audit passed on 2026-07-09 with `AUDIT_TOTAL=30 FAILURES=0`.
- Remaining implementation gap:
  - None known for Phase 10 after `orch_spec::exploration_e2e` and the full gate rerun.
- WSL stability findings:
  - Do not run multiple heavy cargo/npm gates in parallel. Previous work likely stressed WSL during concurrent cargo/clippy/test activity.
  - Prefer the sequential orchestrator, for example `scripts/dverify.sh focused`; never invoke host Cargo.
    The checkout-wide lock is shared by WSL/Git Bash and native PowerShell; do
    not run heavy gates from another checkout at the same time.
  - Current evidence did not show Linux OOM, kernel panic, or hung-task lines in `dmesg`/`journalctl`.
  - Observed risk signals: `/mnt/c` is 97% full, WSL logged `No buffer space available @telemetry.cpp:190`, and Windows System logs show Hyper-V WSL vSwitch reconnect activity shortly after the WSL boot.
  - Windows Application logs exposed historical WER BlueScreen/LiveKernelEvent reports, but the accessible records point at older dump files and are not enough to attribute the prior WSL outage to this repo's code.


On 2026-07-09, a rerun of `cargo test --workspace` exposed a reproducible
`builder_main` PTY smoke failure in
`test_builder_missing_model_message_does_not_force_key_prompt_loop` when the
whole `pty_smoke` file ran together. The live editor treated any event pending
after Enter as paste continuation, so PTY redraw/control-response noise could
turn a normal Enter submission into a newline and leave the message buffered.

The fix is in `crates/builder_main/src/editor.rs`: Enter now treats only
explicit buffered replay as paste continuation and no longer peeks at the live
terminal event queue. README/ARCHITECTURE and public mirrors document the prompt
ownership invariant.

Focused checks passed after the fix:

- `scripts/dbuild.sh fmt --all -- --check`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_main editor::tests -- --nocapture`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke -- --nocapture`

Full gates passed after the fix, run sequentially with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`
where applicable:

- `git diff --check`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh build --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh test --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_config --test schema`
- `npm run verify`
- `npm run refactor:stability`

Maintainer requests for the next continuation:

- Continue from the current worktree state if more review is requested; do not restart or narrow the scope.
- Be careful because prior work caused WSL itself to go down.
- Avoid heavy parallel validation while implementing. Run expensive commands sequentially and with limited jobs.
- `npm run check` was not run because, by contract, it builds Docker and launches the interactive TUI path through `npm run check:docker`.


- Provider terminal state, turn exit, and mission state are separate. Model
  `Stop` emits `TurnCompleted`; only evidence-backed verification emits
  `TaskComplete`.
- Queue steering is deterministic FIFO with revision/ack and explicit
  amend/replace intent. Do not restore auxiliary LLM queue prioritization.
- Built-in, agent, and MCP calls share registered-contract audit and the outer
  hook/policy/resource pipeline.
- The explicit `explore` tool is always registered. Do not restore a core
  Explore strategy, automatic exploration scheduler, or passive `/frontier`
  UI/query path; `[exploration]` config supplies resource caps only.
- Dead probes suppress execution but do not reject knowledge; fresh evidence
  resets the suppression.
- All compilation and tests remain Docker-only even when host disk/RAM is
  healthy. The normal image is `rust:1.96-bookworm`; start at 2 GiB and raise a
  focused linker-only retry to 3 GiB only after a recorded container OOM.
- Current architecture and the completed structural reduction are in
  `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/plans/2026/07/10/minimal-core/README.md`, and
  `minimal-core/07_IMPLEMENTATION_RESULT.md`.
- Runtime intent/semantic classifiers, completion adjudication/consensus,
  recovery synthesis, and hot-path replay/state-card/episode-memory fan-out
  are deleted. Legacy control-plane records are read-compatible projections
  only and must not regain execution authority.


- Repeated terminal closures were recorded by Codex as
  `turn_aborted(reason=interrupted)`, with no matching Windows/Codex crash event.
- Do not infer OOM from a closed exec terminal. Require wrapper evidence with
  `oom_killed=true` or `reason=container_oom`.
- Keep interactive commands short and singular; delegate heavy gates to CI.
- Tests must not acquire `.build-safe/resource-lock-global`.
- Capture a secret-free diagnostic report with
  `scripts/diagnose-interrupted-session.ps1` before cleanup or retry.


- Modal return must restore the pre-modal transcript cursor after reinstating
  the transcript scroll region and before saving cursor state or redrawing the
  fixed bottom UI. Reversing that order makes output overwrite the prompt rows.
- Model setup presence is determined from the persisted session config.
  Provider availability errors belong to the real request path and must not be
  translated into `NoDefaultSession` by a short preflight timeout.
- Every UI session starts with auto mode off. `/goal` records a goal only;
  `/auto` is the sole control that enables autonomous continuation.
- Tool/request budget interruption may self-continue only while auto mode is
  explicitly enabled. Submitted queued input wins over autonomous follow-up and
  is replayed FIFO at the next safe turn boundary.
- The implementation plan and validation record are in
  `docs/plans/2026/07/11/PLAN_InteractiveTuiControlStability_2026-07-11.md`.
- Patch release `v0.100.7` is published as a GitHub Release, npm package, and
  `linux/amd64` Docker image. GitHub Actions CI/CD is intentionally absent;
  validation and releases are maintainer-triggered through capped local Docker
  wrappers only. Keep buildx version/checksum pinned in
  `docker/release-builder.Dockerfile`.
- Docker registry login must run before buildx builder bootstrap. Bootstrap can
  pull the BuildKit image, so placing `maybe_login` after `ensure_builder`
  causes Docker Hub authentication failures before the actual app build starts.
- Storage admission floors are fixed. Do not lower them to make a release build
  fit.
- Published Docker application images support `linux/amd64` only. Do not add
  ARM64/QEMU release compilation; Apple Silicon users run the amd64 image with
  Docker Desktop emulation.
- An explicitly requested local release may use
  `PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1` only with an existing admitted buildx
  builder. The script must verify memory<=4 GiB, swap=memory, CPUs<=2, and
  PIDs<=512 before it builds; it must never create an uncapped local builder.
- Full local release orchestration must enter through
  `run-release-in-docker.sh` with `PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1` and use
  the nested Docker daemon. Do not mount the host Docker socket for local full
  releases; Cross and image-build children must remain inside the outer cap.
- Native Windows local full releases may place only their lock/report root on
  C: when `PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1` and the measured Windows guard
  passes (>=20 GiB free, <=90% used). This exception does not apply to WSL
  `/mnt/c`; heavy data must remain inside capped Docker.
- The final AMD64-only local capped publication succeeded for `v0.100.6` and
  `latest`. Both resolve to image-index digest
  `sha256:f5b63639704ba32c083e5424bc669e334a53b16ba790017913a421d07bb61584`;
  the runnable manifest is Linux AMD64 only. The `unknown/unknown` companion is
  BuildKit provenance attestation, not an ARM image.


- `session_control upgrade` supports explicit `technique="auto"`. It is never
  a silent default and is unrelated to interactive `/auto` mode.
- The listener uses strict framed recon, allowlisted bash/sh selection, and the
  fixed helper order python3 -> python -> python2 -> script -> expect.
- Auto is a bounded ACT -> VERIFY primitive, not a CTF strategy engine. The
  agent owns OBSERVE -> CLASSIFY -> HYPOTHESIZE -> ACT -> VERIFY -> RECORD ->
  BRANCH and uses verified custom `text` for evidence-backed recovery outside
  the catalog.
- Retry is allowed only for an exact unavailable-helper marker, helper return
  before an upgraded prompt, or a completed failed probe. Timeout, disconnect,
  lifecycle cancellation, and writer failure are terminal without blind input.
- One numeric session id, command id, overall deadline, phase-local output
  buffer, same-session byte/terminal/pending-operation lease, ledger row, and
  final reply cover the whole controller. TUI direct writes obey the same
  lease; metadata tag/attach/detach operations remain available.
- `pty_upgrade` remains concrete helper-only and rejects bare `auto`; custom
  `text` still takes precedence. Treat `ok=true` as workflow completion and
  inspect `pty_state` for verified PTY success.
- Plan and results:
  `docs/plans/2026/07/12/PLAN_AdaptivePtyUpgrade_2026-07-12.md` and
  `docs/plans/2026/07/12/RESULT_AdaptivePtyUpgrade_2026-07-12.md`.
- Focused validation passed through capped Docker/Node wrappers: 31 adaptive
  tests, 229 shell-listener tests, shell-session/PTY integration, service and
  domain contracts, snapshots, focused all-target clippy, builder_main check,
  npm consistency/tests, and diff check.
- Native Git Bash `scripts/dverify.sh refactor-stability` is rejected before
  execution because its safe build root resolves onto Windows C:. Do not weaken
  the guard; use the equivalent sequential `dbuild.ps1`/`nverify.ps1` gates.


- Image wrappers must resolve the dedicated BuildKit node by the deterministic
  full name `buildx_buildkit_<builder>0`. Do not restore substring `name=`
  filters or first-match selection.
- Reject zero or multiple matching local BuildKit node containers. Recheck the
  exact container identity plus memory, swap, CPU, and PID limits immediately
  before every image build, including both `bases` builds.
- Detect child compiler/linker OOMs with the BuildKit cgroup `oom_kill` counter
  sampled before and after the build. A positive delta is `container_oom`; an
  unreadable or decreasing counter is `postflight_failed`. Preserve timeout and
  storage-watchdog reasons when their terminal path has already stopped the
  builder and a post-stop cgroup read is unavailable.
- Static resource-safety tests and the project consistency graph enforce these
  contracts. A capped Windows validation image build completed with 4 GiB,
  2 CPUs, 512 PIDs, and `oom_kill=0` before and after.


- The embedded `tract-onnx` encoder caused a confirmed child compiler OOM at
  the former 4 GiB image-building BuildKit limit. Image wrappers now default
  to and reject overrides above 6 GiB memory with equal swap, 2 CPUs, and 512
  PIDs. Ordinary Cargo validation and the outer local-release runner keep their
  independent 4 GiB maxima.
- Docker `.State.OOMKilled` is container-lifetime state and remains true after
  the long-running BuildKit node restarts. It must not classify a later build.
  Only a positive per-build cgroup `oom_kill` delta is `container_oom`; an
  unchanged counter is not a new OOM.


- `explore op=frontier` is the only model-facing frontier view. It performs one
  on-demand canonical snapshot read and returns a bounded brief with focus 1,
- Focus is visibility, not recommendation, authorization, dispatch, or mission
  completion. Internal retention scores are not exposed; execution still
  requires a separate explicit `dispatch(node_ids)` call.
- The rendered model payload is capped at 4 KiB after JSON and HTML escaping.
  The brief does not auto-expand evidence records or `evidence_refs`, but
  title/detail are arbitrary lead input. Normalization removes control layout;
  it is not secret discovery or redaction.
- Do not restore the traversal advisor, scheduler, passive mission-control
  frontier injection, or model-request hot-path repository reads.
- An explicit `/status` adds one optional canonical Lead-ledger read to the
  immutable `RunStatusProjection` and immediately reduces raw nodes to the same
  `AttentionBrief`. Exploration-read failure is fail-soft; core status failures
  retain their existing error behavior. No-run status performs no evidence read.
- Battlefield Lite is transcript-only and read-only. It renders at most eight
  logical rows / 1.5 KiB and omits Lead title, detail, parent/sample IDs,
  evidence references, tool output, and scores. Only revalidated ASCII Lead IDs,
  typed enums, aggregate counts, and numeric metadata may cross this boundary.
  This is not a general secret-redaction claim for goal/task/hook status text.
  missing or malformed mission metadata is `OPEN/UNVERIFIED`. Do not infer
  verified completion from model Stop, `Solved`, or run `Completed`.
- Do not add battlefield state to the live status row, model/system prompt,
  mission-control note, background refresh, or an action shortcut. Dispatch
  remains a separate explicit `explore dispatch(node_ids)` call.
- Phase 4 adopted the bounded visibility layer after a deterministic 256-Lead
  test measured the legacy model payload at 121,420 bytes and the bounded payload
  at 1,858 bytes (98.46% smaller); the completion-provenance corpus passed 9/9.
  Live-model solve-rate improvement was not measured and must not be claimed.
- The npm package description is provider-neutral and must contain `powered by
  Rust`; marketing keywords must not brand the runtime as Claude/Anthropic.
  Historical npm `0.1.0` metadata is immutable, but the next published version
  will take its description from the guarded root `package.json`.

title: Architecture
text:
This document reflects the current `main` branch architecture. It is the single, detailed reference for how the runtime is structured; the [README](README.md) stays intentionally short and usage-focused. For a diagram-level tour of the main runtime flows, see [Main Flows](docs/architecture/MAIN_FLOWS.md). Both are internal-only and are never mirrored to the public repo. > **Engine vs product.** The orchestration engine is **`builder`** — a > general-purpose, local-first Rust agent runtime. **`pentesting`** is the > published, security-focused distribution of that same engine: the npm package > and the command you run. They share one binary. The model owns task reasoning; > the Rust runtime owns protocol normalization, authorization, bounded execution, > observations, and verified outcome provenance. ```text user input → deterministic turn queue → model/provider adapter → one tool gateway → authorized, bounded execution → append observation to the turn → repeat until TurnExit → emit TurnCompleted → emit TaskComplete only for a verified MissionState ``` The core is deliberately narrower than the complete product. Its append-only verification provenance. The complete trajectory is stored in the terminal `RunOutcome`; the request-time `TurnSnapshot` is its bounded O(1) projection. Memory, MCP, delegation, CTF exploration, and security sessions use the same tool boundary. Engagement context changes instructions, not tool reachability; resource caps bound expensive operations. - **Model-Driven Work** — The model chooses plans, probes, commands, and ordinary recovery. The runtime does not duplicate that reasoning with hot-path LLM judges. - **Hard Boundaries, Not Hard Opinions** — Schema, scope, permission, secrets, cancellation, time, output, memory, and process limits are deterministic. - **Typed Turn Lifecycle** — Provider terminal state, `TurnExit`, and `MissionState` are separate. Stop is never proof of success. - **One Tool Entry Boundary** — Built-in, delegated, and MCP tools share allowlist, provenance, registered-contract, and schema validation. Hooks are orchestrator-owned; permission checks apply only when a tool produces a policy operation. Ordinary/MCP tools use configured timeouts, while delegation uses its own runtime budget. - **Append-Oriented Observation** — Trajectory and evidence are local-first; prior-run information is linked by reference rather than copied. - **Deterministic Queuing** — FIFO revisions support amend-next and explicit replace without auxiliary LLM prioritization. - **One Security Surface** — Session, process, finding, flag verification, and frontier operations are ordinary tools. Engagement context, permission, resource budget, and proof remain separate responsibilities. - **Prompt Ownership** — Prompt mode owns Enter submission. Buffered replay may preserve typed-ahead input, but live terminal control responses, redraws, and resize noise are not allowed to turn a normal Enter into a pasted newline. Modal return restores the transcript scroll region and its pre-modal saved cursor before the fixed bottom UI is redrawn. - **Lab Session Multiplexing** — `shell-listener` runs multiple authorized TCP, local PTY, and local pipe sessions. A single actor exclusively owns each session's descriptors, command queue, transcript, raw log, and child lifecycle; the registry keeps only a bounded sender and projection. - **Ebbinghaus-Inspired Memory** — Memories carry a *strength* that fades like human memory and reinforces on recall. Faded notes are de-referenced, never destroyed. - **Git-Backed Rewind** — Working-tree checkpoint/restore keeps autonomous edits reversible. ```mermaid flowchart TD U[User request] --> CLI[builder_main CLI / TUI] CLI --> API[builder_api facade] API --> APP[builder_app coordination] APP --> TURN[Turn kernel] TURN --> MODEL[Provider adapter] MODEL --> GW[Tool entry boundary] GW --> POLICY[Schema + applicable policy/resource boundary] POLICY --> EXEC[Tool / environment execution] EXEC --> OBS[Observation + artifact refs] OBS --> TURN TURN --> EXIT[Typed TurnExit] EXIT --> VERIFY[Outcome verifier] VERIFY --> OUT[TurnCompleted / verified TaskComplete] ``` Plain view: ```text user input -> CLI / interactive prompt loop -> terminal-session prompt ownership + buffered replay boundary -> BuilderAPI facade -> BuilderApp turn kernel and provider adapter -> registered tool contract and common entry boundary -> policy-gated, resource-bounded execution -> observation and artifact references -> typed turn exit and optional verified mission outcome ``` Builder is a domain-neutral runtime with a security-focused distribution. Development, pentesting, CTF, audit, and release behavior layers in through context, tools, and skills rather than new core strategy kinds. Hot-path consumers depend on ten cohesive persistence ports: ```text run/objective/evidence/task/execution/outcome audit/observation/lineage/conversation-memory | local persistence composition root ``` Each producer/consumer depends on the smallest relevant port. The methodless `ControlPlaneRepository` marker composes those ports only at construction and dynamic storage boundaries. Implementations and test fakes implement the physical ports directly; there are no blanket forwarding adapters, fallback methods, alternate schemas, or second runtime state. There is no model-backed intent classifier or weak/standard model mode in the request hot path. Explicit event metadata is routed deterministically; absent metadata receives one general strategy. Named profiles may add context, but coarse labels do not authorize or reject tool calls. CTF engagement metadata may select `ctf-competition` prompt context, and `flag_check` remains a verification tool and evidence source rather than a default completion gate. `explore` is always available; `[exploration]` only sets node and fan-out caps. Installed users edit the relevant engagement, flag, and frontier fields through `/config`. The shipped exploration tool does not replace the core execution strategy. It provides a bounded `EvidenceKind::Lead` ledger and explicit dispatch. Stable generated identity is separate from semantic deduplication. Dead probes suppress an execution branch without rejecting its knowledge hypothesis, and fresh evidence reopens scheduling. An explicit `explore op=frontier` call reads one canonical snapshot and returns a bounded attention brief: one visible focus, at most two alternatives, at most two alerts, state counts, and an omitted count. Focus is a bounded PUCT recommendation, not authorization or an execution lock; the brief exposes a normalized recommendation score and basis while the model must still name leads in a separate `dispatch` call. The model-facing payload stays within 4 KiB after JSON and HTML escaping. On an explicit `/status`, the same pure projection is loaded once and rendered as Battlefield Lite: at most eight logical rows and 1.5 KiB, containing only typed counts/enums/numeric metadata and revalidated Lead IDs. It omits Lead title, detail, parent/sample IDs, evidence references, tool output, and score; that is a narrow Lead-prose disclosure boundary, not a general secret scanner for the rest of the diagnostic output. There is no passive mission-control injection, model-request hot-path repository read, `/frontier` command, detached task registry, advisor, or second scheduler. `orch_spec::exploration_e2e` pins the explicit frontier/pivot/dispatch/merge behavior. A deterministic 256-Lead Phase 4 fixture measured the legacy rendered frontier at 121,420 bytes and the bounded brief at 1,858 bytes (98.46% smaller), while the existing completion-provenance corpus remained 9/9. This supports the bounded visibility decision; it is not a claim of improved live-model solve rate. Reliability guards sit below the profile layer. Provider protocol capabilities default native tool support for OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible responses on registry misses, unparsed tool-shaped markup becomes retryable instead of a false completion, raw control markup is scrubbed from the stream, and the markdown renderer flushes long no-newline prose at soft boundaries while still bounding very large buffers. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[Request] --> GEN["Resolve
task-shaped defaults"] GEN --> REC["Optional
named profile / pack"] REC --> USE["Bound
tool scope and budget"] ``` Request to closure: ```mermaid flowchart TD U[User request] --> A[Agent turn] A --> M[Model output] M --> T{Registered action?} T -- no --> X[Typed turn exit] T -- yes --> G[Common tool gateway] G --> O[Observation] O --> A X --> V{Verified artifact?} V -- no --> TC[TurnCompleted] V -- yes --> MC[TaskComplete + provenance] ``` ## Agent Team The core agent team is domain-neutral. Each agent ships as a markdown persona definition under `crates/builder_repo/src/agents/`. Subagents are explicit and bounded. A `task` call selects one agent; its tasks run concurrently up to four per call and delegation stops at depth two. Separate top-level tool calls are sequenced. Built-ins include `crypto`, `rev`, and `pwn`. `explore dispatch` is a separate path. It runs selected leads as `builder` clones with category overlays, defaults to breadth one, is hard-capped at four, and waits for the batch. It does not auto-route leads to specialist personas. Every child uses the same tool/policy gateway, budget, lineage, and evidence merge contracts. | Agent | Default role | Runtime profile | | --- | --- | --- | | `builder` | Hands-on implementation, refactoring, local file changes, tests | Implement + broad local write | | `planner` | Implementation plans and risk breakdowns | Plan + read-only | | `researcher` | Read-only codebase and reference research | Investigate + read-only | | `coordinator` | Splits broad work into owned packets and consolidates results | Coordinate + broad local write | | `investigator` | Evidence gathering across code, logs, commands, APIs, and behavior | Investigate + shell diagnostics | | `operator` | Builds, tests, packaging, service startup, and runtime workflows | Implement + broad local write | | `reviewer` | Findings-first technical review | Review + strict read-only | | `verifier` | Reproduction, build/test proof, and completion claim checks | Verify + strict read-only | | `report-writer` | Reports, handoffs, release notes, and reproducibility records | Implement + bounded write | > Distinct tool-scope is runtime-enforced for `builder`, `planner`, and > `researcher`; the remaining personas share a task-shaped generic profile > (read-only when the task shape is review/verify, broad local write otherwise) > and differ by their prompt instructions. Optionally pin the top-level profile (`autonomy_profile = "ctf-competition"`); leave unset for the deterministic general default. CTF engagement config may select CTF prompt context when no explicit profile is set, but it never changes tool reachability. Delegated subagent contracts stay intact. Defined in `crates/builder_domain/src/autonomy_profile.rs`. | Profile | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `general-agent` | Broad autonomous local orchestration for mixed tasks | | `local-builder` | Hands-on implementation with fresh evidence retrieval | | `ctf-competition` | Competition/lab workflow; the profile references `ctf-competition` and `pentesting-methodology`, while built-in `write-report` remains explicitly selectable | | `enterprise-review` | Strict, review-heavy profile with read-only dynamic scope | ## Engagement Metadata Runs can attach typed engagement context — scope, phase, tags, flag format, flag-evidence requirement, and standard refs (PTES, MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP, CWE/CAPEC, NIST CSF, CIS Controls) — to workflow metadata. `/workflow report` exports it as a Markdown handoff. Local-first and split across two complementary layers, no vector DB, no cloud: - **Conversation memories** — facts/preferences/gotchas distilled from sessions, persisted in local runtime state and recalled into each prompt by hybrid retrieval. These carry a *strength* that fades like human memory, so the store stays sharp instead of rotting. - **Knowledge vault** — an optional Obsidian-style set of markdown notes under `.pentesting/knowledge` (wiki-links, backlinks, tags). A new user-turn prompt preparation captures an exact-byte snapshot and reuses the immutable index when its SHA-256 identities are unchanged. Manual `write` calls may grow it; retrieval never writes or auto-deletes notes. Both layers feed the same strength-weighted hybrid retrieval. **Storage** — Ebbinghaus lifecycle (decay · reinforce · floor, never deleted): ```mermaid flowchart TD N[New memory] --> S["strength = quality × recall × e^-λ·age"] S --> U{recalled?} U -- yes --> RE[reinforce ↑ · reset age] U -- no --> D[decay over time] RE --> S D --> F{below floor?} F -- no --> S F -- yes --> AR[de-reference: archive / tombstone] AR -. recoverable on disk .-> N ``` Kinds fade at different speeds (procedural outlives episodic); bi-temporal `event_time` vs `ingestion_time` lets newer facts supersede stale ones. **Retrieval** — hybrid fuse, strength-weighted, read-only: ```mermaid flowchart LR Q[Query] --> L[Lexical] Q --> SE[Semantic] Q --> G[Graph] L --> RRF[RRF fuse] SE --> RRF G --> RRF RRF --> RR[rerank: phase · recency · task] RR --> W[weight by strength] W --> P[Prompt context] ``` Faded, private, or unsafe memories are held back from the prompt. Lookups never write — reinforce/archive/supersede are explicit, never search side effects. ## Storage Strategy Builder uses one operational storage strategy: local on-disk runtime state plus markdown-native knowledge artifacts. ```mermaid flowchart LR W[Workspace files] --> AD[Source adapters] S[Skills] --> AD M[Conversation memories] --> AD N[Markdown notes] --> AD AD --> IDX[Local lexical + semantic + graph index] IDX --> RR[Contextual reranker] RR --> PC[Prompt context] PC --> RUN[Agent run] RUN --> LS[.pentesting local state] RUN --> ART[Local artifacts and reports] ``` Key invariants: - Runtime state is local-first and does not require an external data service. - The markdown knowledge graph is derived from local facts: notes, skills, conversation memory, wiki-links, backlinks, and run artifacts. - Graph data is a derived retrieval view, not a second source of truth. - Evidence, workflow runs, state cards, and verified artifacts persist through local repositories. Removed semantic-verdict, recovery-route, completion bundle, replay-archive, and curation projections cannot redirect the active model loop because they no longer exist in the runtime model. - Domain methods such as development, CTF practice, pentesting methodology, audits, and release work live in skills and task instructions; they do not change the core runtime identity. ## Crate Map | Layer | Crates | Responsibility | | --- | --- | --- | | Interaction | `builder_main`, `builder_ratatui`, `builder_select`, `builder_markdown_stream` | CLI, TUI, prompt flow, rendering, selector fallback | | Facade | `builder_api` | Thin application boundary used by entry points | | Coordination | `builder_app` | turn loop, provider adaptation, common tool gateway, observations, verified outcome | | Contracts | `builder_domain` | typed IDs, tools, workflow records, engagement metadata, policies | | Capabilities | `builder_services` | tool services, auth, provider support, file/search/shell/fetch operations | | Persistence | `builder_repo`, `builder_provider_repo` | local repositories, provider catalog, chat repository | | Knowledge | `builder_knowledge`, `builder_workspace_index`, `builder_embed` | markdown note adapters, graph parsing, hybrid retrieval, local semantic scoring | | Infrastructure | `builder_config`, `builder_infra`, `builder_fs`, `builder_walker` | config, environment, filesystem, process/runtime helpers | | Support | `builder_display`, `builder_stream`, `builder_template`, `builder_json_repair`, `builder_snaps`, `builder_brand`, `builder_tracker`, `builder_test_kit`, `builder_tool_macros` | formatting, streaming, templates, JSON repair, snapshots, branding/theming, version tracking, tests, tool macros | ## Tool Surface The runtime tool catalog is file, shell, network-fetch, planning, skill, todo, and delegation oriented. Core tools: - `read`, `write`, `patch`, `multi_patch`, `undo`, `remove` - `fs_search`, `sem_search` - `shell`, `fetch` - `plan`, `skill`, `todo_read`, `todo_write` - `task` and dynamically registered agent tools The full catalog (`builder_domain/src/tools/catalog.rs`) also includes web search, memory, verification primitives, session/process control, and compaction tools. Security-session primitives, `flag_check`, and `explore` are all present on the same surface. Engagement metadata supplies context; permission and resource budgets constrain execution. Direct raw storage-query tooling is not part of the active runtime surface. Turn closure and mission closure are separate: ```text provider terminal -> TurnExit -> TurnCompleted candidate outcome + trusted artifact -> bind objective + target + verifier + artifact + freshness -> MissionState::Verified -> TaskComplete ``` The key rule is that a model response may finish a turn but cannot prove the mission. The former completion-adjudicator, semantic self-review, consensus panel, recovery synthesis, and hot-path replay export have been removed. A trusted verifier with explicit provenance is the only mission-promotion path; `flag_check` is the direct CTF fast path. The default TUI renders the response stream and deterministic input queue. It does not maintain a second workflow engine. `/status` consumes one immutable `RunStatusProjection`; `/workflow report` is the explicit offline export. The former bare `/workflow` alias has been removed. For an active run the projection adds exactly one optional canonical Lead-ledger read and immediately reduces it to `Option`; raw nodes never cross the API boundary, an optional read failure only renders `BATTLEFIELD [UNAVAILABLE]`, and no Lead produces no battlefield rows. Core status read failures retain their existing error path. With no recorded run, `/status` still shows goal, manual/auto mode, queue, and usage without an evidence read. Recorded `TurnExit` and typed `MissionState` are shown separately so model Stop or run completion cannot appear as verified mission completion. The live status row deliberately remains limited to actionable progress/wait state: there is no frontier parsing, background refresh, write, dispatch shortcut, or hidden chrome state. Interactive `/auto` progress is producer-owned rather than inferred from the latest conversation after the fact. Dispatch marks a self-prompt turn in flight; successful cleanup captures that turn's final assistant markdown in memory, records a deterministic completed-turn line in the transcript, and synchronizes optional `current/target` progress to the footer before queued user input is replayed. A regular `AUTO_GOAL_PROGRESS` line is observability-only. `AUTO_GOAL_COMPLETE` and `AUTO_GOAL_BLOCKED` are both non-authoritative model reports. Only the typed `TaskComplete` event produced from `MissionState::Verified` (`goal_loss=0`) stops the autonomous loop. Cancellation, goal/auto reset, and a manual user turn invalidate pending completion provenance so a later reply cannot be misattributed to the autonomous turn. Unexpected stream termination also revokes ownership before queue replay, and explicit stop interrupts disable auto mode before preserved input is replayed. Interrupt-listener shutdown linearizes the terminal boundary as stop, reader join, then pending-source recovery, so an Esc accepted concurrently with `TurnCompleted` wins before progress or completion can be committed. Tool/delegated-agent markdown and terminal events have no root completion authority while a nested producer owns the stream. The auto footer is process-level chrome: turn-local backend resets preserve it until an explicit UI state transition clears it. The footer receives a bounded single-line goal projection, while the deterministic progress title does not repeat the goal every turn, so multiline/control-bearing goals cannot corrupt fixed chrome or inflate transcript history. Completed type-ahead inputs carry an explicit active-turn behavior. Safe inspection commands (`/info`, `/usage`, `/context`, `/memory`, `/status`, `/help`, `/skill`, and `/tools`) are atomically extracted and rendered without cancelling the response stream. State-changing and modal commands, including `/log` and `/model`, remain in FIFO order until the next safe turn boundary. `/new`, `/retry`, `/exit`, and explicit `/replace` retain interrupt semantics and take priority over active-turn query extraction. The input buffer rebuilds replay events after extraction so queued messages and the current draft preserve their original order and cursor. Esc cancellation preserves submitted queued input and starts its FIFO replay after stream cleanup; Ctrl+C remains the explicit clear-buffer interrupt. Accepting Enter during an active turn also queues the same bounded `❯ …` transcript line as the live prompt. That edge belongs to the originating buffer update, while the output actor defers its bytes until prompt/status ownership and partial streaming output reach a safe boundary. The live editor and active-turn buffer share the same bounded process-local submission history. Outside an open slash palette, Up recalls older messages immediately in the fixed input row, Down walks toward the latest entry and then restores the original draft; recalled navigation is reduced to draft state and never replays stale arrow events at the next prompt boundary. An accepted Esc/Ctrl+C writes exactly one durable `Interrupted ` event before cancellation cleanup begins. Cleanup may update fixed chrome or report a distinct auto-mode stop, but it must not append a `Cancelling`/`Interrupted` pair for the same interrupt. Esc cleanup drains that line before FIFO replay; editor replay and queue acknowledgement cannot hide it or print it twice. A conversation reset consumes `/new` but retains its FIFO tail for the new conversation. Modal prompts isolate that pre-existing tail from widget input and expose it again only after modal ownership ends. Commands that eventually open a modal keep the outer interrupt listener during their asynchronous prefetch and persistence phases. Before the widget starts, the terminal session requests a reader pause and waits for its acknowledgement; the reader resumes after modal ownership ends. Type-ahead is therefore buffered FIFO instead of racing or leaking into a later model, agent, or configuration field. Service-layer approval, secret, selection, and follow-up prompts acquire the same lifetime-bound modal handoff through the prompt-entry hook, and concurrent service prompts are serialized so two widgets never read stdin at once. `/resume` is the canonical saved-session selector; `/conversation` and `/conversations` remain compatibility aliases. The selector includes every conversation with persisted context, even when it has no title. Resuming a different conversation clears the process-local goal and forces auto mode off, so state from the previous session cannot drive the resumed one accidentally. `/new` applies the same process-local goal/auto reset at the fresh-session boundary while preserving the queued FIFO tail. Persisted titles are reduced to one bounded control-free selector row before that row is bound to its typed conversation ID. Local upserts stamp the activity time used by `/resume`, `--continue`, and `conversation resume ` ordering. The command remains FIFO-queued while a turn is active because its selector is a modal terminal owner. Normal `/exit` and empty-prompt Ctrl+D termination are serialized through the output actor. It rejects new writes, completes its current render batch, resets styles and terminal modes, restores the full scroll region, clears the tracked multiline footer, shows the cursor, disables raw mode, and drops the terminal surface before printing one plain saved-session message. The shutdown acknowledgement and actor join occur after that message, so no detached redraw can overwrite terminal cleanup. The generic `restore_terminal` function is a best-effort fallback for failures outside this coordinated path. An empty session reports that no resumable messages were created instead of promising a session that the repository intentionally excludes from the resume list. Typing `/` opens the complete registered command catalog. Search includes canonical names and aliases; Up/Down changes the selection, and Enter inserts the selected template into the editor for partial matches and commands that require arguments. A later Enter submits that populated input; a fully typed exact command that needs no expansion submits normally. Palette descriptions expose `[now]`, `[queued]`, and `[interrupt]` so the queue behavior is visible before submission. The selected entry is rendered as the first hint row so it remains visible when the terminal can show only a constrained input viewport. Pentesting and Builder share the **same Rust runtime binary**. The `pentesting` npm package is a thin distribution facade: ```text npm install -g pentesting │ ▼ pentesting CLI (Node.js shim) │ resolves or downloads the matching Builder release asset ▼ Builder binary (Rust) ← single runtime engine │ PENTESTING_PRODUCT_NAME=pentesting ▼ Interactive TUI with "pentesting" banner ``` - The npm package installs a launcher, **not** a second agent runtime. - It resolves or downloads the correct release asset from `agnusdei1207/pentesting-public`. - A managed local binary is reused only when its manifest repository, release tag, and asset match the current npm package. A stale managed binary is reinstalled or rejected instead of being executed silently. - It forwards arguments directly into the Rust binary — no command translation or compatibility shims. - If a change would add orchestration, memory, or prompt logic into the npm layer, that change belongs upstream in the Rust runtime. The npm launcher currently resolves a managed native release asset for Linux x64. Docker is the recommended runtime on Windows and macOS. Published Docker images support `linux/amd64` only; Apple Silicon Macs use Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. Native ARM64 images and binaries are not supported. Advanced users may set `PENTESTING_BIN` to a locally supplied compatible binary. | OS | CPU | Release asset | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux | x64 | `pentesting-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` | `/update` (and the npm postinstall) resolves the matching asset for the current supported OS/CPU target from `agnusdei1207/pentesting-public`. Compilation is outside the application runtime boundary and is always executed through resource-capped Docker wrappers. Host Cargo is not an emergency fallback. `dbuild.sh` owns individual Cargo commands, `dverify.sh` owns sequential gate profiles, and `dbuild-image.sh` owns BuildKit. Each path shares and structured failure reports. Automated CI/CD is disabled; maintainers invoke these wrappers explicitly. The normative contract is [Docker-only build safety](https://github.com/agnusdei1207/pentesting/blob/main/docs/BUILD_SAFETY.md). Patch publication performs one Cross build. The version-checked, checksummed AMD64 musl artifact is uploaded to GitHub and packaged into Docker from a minimal context; its dependency cache stays in a versioned Docker volume. The release is complete only after the final verifier confirms the release commit on `origin/main`, the GitHub release asset, npm version and `latest` dist-tag, Docker Hub and public GHCR version and `latest` tags, executable versions, and matching GitHub/Docker Hub/GHCR binary SHA-256 values. The measured next-stage simplification and deletion plan is indexed at [Minimal Core plan](https://github.com/agnusdei1207/pentesting/blob/main/docs/plans/2026/07/10/minimal-core/README.md). The concrete PTY actor, unified security-tool surface, turn-trajectory, and dead-path reduction is recorded in [the 2026-07-10 implementation report](docs/plans/2026/07/10/IMPLEMENTATION_LightweightCoreRefactor_2026-07-10.md). ## Configuration Pentesting reads a user-global config from `~/.pentesting/.pentesting.toml`, overridden by project-local `.pentesting.toml` files discovered by walking up from the working directory. Local storage is the default; normal setup only needs the public model endpoint environment. The full file shape is represented in `builder.schema.json`; common runtime and CTF fields are editable through `/config`. Set `PENTESTING_CONFIG` to override the global config directory. | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | API key or gateway token for OpenAI-compatible providers. | | `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible base URL, for example `https://api.openai.com/v1` or a self-hosted gateway. | | `OPENAI_MODEL` | Default model id. | | `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` | Optional output-token override; accepts values like `4096`, `32k`, or `1M`. | | `PENTESTING_BIN` | Use an already-installed Builder binary instead of the managed download. | | `PENTESTING_PRODUCT_NAME` | Runtime banner label. The `pentesting` launcher sets this to `pentesting` automatically. | | `PENTESTING_REPO` | Override the public release repo used for binary downloads. Defaults to `agnusdei1207/pentesting-public`. | | `PENTESTING_SKIP_DOWNLOAD` | Skip the postinstall binary download. Useful in CI or when `PENTESTING_BIN` will be provided later. | | `PENTESTING_CONFIG` | Override the global config directory. | The next-generation runtime accepts one product namespace. Configuration uses `PENTESTING_*`, `~/.pentesting/.pentesting.toml`, and project-local `.pentesting.toml`. `BUILDER_*`, `.builder.toml`, `.builder/`, JSON config fallbacks, and runtime alias translation have been removed. Existing users must move data explicitly before upgrading; the runtime does not carry a permanent old/new branch. ## Interactive Commands Inside an interactive session, these commands inspect and drive runtime state (`/help` lists the full set): ```text /status Show goal/mode/queue, turn vs mission, run gates, budgets, and a bounded read-only battlefield /workflow report Export the active run, engagement metadata, evidence, and large outputs to Markdown /context Show recent context-budget snapshots for the current conversation /memory Show stored conversation memories for the current conversation /tools List the currently available tools and schemas /agent Switch the active agent /resume Resume a saved session for the active workspace /goal Set the active goal without enabling autonomous mode /update Download and apply the latest public release asset for supported native targets /help Show all commands /exit Save the session, restore the terminal, and quit ``` Six built-in skills ship with the runtime: `create-skill`, `execute-plan`, `github-pr-description`, `ctf-competition`, `pentesting-methodology`, and `write-report`. For authorized security work, `ctf-competition` covers callback delivery agility, reliable payload/tool delivery, and interpreter-aware execution; `pentesting-methodology` maps assessments to standard frameworks; and `write-report` turns preserved evidence into reproducible CTF and penetration-test writeups. - **PTES** (Penetration Testing Execution Standard) - **MITRE ATT&CK** tactics and techniques - **OWASP** Top 10 and Testing Guide - **CWE/CAPEC** weakness and attack pattern catalogs - **NIST CSF** and **CIS Controls** ```bash pentesting shell-listener --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 4444 --extra-ports 8443,9001 ``` Up to 32 unique primary/additional ports bind concurrently and share one monotonic session-id sequence; an unavailable port is skipped as long as at least one requested port binds. `shell-session --json health` reports the active bound endpoints so callback selection can be evidence-based. The remote-bind safety gate remains unchanged. Manages multiple accepted TCP sessions with per-session routing, buffered output, raw byte logging, full-duplex transcripts, command history, attach / detach events, replay, and evidence manifests. `probe` records the remote's current shell interpreter in `shell`, detected only from `/proc/$$/exe` and `$0`, so a BusyBox `sh` target is not confused with an installed Bash. This interpreter axis is separate from TTY/`pty_state`; it is stored in session state, the `shell-session --json` projection, session snapshots, and evidence manifests, and is restored after a listener restart. `pty-upgrade` sends one concrete helper only; `upgrade` runs a helper plus a probe and records `pty_state` as verified or failed. Explicit `technique=auto` adds a bounded listener-side state machine: framed capability recon, allowlisted `bash`/`sh` selection, ordered helper attempts (`python3`, `python`, `python2`, `script`, `expect`), generic prompt observation, and phase-local probe verification. Only unavailable, early-returned, or completed-but-unverified attempts advance to the next candidate; timeout, disconnect, or writer failure stops without blind input. The entire operation keeps one command id, deadline, session lease, ledger, and final response. There is still no silent default: omission is rejected, manual techniques keep their single-attempt behavior, and custom text remains the escape hatch for unusual targets. A model-facing `spawn` through the default control socket is also the single auto-start boundary for the local no-TUI listener; read-only operations and explicit custom sockets never create a process. Low-level `expect` accepts one bounded non-empty literal and keeps a bounded rolling match window so prompts split across reader chunks still match; the higher-level `process expect` supplies bounded multi-pattern/regex polling. Single-session `observe`/`attach` cursors advance only across committed logical lines. An unterminated tail is returned with `output_partial=true` at the same cursor until it is completed, so incremental consumers replace rather than duplicate a changing prompt. `send` appends exactly one newline and rejects an existing trailing CR/LF, while `raw` preserves UTF-8 text bytes and adds none. Raw logs, transcripts, display-line length, and retained display-line count are capped per session, and closed sessions are archived automatically so a noisy peer cannot grow memory or disk without bound. Secret redaction is applied before new raw/transcript/display records are written; it is not retroactive for output that arrived before the secret value was registered. Bound to loopback by default; `--allow-remote` is an explicit opt-in gate.

title: Pentesting 🔓
text:
Autonomous Penetration-Testing Agent

Local-first, lightweight, and fast. Built in Rust.

[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/pentesting.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pentesting) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/pentesting.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pentesting) [![Docker pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/agnusdei1207/pentesting.svg)](https://hub.docker.com/r/agnusdei1207/pentesting) [![Built with Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-000000?logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-%E2%9D%A4-ea4aaa?logo=github-sponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/agnusdei1207) [![3D Architecture Explorer](https://img.shields.io/badge/3D%20Architecture-Explorer-3b82f6.svg)](https://agnusdei1207.github.io/pentesting-public/)
--- ```bash npm install -g pentesting && pentesting # install npx pentesting # or run once, no install pnpm dlx pentesting yarn dlx pentesting ``` No local toolchain needed. Published images are `linux/amd64` only. The same public image is available from Docker Hub (`ghcr.io/agnusdei1207/pentesting`). ```bash export PENTESTING_IMAGE="pentesting:latest" # published reference or local tag export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://api.openai.com/v1" export OPENAI_MODEL="gpt-4o" export OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS="16384" export BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY="bsk_..." # optional: Brave Search API key docker run -it --rm \ -v "$(pwd):/workspace" \ -v pentesting-config:/root/.pentesting \ -w /workspace \ -e OPENAI_API_KEY \ -e OPENAI_BASE_URL \ -e OPENAI_MODEL \ -e OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS \ -e BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY \ -e WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY \ -e WEB_SEARCH_URL \ "$PENTESTING_IMAGE" ``` ```bash /model # pick a provider / model (or preset OPENAI_* env) /goal 10.10.11.20:8080 get root flag # set the mission in plain language /auto # autonomous recon -> exploit -> verify (Esc stops) ``` --- ## ⚡ Capabilities | Capability | What It Delivers | | :--- | :--- | | **Intelligent Attack Pathfinding** | Maintains an active hypothesis frontier with score-based eviction and outcome backpropagation, ensuring multi-branch attacks stay systematic without losing direction. | | **Adaptive Terminal & Tool Execution** | Seamlessly drives complex analysis toolchains and elevates raw reverse shells into fully interactive, job-controlled PTYs with multi-agent concurrency. | | **Zero-Database In-Memory Hybrid RAG** | Fuses keyword matching, dense vectors, and knowledge graphs in memory. Workspace changes are detected by content on the next retrieval; structural indexes rebuild while an exact-content bounded LRU limits dense ONNX work to unique uncached inputs. | | **Evidence-Backed Mission Verification** | Eliminates hallucinated success claims; missions conclude only when empirical, kernel-verified proof of objective success is received. | | **Complete Autonomy** | `/auto` grants full autonomous agency: end-to-end multi-step missions run hands-free with safe turn interrupt boundaries and deterministic input replaying. | | **Guarded Tool & Agent Boundary** | Built-in commands, multi-agent delegations, and dynamic MCP extensions share a unified security surface with schema validation, permission hooks, and audit trails. | | **Dynamic Context & Memory Lifecycle** | Proactive compaction and intelligent memory retention policies ensure relevant playbooks and session goals stay fresh without context overflow. | --- ## 🧭 Philosophy | Principle | What it means here | | :-------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Simplicity is best** | Prefer the smallest design that preserves the capability, makes ownership clear, and remains easy to verify | | **If it cannot be measured, it cannot be improved** | Instrument outcomes, compare them under repeatable conditions, and let evidence drive the next change | | **The best design is the human being** | Better systems begin with better self-observation: understand how we perceive, decide, learn, and recover, then make those loops observable | | **The agent is the bottleneck** | As AI models advance, the agent framework and the surrounding system must evolve with them | | **Divide and Conquer** | Decompose complex attack surfaces into isolated subtasks and subagent swarms with 4¹ + 4² = 20 instances and up to 16 parallel leaf workers, conquering missions through verified fan-in aggregation | | **Gradient Descent** | Every error and feedback observation serves as a gradient vector, iteratively converging toward the verified objective | | **Evidence-Backed Verification** | No task is complete on model claims alone; only immutable, reproducible artifacts like flags and root shells certify mission completion | --- | Command | Purpose | | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------ | | `/goal ` | Set or clear the active goal | | `/auto` | Run the active goal automatically; Esc stops it | | `/model [query]` | Switch provider, model, or custom endpoint | | `/search` | Configure web search API key (`BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` / `WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY`) | | `/status` | Show the current run and verified mission status | | `/new` · `/retry` | Start a new conversation or retry the last turn | | `/resume` | Resume a saved session from the current workspace | | `/config` | Edit runtime configuration | | `/help` | Show commands | | `/exit` | Save the session, restore the terminal, and quit | ---

> "I believe playing the piano is also a form of orchestration." > > The harmony of polyphony (multiple voices) and homophony (a single melodic line). > > Each voice sings its most beautiful song from its own place, yet when combined, they create one grand, beautiful melody. I believe this structure is no different from AI agents.
