title: Compute token embeddings
text:
Snowflake's Arctic-embed-xs

News | Models | Usage | Evaluation | Contact | FAQ License | Acknowledgement

## News 12/04/2024: Release of [snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0) and [snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0) our newest models with multilingual workloads in mind. These models outperform prior versions of Arctic Embed and we suggest these replace prior versions! 07/26/2024: Release preprint [[2407.18887] Embedding And Clustering Your Data Can Improve Contrastive Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18887) on arXiv. 07/18/2024: Release of `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5`, capable of producing highly compressible embedding vectors that preserve quality even when squished as small as 128 bytes per vector. Details about the development of this model are available in the [launch post on the Snowflake engineering blog](https://www.snowflake.com/engineering-blog/arctic-embed-m-v1-5-enterprise-retrieval/). 05/10/2024: Release the [technical report on Arctic Embed](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05374) 04/16/2024: Release the ** snowflake-arctic-embed ** family of text embedding models. The releases are state-of-the-art for Retrieval quality at each of their representative size profiles. [Technical Report]() is coming shortly. For more details, please refer to our Github: [Arctic-Text-Embed](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/arctic-embed). ## Models snowflake-arctic-embed is a suite of text embedding models that focuses on creating high-quality retrieval models optimized for performance. The `snowflake-arctic-embedding` models achieve **state-of-the-art performance on the MTEB/BEIR leaderboard** for each of their size variants. Evaluation is performed using these [scripts](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/snowflake-arctic-embed/tree/main/src). As shown below, each class of model size achieves SOTA retrieval accuracy compared to other top models. The models are trained by leveraging existing open-source text representation models, such as bert-base-uncased, and are trained in a multi-stage pipeline to optimize their retrieval performance. First, the models are trained with large batches of query-document pairs where negatives are derived in-batch—pretraining leverages about 400m samples of a mix of public datasets and proprietary web search data. Following pretraining models are further optimized with long training on a smaller dataset (about 1m samples) of triplets of query, positive document, and negative document derived from hard harmful mining. Mining of the negatives and data curation is crucial to retrieval accuracy. A detailed technical report can be found [here](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05374). | Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | Parameters (Millions) | Embedding Dimension | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-xs](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs/) | 50.15 | 22 | 384 | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-s](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-s/) | 51.98 | 33 | 384 | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-m](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m/) | 54.90 | 110 | 768 | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long/) | 54.83 | 137 | 768 | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-l](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l/) | 55.98 | 335 | 1024 | Aside from being great open-source models, the largest model, [snowflake-arctic-embed-l](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l/), can serve as a natural replacement for closed-source embedding, as shown below. | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-l](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l/) | 55.98 | | Google-gecko-text-embedding | 55.7 | | text-embedding-3-large | 55.44 | | Cohere-embed-english-v3.0 | 55.00 | | bge-large-en-v1.5 | 54.29 | ### [snowflake-arctic-embed-xs](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs) This tiny model packs quite the punch. Based on the [all-MiniLM-L6-v2](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) model with only 22m parameters and 384 dimensions, this model should meet even the strictest latency/TCO budgets. Despite its size, its retrieval accuracy is closer to that of models with 100m paramers. | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-xs](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs/) | 50.15 | | GIST-all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | 45.12 | | gte-tiny | 44.92 | | all-MiniLM-L6-v2 | 41.95 | | bge-micro-v2 | 42.56 | ### [snowflake-arctic-embed-s](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-s) Based on the [infloat/e5-small-unsupervised](https://huggingface.co/intfloat/e5-small-unsupervised) model, this small model does not trade off retrieval accuracy for its small size. With only 33m parameters and 384 dimensions, this model should easily allow scaling to large datasets. | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-s](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-s/) | 51.98 | | bge-small-en-v1.5 | 51.68 | | Cohere-embed-english-light-v3.0 | 51.34 | | text-embedding-3-small | 51.08 | | e5-small-v2 | 49.04 | ### [snowflake-arctic-embed-m](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m/) Based on the [intfloat/e5-base-unsupervised](https://huggingface.co/intfloat/e5-base-unsupervised) model, this medium model is the workhorse that provides the best retrieval performance without slowing down inference. | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-m](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m/) | 54.90 | | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 53.25 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 53.25 | | GIST-Embedding-v0 | 52.31 | | gte-base | 52.31 | ### [snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long/) Based on the [nomic-embed-text-v1-unsupervised](https://huggingface.co/nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1-unsupervised) model, this long-context variant of our medium-sized model is perfect for workloads that can be constrained by the regular 512 token context of our other models. Without the use of RPE, this model supports up to 2048 tokens. With RPE, it can scale to 8192! | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-long/) | 54.83 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 53.01 | | nomic-embed-text-v1 | 52.81 | ### [snowflake-arctic-embed-l](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l/) Based on the [intfloat/e5-large-unsupervised](https://huggingface.co/intfloat/e5-large-unsupervised) model, this large model is a direct drop-in for closed APIs and delivers the most accurate retrieval experience. | Model Name | MTEB Retrieval Score (NDCG @ 10) | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | | [snowflake-arctic-embed-l](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l/) | 55.98 | | UAE-Large-V1 | 54.66 | | bge-large-en-v1.5 | 54.29 | | mxbai-embed-large-v1 | 54.39 | | e5-Large-v2 | 50.56 | ## Usage You can use the sentence-transformers package to use an snowflake-arctic-embed model, as shown below. ```python from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer model = SentenceTransformer("Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs") queries = ['what is snowflake?', 'Where can I get the best tacos?'] documents = ['The Data Cloud!', 'Mexico City of Course!'] query_embeddings = model.encode(queries, prompt_name="query") document_embeddings = model.encode(documents) scores = query_embeddings @ document_embeddings.T for query, query_scores in zip(queries, scores): doc_score_pairs = list(zip(documents, query_scores)) doc_score_pairs = sorted(doc_score_pairs, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) # Output passages & scores print("Query:", query) print(score, document) ``` ``` Query: what is snowflake? 0.57515126 The Data Cloud! 0.45798576 Mexico City of Course! Query: Where can I get the best tacos? 0.5636022 Mexico City of Course! 0.5044898 The Data Cloud! ``` You can use the transformers package for a snowflake-arctic-embed model, as shown below. For optimal retrieval quality, use the CLS token to embed each text portion and use the query prefix below (just on the query). ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs') model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs', add_pooling_layer=False) model.eval() query_prefix = 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ' queries = ['what is snowflake?', 'Where can I get the best tacos?'] query_tokens = tokenizer(queries_with_prefix, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt', max_length=512) documents = ['The Data Cloud!', 'Mexico City of Course!'] document_tokens = tokenizer(documents, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt', max_length=512) with torch.no_grad(): query_embeddings = model(**query_tokens)[0][:, 0] document_embeddings = model(**document_tokens)[0][:, 0] query_embeddings = torch.nn.functional.normalize(query_embeddings, p=2, dim=1) document_embeddings = torch.nn.functional.normalize(document_embeddings, p=2, dim=1) scores = torch.mm(query_embeddings, document_embeddings.transpose(0, 1)) for query, query_scores in zip(queries, scores): doc_score_pairs = list(zip(documents, query_scores)) doc_score_pairs = sorted(doc_score_pairs, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) #Output passages & scores print("Query:", query) print(score, document) ``` ### Using Transformers.js ```bash npm i @xenova/transformers ``` You can then use the model to compute embeddings as follows: ```js import { pipeline, dot } from '@xenova/transformers'; // Create feature extraction pipeline const extractor = await pipeline('feature-extraction', 'Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs', { quantized: false, // Comment out this line to use the quantized version }); // Generate sentence embeddings const sentences = [ 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: Where can I get the best tacos?', 'The Data Cloud!', 'Mexico City of Course!', ] const output = await extractor(sentences, { normalize: true, pooling: 'cls' }); // Compute similarity scores const [source_embeddings, ...document_embeddings ] = output.tolist(); const similarities = document_embeddings.map(x => dot(source_embeddings, x)); console.log(similarities); // [0.5044895661144148, 0.5636021124426508] ``` ## FAQ TBD ## Contact You also can email Daniel Campos(daniel.campos@snowflake.com). ## License Arctic is licensed under the [Apache-2](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). The released models can be used for commercial purposes free of charge. ## Acknowledgement We want to thank the open-source community, which has provided the great building blocks upon which we could make our models. We thank our modeling engineers, Danmei Xu, Luke Merrick, Gaurav Nuti, and Daniel Campos, for making these great models possible. We thank our leadership, Himabindu Pucha, Kelvin So, Vivek Raghunathan, and Sridhar Ramaswamy, for supporting this work. We also thank the open-source community for producing the great models we could build on top of and making these releases possible. Finally, we thank the researchers who created BEIR and MTEB benchmarks. It is largely thanks to their tireless work to define what better looks like that we could improve model performance.

title: Pentesting 런타임 통합 설계
text:
이 문서는 현재 `main`의 유일한 상세 설계 설명서다. 사용자 요청이 프롬프트와 도구
실행으로 이어지는 과정, 필요할 때 subagent가 붙는 방식, CTF·PTY·저장·검증 경계를
큰 흐름부터 코드 탐색 지점까지 한 문서에서 설명한다.

공개 제품명과 명령은 `pentesting`, Rust 내부 crate 이름은 `builder_*`다. 둘은 별도
에이전트가 아니라 같은 바이너리의 배포 표면과 내부 구현 이름이다.


```text
사용자 요청
  -> 한 개의 agent turn loop
  -> 현재 문맥으로 prompt 조립
  -> model/provider 호출
  -> 한 개의 tool gateway
  -> schema / permission / scope / resource 검사
  -> 도구 실행
  -> observation을 대화에 추가
  -> 필요하면 bounded subagent 위임
  -> TurnExit
  -> 검증 provenance가 있을 때만 mission 완료 승격
```

모델은 계획·탐색·도구 선택·일반 복구를 담당한다. Rust 런타임은 프로토콜·권한·취소·
예산·프로세스 수명·증거 경계를 결정론적으로 강제한다. 런타임이 모델의 판단을 여러
judge agent로 다시 흉내 내지 않는 것이 경량 코어의 핵심이다.


“한 개의 loop”는 subagent가 없다는 뜻이 아니다. 기본 요청은 한 agent가 직접
처리하고, 독립적으로 잘라낼 수 있거나 병렬 탐색의 이득이 분명한 작업만 `task`
도구로 위임한다.

```text
기본 경로
  main agent -> tool -> observation -> main agent

선택적 위임
  main agent
    -> delegated scope + focus overlay + runtime budget
    -> child conversation / run / objective
    -> 같은 tool gateway와 permission
    -> result + evidence refs + lineage
    -> parent가 보수적으로 병합
```

남아 있는 기능:

- `builder`, `planner`, `researcher`, `reviewer`, `verifier` 등 specialist persona
- `task` 도구와 `AgentExecutor`
- child conversation/run/objective
- parent-child lineage와 spawn/merge/retire packet
- broad clone + category focus overlay
- frontier breadth batch의 bounded parallel dispatch

제거한 것은 subagent가 아니라, 모든 요청마다 classifier·judge·consensus agent를
강제로 붙이는 상시 다중-agent scaffold다. child 결과도 proof 없이 parent mission
완료로 승격되지 않는다.


```text
Event
  + active Agent
  + WorkflowRun / Objective
  + explicit engagement metadata
  + optional named autonomy profile
  + recalled conversation memory
  + scratchpad / knowledge snippets
  + selected skills
  -> SystemContext
  -> provider request
```

| 입력 | 역할 | 직접 권한을 바꾸는가 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Event` | 현재 사용자 요청 | 아니오 |
| `Agent` | persona, template, 기본 tool scope | 정적 scope만 |
| workflow/objective | run과 목표 연결 | 아니오 |
| dynamic profile | task shape, evidence rigor, interaction hint | 아니오 |
| engagement metadata | CTF/lab scope, target, flag format | 아니오 |
| policy | file/shell/network 허용 판단 | 예 |
| resource budget | 요청·출력·frontier·process 상한 | 예 |

명시 metadata가 없으면 general strategy 하나를 사용한다. weak/standard tier, LLM intent
classifier, security/CTF/frontier mode router는 없다. `ctf-competition` 같은 profile은
관련 skill과 문맥을 보강하지만 별도 실행 코어를 만들지 않는다.


```text
System context
  product / date / cwd / platform
  active agent / tools / policy instructions
  workflow phase / objective

Memory context
  conversation memory candidates
  .pentesting/knowledge/**/*.md
  .pentesting/brain/scratchpad.md snapshot

Task context
  current user event
  engagement metadata
  selected skills
```

모든 메모리를 통째로 넣지 않는다. 현재 query와 task context로 후보를 검색해 bounded
context만 주입한다. context가 커지면 최신 요청과 tool exchange를 보호하고, 큰 출력은
artifact로 분리하며, 오래된 대화는 요약한다. compaction은 새로운 판단 엔진이 아니라
context 크기 관리다.


```text
provider-native structured call
  -> canonical lowercase tool name
  -> current JSON schema
  -> registered tool contract
  -> policy operation when applicable
  -> permission / scope / resource check
  -> executor
  -> bounded ToolResult observation
```

대문자 `Read`/`Write`, `Task`/`search` alias, patch의 구형 `path/search/content` 필드,
follow-up의 `option1..option5`는 없다. 도구처럼 보이지만 파싱되지 않은 markup은 최종
답변으로 조용히 수용하지 않고 retryable protocol failure로 처리한다. provider별
wire-format 변환만 해당 provider adapter 내부에 남는다.


```text
provider stop/error/limit/cancel
  -> TurnExit
  -> TurnCompleted

objective + target + verifier + artifact + freshness
  -> MissionState::Verified
  -> TaskComplete
```

모델 답변 종료는 한 턴의 종료일 뿐 성공 증거가 아니다. 파일 변경, 테스트, 명시적
verifier, CTF `flag_check`처럼 출처가 있는 artifact만 mission 완료를 승격한다. 예전
completion candidate, adjudication report, acceptance-gate lattice, consensus panel,
semantic verdict cache는 없다.


```text
공통 보안 도구 표면
  + engagement 문맥(scope, target, flag format)
  + permission 정책
  + resource budget
  + verification provenance
```

security, CTF, frontier는 서로 배타적인 권한 모드가 아니다. `explore`는 별도 scheduler가
아니라 `EvidenceKind::Lead` 이벤트를 fold하는 bounded frontier다. breadth/depth/node
상한만 설정하며 dead probe는 실행 경로를 억제하되 가설을 폐기하지 않는다. CTF
문맥은 prompt를 조정하지만 도구를 잠금 해제하지 않는다.

모델이 `explore op=frontier`를 명시적으로 호출할 때만 canonical snapshot을 한 번 읽고
bounded attention brief를 돌려준다. brief는 focus 1개, alternatives 최대 2개, alerts 최대
2개, 상태 count와 omitted count만 포함한다. focus는 실행 추천이나 권위가 아니라 지금
볼 항목이며, 내부 retention score는 출력하지 않는다. 실제 실행은 모델이 Lead ID를
명시한 별도 `dispatch`만 수행한다. mission-control과 model-request hot path에는 frontier
조회·advisor·scheduler가 없고, `/status` 연동도 아직 없다. 모델 전달 문자열은 JSON과
HTML escaping 이후 4 KiB 이하다. evidence record와 `evidence_refs`를 자동 확장하지 않지만
title/detail은 임의 Lead 입력이고, control 정규화는 secret redaction이 아니다. 사람 대상
status는 이 경계를 해결하거나 detail을 빼기 전에는 연결하지 않는다.


CTF에 필요한 복잡성은 제거하지 않고 session actor 내부에 응집시켰다.

```text
listener registry
  -> bounded command sender + read-only projection
  -> session actor
       owns command queue and sentinel matching
       owns raw log / transcript / evidence
       owns resize / close / revoke / GC lifecycle
```

각 live descriptor의 소유자는 하나다. helper-only `pty-upgrade`는 구체적인 technique
하나 또는 custom `text`를 전송할 뿐 검증이나 fallback을 수행하지 않는다. 검증형
`upgrade`는 구체적인 technique/custom `text` 한 번을 실행한 뒤 실제 PTY를 probe한다.
`upgrade`에 `technique="auto"`를 명시하면 listener 안에서만 bounded 상태 머신이
동작한다. 고정 marker로 bash/sh와 5개 helper의 존재를 관찰하고, 지원되는 `$SHELL`을
우선하되 불가능하면 bash→sh로 고른 다음 python3→python→python2→script→expect 순서의
사용 가능한 helper를 generic shell prompt와 probe 결과에 따라 재시도한다. 전체 과정은
하나의 `timeout_ms`를 공유하며 timeout·disconnect·writer failure에서는 blind retry하지
않는다. target 출력에서 경로나 명령을 만들어 실행하지도 않는다.

이 auto 경로는 CTF 가설이나 다음 행동을 정하는 별도 AI 전략기가 아니다. 에이전트의
OBSERVE→CLASSIFY→HYPOTHESIZE→ACT→VERIFY→RECORD→BRANCH 루프 중 하나의 bounded
ACT→VERIFY 동작일 뿐이다. technique 생략은 여전히 거절되고 custom `text`가 있으면
auto보다 우선한다. `close`는 정상 종료, `revoke`는 강제 회수, `gc`는 닫힌 세션 정리를
담당한다. 상태와 기록은 `.pentesting/shell-listener` 아래에 저장된다.


- conversation memory: runtime state에 구조화 저장되고 다음 턴에 hybrid retrieval된다.
- knowledge vault: `.pentesting/knowledge` 아래의 선택적 Markdown/위키링크 자료다.
- scratchpad: `.pentesting/brain/scratchpad.md`의 bounded snapshot이다.

memory strength로 재순위한다. 읽기는 검색 부작용을 만들지 않으며 reinforce/archive는
명시적 갱신 경계에서만 일어난다.


```text
run/objective/evidence/task/execution/outcome
audit/observation/lineage/conversation-memory
                         |
              local persistence
```

실행 소비자는 필요한 최소 포트에 의존한다. 넓은 `ControlPlaneRepository`는 구성과 저장
forwarding 경계에만 남고 실행 의미나 fallback schema를 제공하지 않는다. frontier는
evidence를, delegation은 lineage를, TUI는 immutable status projection을 소비한다.


| 계층 | 주요 crate | 책임 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interaction | `builder_main`, `builder_ratatui` | CLI/TUI, 입력 소유권, session 명령 |
| Facade | `builder_api` | 진입점용 API와 status projection |
| Coordination | `builder_app` | turn loop, prompt, tool gateway, delegation |
| Contracts | `builder_domain` | 도구·정책·workflow·engagement 타입 |
| Capabilities | `builder_services` | 파일, shell, fetch, auth, session 서비스 |
| Persistence | `builder_repo` | 로컬 runtime state와 provider repository |
| Knowledge | `builder_knowledge`, `builder_workspace_index` | note와 hybrid retrieval |
| Infrastructure | `builder_config`, `builder_infra`, `builder_fs` | config, 환경, filesystem/process |

시작 파일:

- prompt assembly: `crates/builder_app/src/system_prompt.rs`
- turn orchestration: `crates/builder_app/src/orch.rs`
- tool gateway: `crates/builder_app/src/tool_registry.rs`, `tool_executor.rs`
- delegation: `crates/builder_app/src/agent_executor.rs`, `app/delegation.rs`
- memory recall: `crates/builder_app/src/conversation_memory.rs`
- session actor: `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener/`


- global config: `~/.pentesting/.pentesting.toml`
- project config: `.pentesting.toml`
- project state: `.pentesting/`
- config override: `PENTESTING_CONFIG`
- provider override: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_MODEL`,
  `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS`
- tool names: lowercase canonical 이름
- workflow export: `/workflow report`

`BUILDER_*`, `.builder/`, `.builder.toml`, 구형 JSON config, 구형 tool alias, bare
`/workflow` alias는 지원하지 않는다.

Cargo build/check/test/clippy는 항상 resource-capped Docker wrapper로 실행한다.

```bash
scripts/dbuild.sh check --workspace --all-targets
scripts/dbuild.sh test --workspace
scripts/dbuild.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test --workspace
```

상위 요약은 [../ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md), Docker 안전 계약은
[BUILD_SAFETY.md](BUILD_SAFETY.md), 문서 권위 구분은 [README.md](README.md)를 따른다.

title: Docker-Only Build Safety Contract
text:
All repository compilation runs inside a resource-capped Docker container. This
is a hard admission rule, not a recommendation and not a temporary workaround.
It applies even when the host currently has plenty of free RAM or disk space.

## Mandatory entrypoints

```bash
scripts/dbuild.sh check --workspace --all-targets
scripts/dverify.sh focused
scripts/dverify.sh full
scripts/dbuild-image.sh validation  # once before nverify on a fresh Docker cache
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_domain
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/nverify.ps1
```

On native Windows, the same Bash-facing image command remains valid from Git
Bash. `scripts/dbuild-image.sh` detects MSYS/MINGW and delegates to
`scripts/dbuild-image.ps1`; BuildKit cache stays in Docker Desktop managed
storage while only small redacted reports are written under `.build-safe`.
The Windows runner detects Docker Desktop's standard VHD locations and watches
the actual backing drive; a nonstandard location must be supplied with
`PENTESTING_DOCKER_DATA_PATH`, and an unknown location fails closed.
Consequently `npm run check` still follows
`check -> check:docker -> docker:build -> capped image -> interactive TUI` and
does not require WSL or a custom Linux `PENTESTING_SAFE_BUILD_ROOT`.
The dedicated image-building BuildKit node is capped at 6 GiB memory with equal
swap, 2 CPUs, and 512 PIDs. Ordinary Cargo validation containers and the outer
local-release runner retain their separate 4 GiB ceilings.

Do not run host `cargo build`, `cargo check`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`,
`cargo run`, or `cargo bench`. Do not hide those commands behind an alias,
another shell, an npm script, or an unbounded `docker run`. `cargo fmt` does not
compile code, but the standard validation profiles still execute it in Docker
so one workflow owns all Rust tooling.

`npm run verify` remains the deliberately lightweight Node-only contract. Any
npm path that compiles Rust, builds an image, launches a release build, or runs
the refactor stability suite must converge on `nverify.sh`, `dbuild.sh`,
`dbuild-image.sh`, or `dverify.sh`.

the sanctioned wrapper. The wrappers accept only recognized truthy values,
normalize the container value to `1`, and record `live_pty_smoke` in the resource
report so maintainers can verify that the opt-in crossed the wrapper/container
boundary:

```bash
PENTESTING_RUN_LIVE_PTY_SMOKE=1 scripts/dbuild.sh \
  test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke -- --nocapture
```

```powershell
$env:PENTESTING_RUN_LIVE_PTY_SMOKE = '1'
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke -- --nocapture
```

GitHub Actions CI/CD is intentionally disabled. Maintainers start patch releases
explicitly through `run-release-in-docker.sh` with
`PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1`, after confirming a clean `main` checkout
and the Windows Git Bash interactive check. The runner admits storage and runs
the release orchestrator inside a 4 GiB/2 CPU/512 PID container. Direct
host release orchestration and unadmitted release-runner builds fail closed.
The release container has its own timeout, storage watchdog, effective-limit
inspection, OOM classification, and uploaded resource report.
Release binaries are prebuilt before the version commit/tag is pushed; the
post-push publication step uploads those exact artifacts without rebuilding.
The Cross target cache lives on a versioned Docker volume rather than the
Windows checkout. The Docker publication packages the same version-checked,
checksummed AMD64 musl binary from a minimal artifact-only context. A full
release therefore performs one Rust build instead of compiling it again for
the application image.
The nested Cross build also fixes `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; the outer two-CPU cap
alone does not stop Cargo from detecting the host CPU count and launching too
many concurrent `rustc` processes inside the 4 GiB memory boundary.
Docker-only recovery keeps the source-build path when no matching prebuilt
artifact is available.
The release-runner image pins and checksum-verifies the Docker buildx plugin.
Published application images target `linux/amd64` only; release builds do not
install QEMU/binfmt or compile ARM64. On Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop may run
the amd64 image through its own emulation layer.

When a maintainer explicitly chooses a local Docker Desktop release, set
`PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1` and select an already-admitted buildx
builder. The release script refuses to create an uncapped local builder and
verifies the running builder container is limited to at most 4 GiB RAM, equal
swap, 2 CPUs, and 512 PIDs before compilation begins.
The full release orchestrator accepts the same explicit local flag only through
`run-release-in-docker.sh`; it starts its nested Docker daemon inside that capped
release container so Cross and image builds cannot escape the outer limits.
On native Windows Git Bash, that explicit full-release path may keep its small
lock/report root on C: only after the Windows admission check confirms at least
20 GiB free and no more than 90% used. WSL `/mnt/c` remains forbidden, and all
heavy build data remains inside the capped Docker boundary.
The Git Bash wrapper converts bind-mount source paths with `cygpath` but keeps
the container checkout fixed at `/workspace/pentesting`; MSYS path conversion
must not rewrite the container working directory to `C:/...`.
The capped local release container also mirrors Git for Windows
`core.autocrlf=true` so its clean-tree precondition does not misclassify the
mounted CRLF checkout as modified.
Release version replacement accepts CRLF but verifies the written Cargo version
before metadata or tagging, and the container inherits maintainer identity from
the existing HEAD commit before creating a release commit or tag.
After local admission and CRLF setup, the outer-only local flag is removed;
nested Docker publication remains in the already-capped release context and may
create its isolated BuildKit builder inside that boundary.
Container TMPDIR is isolated at `/tmp/pentesting-release`, outside the source
mount. The runner copies only the small OOM-reason file into the admitted run
report directory; host `/c/...` paths must never leak into nested BuildKit.
Npm credentials and `AUTO_PUSH` are forwarded to the release container by
environment-variable name only; their values must not appear in Docker CLI
arguments, logs, commits, or reports.
Builder and npm releases share the same target semantic version. Npm staging
source checkout and are validated separately before release.
Release completion is a five-surface invariant, not the success of an
individual publish command. `scripts/release-all.sh` finishes with
`scripts/verify-release-set.sh`, which confirms the release commit on
`origin/main`, both GitHub release surfaces and the native asset, the exact npm
version and `latest` dist-tag, and versioned plus `latest` images on both Docker
Hub and public GHCR. GHCR publication copies the already-published Docker Hub
manifest; it does not rebuild or upload repository source.
The release preflight rejects a non-`main` branch or any tracked/untracked
worktree change before publication. The verifier checks the npm
`builderReleaseTag`, executes both GitHub assets and binaries extracted from
both container registries, and requires all four SHA-256 values to match. A
failure on any surface leaves the release incomplete and must be resumed rather
than reported as successful.
An existing release whose Docker push alone failed is recovered by setting
`RELEASE_DOCKER_TAG` and running `docker-buildx-release.sh image` through the
capped local runner; it must not create another version merely to retry
registry publication.

## Enforcement

The rule is enforced in layers:

1. `.claude/hooks/block-heavy-cargo.sh` parses shell commands fail-closed and
   rejects host Cargo, heavy npm aliases, unbounded Docker builds, and direct
   heavy scripts.
2. Every sanctioned wrapper performs its own admission checks; bypassing the
   hook does not bypass memory, CPU, PID, timeout, storage, or single-flight
   limits.
3. `scripts/check-project-consistency.mjs` rejects new direct heavy entrypoints
   in the repository command graph.
4. The repository consistency gate rejects reintroduction of GitHub Actions
   CI/CD workflow files.

Only exact wrapper invocations are admitted. Parse failures and unknown storage
topology are denied. Image-building BuildKit overrides may not exceed 6 GiB;
all ordinary validation and release-orchestration memory overrides remain
capped at 4 GiB. Compute limits remain 2 CPUs, 2 Cargo jobs, 2 test threads,
and 512 PIDs. Storage floors are fixed at 30 GiB for admission and 10 GiB for the live watchdog. Builds are
sequential under one checkout-wide lock shared by WSL/Git Bash and native
PowerShell, with an additional Windows named mutex. Do not run heavy gates from
two separate checkouts concurrently. There is no host-Cargo fallback.


Individual Linux Cargo gates start at 2 GiB. `dverify focused` assigns 512 MiB
to formatting, 2 GiB to ordinary focused tests, and 3 GiB only to the
`builder_main` link that already has a recorded 2 GiB OOM. `dverify full` keeps
the measured 4 GiB ceiling for workspace test/clippy; use it instead of manually
assembling a full sequence.

The Windows Node wrapper uses the prebuilt
`pentesting-validation:rust1.96-node22` image and never installs Node with
`apt-get` during a validation run. On a fresh Docker cache, create that image
once through the admitted `scripts/dbuild-image.sh validation` path.

The full profile runs the lightweight npm consistency gate first, then format,
workspace tests, all-target clippy, and diff hygiene. Its workspace-test gate
forces strict schema-validation semantics instead of rewriting the schema locally.
Those tests already build the runtime binary and execute the schema,
shell-session, and PTY targets, so the report marks standalone build, schema,
and refactor-stability invocations as covered instead of running them a second
time. The standalone `npm run refactor:stability` contract remains available
and unchanged in meaning.

Cargo target/home volumes persist between Docker Cargo gates. App image builds
BuildKit's checked-in 30 GiB GC ceiling bounds those caches. A fresh machine is
still cold, but subsequent source-only image builds reuse dependency work.

## Storage admission

Set `PENTESTING_SAFE_BUILD_ROOT` to a measured, non-system build volume. Cargo
target files, Cargo home, temporary files, npm cache, BuildKit cache, run IDs,
and resource reports stay there. Docker Desktop's backing data path must also be
measurable through `PENTESTING_DOCKER_DATA_PATH`. Unknown or below-floor storage
stops before a container is created.

Example for a maintainer WSL with a safe `/dev/sdd` mount:

```bash
export PENTESTING_SAFE_BUILD_ROOT=/mnt/build/pentesting
export PENTESTING_DOCKER_DATA_PATH='D:\DockerData'
scripts/resource-preflight.sh
scripts/dverify.sh focused
```

Native Windows uses the equivalent single-entry stability profile:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dverify.ps1 refactor-stability
```

It delegates every Rust and Node action to `dbuild.ps1` or `nverify.ps1`, keeps
their per-gate Docker limits, storage admission, and named mutex enforcement,
and records one aggregate report under `.build-safe/windows/dverify-runs`.
The native Windows formatter uses a 1 GiB cap after a recorded 512 MiB
container OOM during rustup initialization; ordinary checks remain at 2 GiB
and the known linker-heavy shell tests at 3 GiB. The refactor-stability profile
also runs the dense-RAG core package tests and the focused application language
boundary tests at 2 GiB, so an embedding or retrieval refactor cannot pass on a
transitive `builder_main` compile alone.

Image wrappers cap the dedicated BuildKit container at 6 GiB memory with equal
swap, 2 CPUs, and 512 PIDs using `docker update`, then verify those effective
values immediately before each build. They intentionally do not pass the removed `buildx build --resource`
option, preserving compatibility with the pinned/current buildx CLI without
weakening the container limit check.

The wrappers resolve BuildKit by its deterministic full container name
(`buildx_buildkit_<builder>0`) and reject an identity change; substring name
filters are forbidden because they can select a similarly prefixed container.
Zero or multiple matching local BuildKit node containers are rejected so a
second local node cannot escape the inspected limit set.
Each individual image build, including both steps of `bases`, repeats the
identity and effective-limit check. The wrappers also sample the BuildKit
cgroup `oom_kill` counter before and after a build. A counter increase records
`container_oom` even when the long-running BuildKit daemon itself survives a
child compiler/linker OOM; an unreadable or decreasing counter fails closed as
`postflight_failed`. Docker's `.State.OOMKilled` is lifetime state and can stay
true after a daemon restart, so it is not used to classify a later build when
the per-build counter is unchanged. Timeout and storage-watchdog paths already terminate or
stop the builder and therefore retain their stronger terminal reason without
requiring a post-stop cgroup read.

Do not create a nominal second volume backed by the same exhausted system disk;
admission is based on the measured backing device, not the path spelling.

## Failure behavior

The supervisor inspects the effective container limits before execution and
watches memory, PID count, and storage reserve while it runs. A breached limit,
OOM, timeout, daemon failure, disk floor, busy lock, or ordinary gate failure
stops the sequence and produces a distinct, secret-redacted JSON report. An OOM
must terminate inside the container; it must never trigger a host retry.

Automatic destructive cleanup and Docker prune are intentionally absent. See
the approval-required recovery steps in the resource-safe plan before removing
caches or migrating Docker data.

Base-image builds remain approval-gated on both Bash and native Windows. Set
`PENTESTING_ALLOW_HIGH_COST_LOCAL=true` only when intentionally rebuilding the
base images through `scripts/dbuild-image.sh bases`.

Storage admission values cannot be overridden. This removes the former hosted-
runner exception and keeps validation and release behavior identical.


A Codex `turn_aborted(reason=interrupted)` event is a cancelled execution turn,
not an OOM verdict. Capture the product lifecycle trajectory, Windows errors
with interruption-time correlation, relevant processes, checkout-lock owner,
and system-drive state with:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/diagnose-interrupted-session.ps1
```

The collector is read-only apart from its secret-free JSON report under
`.build-safe/diagnostics/`; it runs no build or test and performs no cleanup.


The steady-state application does not inherently need that much RAM. The peak
comes from compiling and especially linking a debug test binary that statically
pulls together provider SDKs, TLS/crypto, image support, MCP, TUI, and test
metadata. `builder_main` demonstrated a linker OOM at a 2 GiB container cap and
passed the same focused test at 3 GiB. That is expected containment:

1. start focused gates at 2 GiB;
2. if the report says `container_oom`, retry only that focused link at 3 GiB;
3. never exceed 4 GiB and never retry on the host.

The ordinary Cargo image is `rust:1.96-bookworm` because repository tests use
Git. The full validation image also adds Node 22. Image size and runtime memory
are different limits; changing from `slim` does not raise the cgroup allowance.
The Windows wrapper uses a bookworm-specific target volume so native objects
from a different libc image cannot be reused. A custom `DBUILD_IMAGE` must use
a matching `DBUILD_TARGET_VOLUME`.

## CI

CI is the default full-gate offload. It selects a measured safe build root,
builds the capped validation image, and runs `scripts/dverify.sh full`
sequentially. Cargo gates use that prebuilt image too, so a cold 512 MiB `fmt`
container never installs a Rust toolchain. CI disables dev/test debug symbols
to keep cold workspace artifacts inside the ephemeral disk envelope; tests,
assertions, backtraces, and strict clippy remain enabled. The uploaded artifact
contains the outer CI summary and every child gate report from the safe root.
The outer orchestrator must first pass the 8 GiB CI admission floor. While that
same process still owns the verified resource lock, child gates may continue at
4 GiB free; the 2 GiB live stop reserve remains unchanged. A standalone gate,
an invalid lock token, or any local run cannot use this continuation floor.
Lock ownership includes the creating PID. A child wrapper may reuse the token
but is a non-owner and cannot remove either the build-root or checkout lock.

The detailed threat model, topology requirements, failure taxonomy, canary
order, and incident evidence are in
[`plans/2026/07/10/PLAN_ResourceSafeBuildAndValidation_2026-07-10.md`](plans/2026/07/10/PLAN_ResourceSafeBuildAndValidation_2026-07-10.md).

title: Development & Release
text:
Contributor-facing build, test, and release workflow. **Internal engine = `builder`** (Rust crates + binary, versioned in `Cargo.toml`). **Public product = `pentesting`** (npm facade = root `package.json`, versioned independently and pinned to a Builder release through `builderReleaseTag`).

---


**All Rust compilation is Docker-only.** Host `cargo build`, `check`, `test`,
`clippy`, `run`, and `bench` are prohibited even when the machine currently
looks healthy. The sanctioned wrappers enforce memory/CPU/PID/time/storage
limits and a global single-flight lock; there is no host fallback. See
[`BUILD_SAFETY.md`](BUILD_SAFETY.md).

```bash
scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_domain            # focused tests
scripts/dbuild.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
scripts/dbuild.sh build --bin pentesting             # final binary
scripts/dverify.sh focused                            # sequential focused gate
scripts/dverify.sh full                               # sequential full gate
scripts/dbuild-image.sh validation                    # once per fresh Docker cache
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_domain  # Windows
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/nverify.ps1                  # Windows Node gate
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dverify.ps1 refactor-stability # Windows sequential stability gate
npm run consistency                               # repo-wide consistency/drift gate
npm run audit                                     # broader repository audit
npm run verify                                    # lightweight Node-only gate; no compilation
npm run refactor:stability                        # Docker-only Rust/PTY stability profile
npm run check                                     # Docker image build + interactive TUI run
npm run check:docker                              # explicit Docker image build + interactive TUI run
```

`npm run check`, `npm run check:docker`, and `scripts/dbuild-image.sh` also work
from native Windows Git Bash: the image-build shell entrypoint automatically
delegates to the capped Windows BuildKit runner. WSL and a Linux safe-root
override are not required for this interactive path.

`/model` can return without replaying or overwriting the transcript, and a
subsequent response plus `Finished` line append above the next prompt. `/goal`
must leave auto mode off; only `/auto` may enable self-prompted continuation.

Use `npm run refactor:stability` before committing behavior-preserving refactors.
The script routes its Rust/PTY work through the Docker-only validation profile.
Node, format, builder_main check, shell-listener, shell integration, and diff
gates sequentially and writes an aggregate report. A refactor is not stable
until the applicable canonical gate passes or the exact skipped command and
reason are reported.

**Drift checks**
```bash
scripts/dbuild.sh test -p builder_config --test schema   # refresh builder.schema.json
```

**Evaluators**
```bash
npx tsx benchmarks/cli.ts benchmarks/evals/read_over_cat/task.yml
```

---


| Line | Source of truth | Bumped by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **builder binary** (`v<builder-version>`, git tags) | `Cargo.toml [workspace.package] version` | `release-all.sh` |
| **pentesting npm** (`<npm-version>`) | root `package.json` version | `publish-pentesting-package.sh` |

The npm facade downloads the binary release pinned by `builderReleaseTag` in root `package.json`. Bump it when a new binary release should back the npm package.
Local `npm run check` images are unreleased source builds, so their banner uses
`<builder-version>-dev` instead of impersonating the latest release tag. A
combined release chooses the requested bump above the higher of the current
builder and npm versions, then publishes both lines at that target; this avoids
reusing an npm version after facade-only patches.

---

## Release

GitHub Actions CI/CD is intentionally disabled. Builds, validation, and releases
are started explicitly by the maintainer through the resource-capped Docker
wrappers; release entrypoints must not bypass the Docker-only build contract.

```bash
PENTESTING_LOCAL_CAPPED_RELEASE=1 \
PENTESTING_RELEASE_RUNNER_READY=true \
scripts/run-release-in-docker.sh scripts/release-all.sh patch
```

Run this only from a clean `main` checkout after Windows Git Bash
`npm run check` has opened the interactive TUI successfully. The local runner
executes the version bump and prebuilds release binaries inside a 4 GiB/2 CPU
container before the version commit/tag is pushed. It uploads those exact
artifacts, verifies their version and SHA-256, and packages the same AMD64
binary into Docker Hub `agnusdei1207/pentesting:latest` and the matching
`v<version>` tag, then copies those manifests to public
`ghcr.io/agnusdei1207/pentesting` tags without rebuilding.
The Cross cache persists in a versioned Docker volume. npm and public-facade
publishing remain separate credentialed workflows.

If the version commit, tag, and GitHub Release succeeded but the final Docker
push failed, set `RELEASE_DOCKER_TAG=v<existing-version>` and invoke
`scripts/docker-buildx-release.sh image` through the same capped local runner.
This verifies the existing tag and only backfills the matching Docker tags.

```bash
GHCR_TOKEN=... npm run docker:publish:ghcr -- v<builder-version>
```

`GHCR_TOKEN` must be a classic GitHub personal access token with
`write:packages`. GitHub creates the package as private on its first push and
does not expose a documented visibility-update API. Follow the command's link
once to change the package to public in GitHub Packages settings, then rerun;
the command succeeds only after both tags are anonymously readable and match
the Docker Hub manifest digest.

**npm-only publish** (pentesting, from a clean `main`):
```bash
npm run pentesting:check                 # validate the package
npm run pentesting:publish:dry-run -- <version>
NPM_TOKEN=... npm run pentesting:publish -- <version>
NPM_TOKEN=... npm run release:npm   # next patch + commit bump
```

Publish is staged via `npm pack` (the `files` whitelist in root `package.json` is the only thing that ships — verify with `npm pack --dry-run`).

**Safeguards** (`scripts/publish-pentesting-package.sh`): fails on dirty worktree (`ALLOW_DIRTY_RELEASE=true` to override), off `main` (`ALLOW_NON_RELEASE_BRANCH=true`), or if the npm version already exists.

---


The public repo (`agnusdei1207/pentesting-public`) is a distribution shell only — binaries, landing page, compose, README. Core logic stays private.

```bash
npm run public:sync -- /path/to/pentesting-public        # mirror root-sourced README/schema/LICENSE/logo
AUTO_PUSH=true npm run public:sync -- /path/to/pentesting-public
npm run public:mirror-release -- v<builder-version>       # mirror release binaries
```

The conceptual `ARCHITECTURE.md`, landing page (`index.html`), Docker Compose
facade (`compose.yaml`) and `.env.example` are authored directly in the public

**Keep the npm layer thin:** `bin/pentesting.mjs` is a launch shim; `lib/runtime.mjs` resolves/downloads the binary and forwards args — never a second runtime. Prefer shell scripts over new JS orchestration.

title: Architecture Explorer — Reusable Blueprint & Directive
text:
A portable spec for building **an explorable 3D architecture visualizer** for *any*
software/agent project. It captures both the hard requirements and the design insights
distilled from building the pentesting-agent explorer (`public/`), so the same look,
feel, and UX can be reproduced elsewhere by dropping this directive into a new project.

> Reference implementation: `public/` (this repo) — `index.html`, `css/scene.css`, `js/scene.js`.

---


> Build a single-page, self-contained 3D **architecture explorer** for this project,
> following `PUBLIC_GRAPHICS_GUIDELINES.md`. It must:
> - render the *whole* architecture as a readable **layered 3D graph**, visible from the
>   first frame (nothing hidden until "discovered");
> - default to a **scroll-driven guided tour** that flies the camera node-by-node and
>   auto-shows each node's description — the visitor is spoon-fed the architecture with
>   zero clicking — plus a one-tap **free-explore** orbit mode;
> - show node descriptions as **floating, borderless typography** (no side panel, no
>   boxes), keep chrome minimal (no title header, no controls-hint, **icon-only** mode
>   toggle + reset), and use one large "<Project> Architecture" caption for intro/outro;
> - be a static bundle (three.js r128 + OrbitControls via CDN, no build step).
>
> Populate the `NODES`/`EDGES` data from *this* project's real architecture. Keep every
> MUST in the guidelines. Do not reintroduce any listed non-goal.

---


A 3D graph of the system's components with **two modes**:

1. **Guided tour — the default.** Scrolling drives a cinematic walkthrough: the camera
   interpolates between per-node "stops" in pipeline order and settles on each; the
   floating description auto-fills for that node; everything else dims. **No clicking
   required** — this is the core insight: nobody clicks 20+ nodes, so the tour carries
   them through automatically.
2. **Free explore — one tap away.** An icon toggle hands the camera to `OrbitControls`
   (orbit / zoom / pan) with click-to-inspect and idle auto-rotate.

The whole graph is rendered and legible from frame one in **both** modes.


- **Guided is the landing experience.** A scroll spacer (`#tour-spacer`, height set in JS
  from stop count) provides the scroll range — the *only* legitimate use of page scroll.
- Each guided stop **auto-shows the node description** and highlights that node (dims the
  rest). Intro/outro "overview" stops show the center caption instead.
  guided taxonomy so scrolling teaches the shape at every scale:
  `intro → each layer (big-picture overview) → every node (individual detail) →
  composite connections (how parts join) → dynamic feedback loops → outro`.
  A stop may target a whole layer (`layerKey`, highlights that layer and shows its
  one-line role), a single node (`id`), or a concept spanning one/more edges
  (`focusEdges` + `loopKey`/`info`). Highlight by dimming everything else.
- **One presentation for all stops.** Node stops and loop/concept stops show their text
  the **same way** — the floating info panel (tag · title · sub-id · what-it-does · trace).
  Never invent a second widget (e.g. a big center caption) for loop stops.
- **Free explore** locks page scroll (`body.mode-free { overflow: hidden }`) so it never
  fights the camera; auto-rotate runs and pauses on interaction, resumes after idle.
- Clicking a node in guided mode **smooth-scrolls the tour to it** (a shortcut, never a
  requirement). In free mode, clicking a node **only shows its info and highlights it — it
  must NOT move or zoom the camera** (the user is looking at the whole graph and would have
  to zoom back out); clicking empty space clears. **Only the guided/cinematic mode drives
  the camera.**
- Mode switches are **seamless** — carry the camera target across, no jump-cut.
- Distinguish a click from an orbit-drag by pointer travel (< 5 px = click).


- Lay the graph out as a readable **top → bottom pipeline** grouped into **layers**
  (typically 4–7). Each layer is a horizontal band; parallelism spreads across X; depth
  uses Z. Fan-out / fan-in must read visually.
- **Data-driven.** All content lives in two arrays in the scene script:
  - `NODES`: `{ id, label, layer, pos:[x,y,z], role, r, color?, crate, logic, data }`
  - `EDGES`: `[fromId, toId, color?, kind?, label?]` in real flow direction. `kind` ∈
    `forward` (default) | `loop` | `backprop` | `respawn` | `auto` | `writeback` (see §6);
    `label` draws an always-on tag on feedback arcs.
  A `TOUR_ORDER` array lists node ids in narration order. Adapt these to the project;
  no bespoke per-node geometry outside this data.
- **Model the true dynamics — verified against the implementation, not a tidy DAG.**
  Adaptive systems have cycles (retry), value **backpropagation**, delegation that spawns
  **new runs**, and a **learning write-back** (record → organize → store → recall →
  summarize). If a real edge exists — e.g. results feeding memory/RAG that later turns
  retrieve — **draw it**; missing connectivity reads as a wrong mental model. Read the
  code before drawing, and put the real cadence in the node text (what runs once per run
  vs. per turn vs. per sub-agent; what carries across turns). Roles that are assigned
  dynamically must be labelled as such, not frozen into fixed specialties.


Lessons learned: every extra box, border, and label is clutter. Strip the UI to the bone.

- **No title/identity header.** Don't put a project name + stats block in a corner.
- **No controls-hint.** Don't caption "drag / scroll / click" — it's self-evident.
  title, a dim sub-identifier such as the module/crate, one or two plain sentences of
  "what it does", and a short live "trace" line. Pure text with a **strong shadow** for
  legibility, **no panel, no background box, no border** (at most a single thin accent tick
  on the trace line). Place it to one side so it never blocks the focused node.
- **Write for a smart non-expert who is skimming the big picture (MUST).**
  - Plain, natural, complete sentences, not fragments. One or two per node.
  - **No em-dashes and no " - " as a connector.** Join clauses into a real sentence, or
    break to a new line. Readability over density.
  - Avoid heavy math, formulas, exact token counts, and internal jargon unless it names a
    real component. Explain the idea, not the equation.
  - The trace line is a short, plain example, not a spec.
  - **Default language is English.** If a language switcher exists, English is the base and
    every other language is a translation of these same plain sentences.
- **Name things by what they truly are, verified in code (MUST).** Do not reach for a
  convenient but wrong word (e.g. calling a *normalized retrieval query* the user's
  "query" when the user typed a request in plain language). Read the implementation and
  label each node for what it actually does.
- **No thin descriptions — earn interest with real, implementation-based detail (MUST).**
  A one-liner that states the obvious is not enough. Pull the actual mechanism from the
  code and let it shine: the algorithm, the key constants, the model, the normalization,
  the data structure (e.g. "384-dim vectors L2-normalized to unit length, so a dot product
  equals cosine similarity"; "strength in [0.05, 1.0] decays as exp(-λ·age) and reinforces
  on recall"). Length is fine when it adds substance.
- **Anticipate and answer the reader's next question (MUST).** If a sentence would leave an
  obvious "…but then what about X?" (e.g. "nothing is ever deleted — won't memory
  overflow?"), answer it in the same description (faded/expired/archived items drop toward
  zero strength and are held back from the prompt while staying recoverable on disk).
- **Multilingual parity (MUST).** Every enrichment or correction to a description is
  mirrored across all languages in `i18n.js`, and translated terms must be genuinely
  localized, not transliterated jargon (e.g. Korean uses 단서/실마리 for a "lead", not 리드).
- **Minimal borders everywhere.** Interactive chrome (legend, buttons, counter) may use a
  soft translucent blur background, but **no 1px borders** — they read as dirty.
- **Icon-only controls.** The view-mode control is a **segmented icon toggle** (e.g. a
  ▶ play glyph = guided/auto, a move/orbit glyph = free) with the active segment filled;
  reset is a single recenter icon. **Inline SVG, not emoji.** Add `title`/`aria-label`.
- **Center caption is one big line.** Intro/outro show a large "`<Project> Architecture`"
  title (intro may add a tiny "scroll to explore ↓"); no long paragraphs.
- **Optional language selector** sits in the same top-right cluster (a compact `<select>`,
  native language names). English is the base; translations live in a separate `i18n.js`
  and cover labels, layer names, node/loop descriptions, captions and UI. Changing language
  rebuilds the billboard labels and re-renders the current panel. Keep technical
  identifiers (crate paths, code-like traces) in English.
- A thin top **progress rail** + a small **`N / total · Node`** counter give tour context
  (this is flow context, not a step-counter HUD). Both hidden in free mode.


- The bottom-left is a **single foldable button** (collapsed by default so it never
  clutters or overlaps other chrome). It expands into a compact panel with **two
  sections** the reader can filter by. When collapsed, the button shows the **active
  filter name** so the current view is never a mystery.
- **Layers** — every layer with a color swatch + node count. Clicking a layer **isolates**
  it (bright layer, everything else dims). Layer colors are the single source of truth and
  **must stay in sync** across the CSS `--l*` tokens and the scene script's `LAYERS` map.
- **Views (lenses)** — cross-cutting perspectives that highlight a concept **across**
  layers, because a layer split is only one way to read the graph. Each lens (e.g. single
  tool gateway, hybrid retrieval, learning loop, exploration, feedback & cycles) lists a
  node set (or `feedback:true` to select every feedback edge); selecting it brightens those
  nodes/edges and dims the rest. Render lenses with a **ring** swatch so "views" read
  differently from the filled-square "layers".
- Layer and lens selection are **mutually exclusive**; picking one clears the other, and
  entering guided mode or reset clears both.


- **Nodes are faceted crystals** (`flatShading`) with a white wireframe overlay and an
  additive glow aura — never plain smooth spheres. Map role → geometry, e.g.:
  - hub/core → `IcosahedronGeometry(r, 1)` · gateway → `IcosahedronGeometry(r, 0)`
  - storage → `DodecahedronGeometry(r, 0)` · worker → `OctahedronGeometry(r, 0)`
  any zoom (constant apparent size, clamped). Subtle rounded chip behind the text only if
  needed for contrast.
- **Edges carry a continuous bright pulse** traveling in real flow direction along a
  curved spline — always animating, never gated by scroll/stage. Make the pulse flow
  **naturally off the end**: use a travel period of `1 + tail` so the head clamps at the
  endpoint while the tail keeps arriving (the segment slides in), then re-emerges from the
  start. Never let the whole segment vanish the instant its head arrives.
- **Backdrop = a multi-dimensional space, not a black void.** Layer several cheap cues:
  faint **static coordinate grids** (a floor + a back wall) for dimensionality; a hollow
  **vector field** (short line segments on a lattice, oriented by a smooth curl) that reads
  as a "vector/scalar world"; a two-tint **starfield**; and a **twinkle** layer — a
  `ShaderMaterial` giving each star its own phase so they sparkle randomly. Rotate the
  star/vector group very slowly; keep grids static. Exponential fog for depth; motion stays
  calm, no strobing.
- **Color = layer hue**, except where a per-node color encodes live status (e.g. a failed
  step red, a success green). Emphasis is by **dimming, never hiding**.
- **Represent feedback explicitly — never render an adaptive system as a pure DAG.**
  Give each feedback flow its own visual language: **dashed return arcs** that bow away
  from the forward flow, **tinted (non-white)** reverse pulses, and an **always-on label**
  naming the concept. The `kind` on an edge selects the treatment:
  - `loop` — intra-cycle retry (e.g. `retry loop ↺`); bows out, dashed.
  - `backprop` — value flowing back up a tree (e.g. `Q backprop`); solid-tinted.
  - `respawn` — an action that spawns a **new run** (e.g. delegate → sub-agent that
    re-retrieves); dashed, bows toward the entry point.
  - `auto` — the grand autonomous cycle (completion → self-prompt → top of pipeline);
    the biggest dashed sweep, so "the whole thing repeats" is unmistakable.
  - `writeback` — the **learning loop**: results recorded → organized → stored → recalled
    (e.g. evidence → memory → RAG index → next-run retrieval). This is frequently the most
    important and most-omitted flow; draw it.
  The node that closes each loop should say so in its description.


- Self-contained static bundle: **three.js r128 + OrbitControls** via CDN, no build step.
- Single `requestAnimationFrame` loop; `pixelRatio` capped at 2; raycast only node meshes.
- WebGL fallback message on context-creation failure.
- Fully responsive: on phones the description panel moves to the **top** and shrinks so it
  never overlaps the bottom-left filter; icons and the language select shrink too.
- Theme: a committed dark look is fine for a public showcase; paint backgrounds explicitly.
- **Language pack** in a separate `js/i18n.js` (English base, ~20 languages). Node/loop/
  layer/lens/caption/UI strings are localized; technical identifiers stay English. Changing
  language rebuilds billboard labels and re-renders the current panel/legend. Missing keys
  fall back to English per-string.


Because the 3D Architecture Explorer is publicly exposed on the web (e.g. GitHub Pages), raw shaders, 3D scene parameters, node topology data, and interactive UX logic are high-value targets for unauthorized cloning, scraping, and reverse-engineering. Shipping clean plain-text JavaScript is strictly forbidden.


1. **Layer 1: Physical Source Isolation (`web_explorer_src/` vs `public/`)**
   - Clean, readable, uncompiled source code resides exclusively in `web_explorer_src/js/` (`scene.js`, `i18n.js`).
   - The publicly served directory (`public/js/`) contains **zero plain JavaScript** — only compiled binary payloads.

2. **Layer 2: Non-Linear Bytecode Virtual Image Encryption (`scripts/pack_web_binary.cjs`)**
   - Source files are converted to raw UTF-8 byte streams and encrypted via multi-round non-linear transformations:
     - 12-byte dynamic key schedule (RC4 / XOR composite mask).
     - Dynamic polynomial index offset: `k = key[i] ^ ((i * 47 + 13) & 0xFF)`.
     - 3-bit circular bitwise rotation per byte: `((b << 3) | (b >>> 5)) & 0xFF`.
   - Formatted into static `Uint8Array` hex byte arrays (`_0xbin = new Uint8Array([0xad, 0xa1, ...])`), completely rendering standard JS AST deobfuscators, prettifiers, and beautifiers useless.

3. **Layer 3: Active Anti-Debugging & DevTools Interception Trap**
   - The compiled loader injects dynamic anti-debugging timing probes (`debugger` evaluation trap).
   - If an unauthorized actor opens Browser DevTools (F12), inspects the console, or pauses on breakpoints, the execution time delta exceeds the threshold (`Date.now() - t0 > 150ms`), triggering an **instant session reload (`window.location.reload()`)** to terminate analysis and block memory dumping.

4. **Layer 4: In-Memory Virtual Machine Execution & License Sealing**
   - Decryption occurs entirely in-memory at runtime through a lightweight synchronous VM decryptor into an isolated IIFE function scope (`new Function(_0xcode).call(_0xglobal)`), leaving no unencrypted `.js` files in browser caches or network tabs.
   - Every compiled output includes a sealed binary distribution license prohibiting unauthorized reverse-engineering.

- **Rule**: Never edit files in `public/js/` directly.
- **Workflow**: Make all edits in `web_explorer_src/js/`, then execute:
  ```bash
  node scripts/pack_web_binary.cjs
  ```
  This emits newly encrypted binary payloads into `public/js/` before git commit, push, or release.


Because the bundle is fully static, the simplest reliable host is GitHub Pages served from
the branch (no Actions build needed):

- **Source = Deploy from a branch** (`main`, `/root`) and add an empty **`.nojekyll`** at
  the repo root so files are served exactly as-is (no Jekyll pass that could drop assets).
- **GitHub Actions must be enabled on the repo.** GitHub's *managed* "pages build and
  deployment" itself runs as an Actions job, so if Actions is disabled every deploy silently
  stays `queued` and the site goes stale. Enable it (Settings → Actions → General → Allow),
- Prefer the managed branch build over a hand-written Actions deploy workflow: one less
  thing to fail, and it does not need `build_type: workflow`. If a custom deploy workflow
  and a branch source coexist, the workflow will fail against the branch source — remove it.
- Quick health check after a push: the live `index.html` should reference `js/i18n.js`, and
  `js/scene.js` should contain the latest markers.


- ❌ A scroll cinematic that shows only abstract shapes with **no descriptions**.
- ❌ **Free-explore-only** with no guidance — visitors won't click through everything.
- ❌ Hidden-until-approached nodes/labels; the graph is always fully rendered.
- ❌ Side/slide-in **inspector panels**, boxed cards, and 1px borders — use floating text.
- ❌ A title/identity **header** and a **controls-hint** legend of drag/scroll/click.
- ❌ **Emoji** as button labels — use inline SVG icons.
- ❌ "Ultra-minimal" 1–2-word HUD that conveys no information; overloaded metaphor jargon
  detached from real component names.
- ❌ A second, different presentation for loop/overview stops — keep one info style.
- ❌ Faking connectivity or omitting real feedback / write-back edges; freezing
  dynamically-assigned roles into fixed specialties.
- ❌ Pulses that vanish the instant they reach the endpoint (period must be `1 + tail`).
- ❌ A flat black background when a few cheap layers (grids, vector field, twinkle) make it
  read as a real space.


1. Copy `public/index.html`, `css/scene.css`, `js/scene.js`, `js/i18n.js` and `.nojekyll`
   into the new project's static dir.
2. Replace `LAYERS` (+ the CSS `--l1..--lN` tokens) with this project's layers/colors.
3. Replace `NODES`, `EDGES`, `TOUR_ORDER`, `LENSES` with the real architecture; set `pos`
   for a clean top→bottom layered layout.
4. Replace `scene.js` and `i18n.js` in `web_explorer_src/js/` (English base first); keep technical identifiers English.
5. Run `node scripts/pack_web_binary.cjs` to compile and emit protected binary runtimes into `public/js/`.
6. Update the intro/outro caption title to "`<Project> Architecture`" and `<title>`/meta.
7. Enable GitHub Actions + set Pages to the branch with `.nojekyll` (see §8).
8. Verify: whole graph visible on load · scroll runs the narrated tour · descriptions are
   floating & borderless · toggle icons work · legend isolates layers · no header / no
   controls-hint · binary protection active · no non-goal reintroduced.
