title: Footer UX, Autonomy Gap, and Refactoring Hardening Plan
text:
Date: 2026-07-17
Status: Implemented (behavior + UX + C1/C4); C2/C3 deferred (see below)
Baseline: `095df0b2` (`chore: bump pentesting package to 0.101.7`)
Branch: `feat/footer-ux-autonomy-hardening`
Related: `PLAN_AutoGoalPersistence_Minimal_2026-07-17.md` (Completed, commit `cbec9a18`)


Delivered and validated on branch `feat/footer-ux-autonomy-hardening`
(`b6d3073d` feature, `fc85a074` C1 refactor):

- **A1** context-overflow → one-shot auto-compaction recovery; second overflow
  after compaction falls back to waiting. Done.
- **A2** completion signal read from the just-finished turn's in-memory reply,
  fetch only as fallback. Done.
- **A3 + C4** `AutoErrorPolicy` (WaitForUser | Compact | Retry) with bounded
  exponential backoff, reset on any completed turn; no failure cap. Done.
- **A4** short natural-language stop recognition with negation guard. Done.
- **A5 + B1** footer autonomous-run indicator (badge, goal, `current/target`,
  stop affordance) wired from `UIState`. Done.
- **B2** `footer_text` refactored into padding/candidate/fit/assemble helpers;
  manual-mode output unchanged. Done.
- **B3** interrupt-hint copy clarified. **B4** clock formatter renamed. Done.
- **B5** signal-fallback footer confirmed to keep the model via the shared
  fit ladder. Verified.
- **C1** numeric-target cue vocabularies extracted into named const slices,
  behavior-identical. Done.

Validation (Docker wrappers): `check --all-targets` (workspace deps), `fmt
--check`, `clippy -p builder_main -p builder_ratatui --all-targets -D warnings`,
`test -p builder_ratatui status_row` (66), `test -p builder_main ui::tests`
(41) incl. the 30+ numeric-target cases, full `--lib` (builder_ratatui 229 +
builder_main), and `dverify refactor-stability` (all-target clippy, PTY smoke,
shell e2e, stability diff) — all green.

**Deferred to a standalone follow-up: C2** (group auto-signal parsing into an
`auto_signal` submodule) **and C3** (move the auto loop into `auto_loop.rs`).
Both are pure structural reorganizations with no behavior or UX change. They are
kept out of this branch deliberately so the ~1000-line file move does not bury
the reviewable behavior/UX diff; each can land and be validated on its own.

Note: an unrelated pre-existing `README.md` working-tree edit (a personal
"Insight" section) leaves `public/README.md` out of sync, which trips the
`npm_verify` consistency sub-gate. That edit is not part of this work and was
not committed here; the Rust stability gate was validated with it stashed.

## Purpose

Two threads are merged into a single plan:

1. **Footer / bottom-chrome UX**: the persistent footer feels ambiguous while
   using the TUI. Fix the concrete UX issues and the code plumbing behind them.
   completes" work (`cbec9a18`) is assessed here for soundness, and the gaps it
   left open are folded into this plan so autonomy and footer are hardened in one
   coherent pass.

This document is a plan only. No code, test, commit, release, or Docker action
is taken until the plan is approved.

---


The completed minimal plan is **sound in its core design**. Verified against the
current implementation:

- `decide_auto_continuation` (`crates/builder_main/src/ui/mod.rs:611`) correctly
  treats `AUTO_GOAL_BLOCKED` and sub-target progress as *continue*, not stop.
- The `auto_completion_armed` one-shot guard (`mod.rs:298`, `:1266`) prevents a
  stale completion marker from an earlier goal/activation from stopping a freshly
  armed loop.
- Numeric completion fails closed: missing, mismatched, or multiple numeric
  candidates keep running (`decide_auto_continuation` + `explicit_numeric_target`
  at `mod.rs:490`).
- Queue priority is enforced at three linearization points before completion or
  continuation mutates state (`mod.rs:1261`, `:1272`, `:1289`).
- Explicit stop paths (`/auto`, Esc, Ctrl-C, `/exit`, `/goal` change) invalidate

**Verdict:** the behavior contract from the prior plan holds. The gaps below are
*missed edges*, not defects in the shipped contract — they are exactly the
"혹시 놓친 것" the loop still trips over in a long real run.


`auto_error_requires_user` (`mod.rs:736`) classifies `context length exceeded`,
`context window exceeded`, `maximum context length`, `input token count exceeds`,
`prompt is too long`, and `413 payload too large` as **"wait for the user."** In
an autonomous loop this is the single most likely terminal condition: a
long-running goal *will* fill the context window, and when it does, the loop
parks at the prompt with no autonomous recovery. The user is told to "resolve the
context error" — but the natural remedy (compaction / summarize-and-continue) is
something the agent can do itself.

The prior plan listed compaction as a non-goal *for that minimal scope*. It is
in scope here. The fix does **not** require a new compaction subsystem — it
requires routing context-exhaustion errors to the **existing** compaction/summary
path instead of the user-wait path, then re-issuing the self-prompt once.


`current_auto_completion_signal` (`mod.rs:1335`) calls
`self.api.conversation(...)` on **every** idle auto-continue cycle just to parse
the completion marker out of the latest assistant reply. The loop already
produced that reply in the turn it just ran. This is an avoidable network
round-trip + latency on every autonomous heartbeat, and it couples completion
detection to conversation-fetch availability.

Fix: capture the just-finished turn's final assistant markdown from the turn
outcome and parse the signal from that in-memory value; fall back to the fetch
only when the in-memory reply is unavailable (e.g., after `/resume`).


On a non-user error, `wait_for_auto_retry(auto_retry_delay(&error))`
(`mod.rs:1148`) retries forever at a **fixed** delay (`AUTO_RETRY_DELAY`, or the
throttled delay only for 429/resource-exhausted). A persistent transient-looking
failure (e.g., a repeatable 500, a flapping tool) becomes a fixed-cadence hot
loop against the provider with no escalation. The prior plan's "no artificial
failure limit" intent is preserved — we are **not** adding a stop cap — but the
delay should escalate (bounded exponential backoff with a ceiling) when the same
error class repeats, and reset on any successful turn.


`is_explicit_auto_stop_message` (`mod.rs:713`) matches only whole-message exact
equality against a fixed list ("stop", "cancel", "중지", …). "please stop",
"stop the loop", "그만 좀 해줘" do not match. Because queued input wins, such a
message is still processed as a turn, but auto mode then **resumes** afterward —
the user's intent to stop is silently dropped. Widen recognition to a contained
match against the same vocabulary with light normalization, while keeping it
conservative enough not to false-positive on a message that merely mentions the
word.


The bottom chrome (`crates/builder_ratatui/src/backend.rs`,
`crates/builder_ratatui/src/status_row.rs`) has **zero** awareness of auto mode
or the active goal — confirmed: no `auto_mode` / `active_goal` reference exists
in `builder_ratatui`. During an autonomous run the footer shows the same static
`Esc keep queue · Ctrl+C clear queue/input` hint as manual mode. The user cannot
tell the agent is self-driving, what goal it is chasing, what cycle it is on, or
how to stop the loop specifically. This is both an autonomy-observability gap and
the footer UX complaint — resolved together in Part B.

---


### Findings

**B1 — Footer does not reflect autonomous state.** The footer hint is static
(`FOOTER_HINT_FULL` / `_COMPACT` / `_TINY`, `status_row.rs:36`). When `/auto` is
active the persistent footer should communicate: auto is on, the active goal
(truncated), optional `current/target` progress, and the stop affordance
(`/auto` or Esc). Today none of that surfaces — the footer's job of "tell me the
state and what my keys do" is unmet exactly when the agent is least
interactive.

**B2 — `footer_text` mixes four concerns in one 70-line function**
(`status_row.rs:143`): padding budget, candidate-hint fit, model truncation, and
gap/pad assembly are all inlined with nested branching. It is correct but hard to
extend (e.g., to add an auto segment) and hard to test in isolation. Extract:
`resolve_padding`, `select_hint`, `fit_model`, `assemble(hint, segments,
inner_width)`.

**B3 — Hint semantics are unclear at a glance.** `Esc keep queue · Ctrl+C clear
queue/input` compresses two different actions onto one line with "queue"
appearing twice. Re-word for scannability (e.g., `Esc keeps queue · Ctrl+C
clears`) and verify the compact/tiny fallbacks degrade gracefully; the tiny
variant `Esc / Ctrl+C` gives no verb at all.

**B4 — Two divergent duration formatters with near-identical names.**
`format_elapsed` (clock `M:SS`, `status_row.rs:303`) vs
`format_elapsed_for_status` (prose, `elapsed.rs:50`). The intentional difference
is documented, but the names invite mis-use. Rename to intent (`format_clock` vs
`format_prose_elapsed`) and colocate, or document the split at both sites.

**B5 — Signal-fallback footer drops the model.** When `interrupt_hint ==
SIGNAL_INTERRUPT_HINT`, only `Ctrl+C interrupt` is shown and the candidate list
is single-element (`status_row.rs:159`); the model still renders via the
`footer_model()` path, but the compaction ladder can't shorten the hint, so on a
narrow terminal the model is dropped entirely rather than truncated. Confirm this
is intended; if not, allow model truncation in the signal path too.


```
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 auto · goal: enumerate 40 subdomains  12/40   /auto to stop   model
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

- `auto` badge only when `state.auto_mode`.
- goal text truncated to a width budget (reuse `truncate_to_width`).
- stop affordance replaces the manual hint while auto is on.
- model stays right-aligned via the existing gap-fill.
- Manual mode is unchanged.

---


**C1 — `explicit_numeric_target` is a 120-line heuristic**
(`mod.rs:490`) with hardcoded English + Korean cue words, structured-identifier
sniffing, and scoped-target fallbacks. It is the most brittle surface in the auto
path. Refactor into named sub-steps (`scan_number_spans`,
`is_structured_identifier`, `classify_target`) with the cue vocabularies pulled
into named `const` slices, so each rule is independently testable and the Korean
cues (`목표:`, `최소:`, `총:`) sit beside their English peers.

**C2 — Auto-signal parsing spread across four free functions**
(`parse_auto_completion_signal`, `parse_grouped_u64`, `parse_auto_signal_payload`,
`normalized_auto_signal_reason`, `mod.rs:398–486`). Group them into a small
`auto_signal` submodule with a single documented entry point; keeps `mod.rs`
(currently very large) from accreting more top-level parsing helpers.

**C3 — `mod.rs` size.** After `cbec9a18` this file carries the entire auto loop,
signal parsing, target heuristics, retry policy, and REPL glue. Moving the auto
loop into `crates/builder_main/src/ui/auto_loop.rs` (state machine + pure
helpers + their tests) would isolate the most-changed logic and shrink the review
surface for future autonomy edits. Mechanical move, no behavior change.

**C4 — Retry/backoff policy is scattered.** `auto_error_requires_user`,
`auto_retry_delay`, and the retry branch in the REPL loop (`mod.rs:1136–1151`)
together *are* the autonomy error policy but live in three places. Consolidate
into one `AutoErrorPolicy::classify(&error) -> {WaitForUser | Compact | Retry(delay)}`
returning the escalated delay from A3, so the REPL loop reads as a single match.

---

## Sequencing

1. **A1 context-window recovery** — highest real-world impact on long runs.
2. **A2 in-memory signal read** — removes per-cycle fetch; unblocks cheaper heartbeat.
3. **A3 bounded backoff** + **C4 policy consolidation** — one change.
4. **B1/B5 footer auto-awareness** + **A5** — one change (footer surfaces auto/goal/progress/stop).
5. **B2/B3/B4 footer refactor + copy** — cleanup riding on B1.
6. **A4 inline stop recognition** — small, independent.
7. **C1/C2/C3 refactors** — pure structure, last, each behavior-preserving.

Each item is independently shippable; 1–3 are the autonomy correctness core, 4–5
are the UX deliverable, 6–7 are hygiene.


- No goal repository, evidence projection, service/API layer, scheduler, second
  runtime, UUID, lineage graph, or trusted-receipt system.
- No new compaction subsystem — A1 reuses the **existing** compaction/summary path.
- No cycle cap or consecutive-failure stop limit (A3 only escalates delay).
- No release-metadata changes during implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

Autonomy:
1. A context-window error during `/auto` triggers one automatic compaction and a
   re-issued self-prompt instead of parking at the prompt; if compaction cannot
   help, it then falls back to the user-wait path.
2. Idle auto-continue reads the completion signal without a conversation fetch
   when the just-finished reply is in memory; the fetch path still works after
   `/resume`.
3. A repeating non-user error escalates the retry delay up to a ceiling and
   resets to base after any successful turn; the loop never hard-stops on it.
4. "please stop" / "stop the loop" / "그만해 주세요" disable auto mode; a message
   that merely mentions "stop" in a sentence does not.
5. All eight prior acceptance behaviors still pass unchanged.

Footer:
6. With `/auto` on, the footer shows the auto badge, truncated goal, numeric
   `current/target` when known, and a stop affordance; manual-mode footer is
   byte-identical to today.
7. `footer_text` width invariants (symmetric padding, model truncation, compact
   ladder) hold at 79 / 39 / narrow widths after the refactor — existing footer
   tests pass with only the auto-segment additions.

Refactor:
8. `explicit_numeric_target`, auto-signal parsing, and retry policy behavior are
   byte-for-byte preserved by their extractions (guarded by the existing and new
   unit tests); no public API of `builder_main` changes.

## Validation

All Rust build/test/lint/format via the repository's memory-capped Docker
wrappers (`scripts/dbuild.ps1`), never host Cargo. Node checks via
`scripts/nverify.ps1` / `scripts/dverify.ps1`. Run focused `ui::tests` and
`builder_ratatui` status-row tests first, then the full sequential gates. No
commit, push, package release, or Docker publication until focused behavior and
full stability gates pass.

title: Deep Code Review — Improvement & Refactoring Plan (2026-07-18)
text:
Date: 2026-07-18
Status: **Complete** — P0, P1, P2, and P3 all landed and green on `main`. See "Execution status" below.
Baseline: `main` @ `854fd25b`
Scope: deep review of the autonomous loop / REPL, the TUI rendering pipeline, and
the interrupt / input / terminal-session code, plus workspace-wide tech-debt
signals. Three independent reviewers traced each finding to its references.

---


Every item below was validated in Docker (`fmt` + `clippy -p <crate> --all-targets
-- -D warnings` + the relevant `--lib` test suite) and committed to `main`
individually, so `main` is green at each step. `README.md` and `docs/linkedin/`
were intentionally left untouched (user-owned content).

### Done ✅
- [x] **P0.1** — reader-thread death no longer synthesizes a spurious interrupt (`SignalFallback` split; `wait()` fixed).
- [x] **P0.2 / P0.3** — `InputBuffer` lock-poisoning recovery via a single `lock()` helper used by every method.
- [x] **P0.4** — output backpressure double-decrement fixed (`already_dequeued` flag on the re-flush path).
- [x] **P0.5 / P0.6** — quota classification (`insufficient_quota` / `quota_exceeded` needles) + `pending_auto_completion` now peeks instead of `take()`.
- [x] **P1** — removed dead plumbing: `usage` field/param end-to-end, `queued_count`, dead status-row renderers, `spinner_char`.
- [x] **P2.1** — extracted the autonomous-loop surface into a dedicated `ui::auto_loop` submodule (`pub(super)` + `use auto_loop::*`); shrinks the 2800-line `ui/mod.rs`.
- [x] **P2.3** — replaced the hand-rolled Unicode width table with `unicode-width` (`unwrap_or(1)` preserves `\n` cursor width — `unwrap_or(0)` regressed 2 tests).
- [x] **P2.4** — `input_buffer::clear()` → `clear_all(None)` dedup; `on_dump` subtitle dedup (`dump_subtitle`).
- [x] **P3.2** — pure `plan_auto_continuation(...) -> AutoDispatchPlan` extracted; the auto-dispatch TOCTOU queue guard is now unit-tested (+5 tests).
- [x] **P3.1** — interrupt reader loop body lifted into testable `process_interrupt_event(...) -> ReaderStep` (+4 tests: Ctrl+C-clear / Esc-interrupt / paste / PageUp-scroll).
- [x] **P3.3** — replaced the 6-variant routing spot-check with an exhaustive `SlashCommand`→route table + an `EnumIter` completeness guard (a future variant not added to the table fails the test).
- [x] **D4** (follow-on) — dropped the unused `_interrupt_hint` param from `render_status_row_snapshot`.
- [x] (out-of-plan, earlier this session) fixed gray input/footer chrome; subtle primary-tint random spinner; removed hardcoded autonomy heuristics (stop-word matcher, numeric-target parser); English-only product code.

- [x] **P2.2** — decomposed the 210-line `redraw_bottom_area` closure in `backend.rs` into three behavior-preserving free functions (`draw_minimal_input_echo`, `repaint_transcript_on_resize`, `draw_bottom_chrome`) + a `BottomAreaLayout` struct grouping the eight row indices; the closure shrinks to ~100 lines of orchestration. Validated with `builder_ratatui --lib` (234 tests green). The two long-lived `Cell` locals were **deliberately left as actor locals** (not promoted into an `OutputActorState`): that grouping touches ~10 call sites for marginal gain and is better as its own change.

### Remaining ⬜
- None. All plan items are landed on `main`.

### Verification note
Full `nverify` / `dverify` end-to-end runs are currently gated by a pre-existing
`public/README.md out of sync with README.md` error, which stems from an
uncommitted local `README.md` edit (user-owned WIP, intentionally untouched) — a
generated docs mirror with **zero functional impact**. All code gates pass: the
whole-workspace build, `clippy -D warnings`, every plumbing consistency check,
`builder_main --lib` (922 tests), the `shell_session_e2e` + `pty_smoke` integration
binaries, and `builder_ratatui --lib` (234 tests) are all green.

See the per-item detail in the sections below.


Items are grouped by priority. **P0** = latent correctness bugs (fail silently
in production). **P1** = dead/unnecessary plumbing to remove (the LLM/product
does not need it). **P2** = decomposition/refactor of oversized modules. **P3**
= testability. Each item lists file:line and a concrete fix. Nothing here is
implemented yet.

---


`interrupt.rs:462` (`Err(_) => SignalFallback`) + the error `break` at
`interrupt.rs:531-538`. Any `event::poll`/`event::read` error drops the unsent
one-shot; `wait()` maps the closed channel to `SignalFallback`, which the caller
treats as a real user interrupt and cancels the running turn. A transient
crossterm error (plausible on Windows) therefore kills a turn.
**Fix:** distinguish "reader exited without a decision" from "user interrupted" —
send an explicit sentinel on clean/error exit, or make `wait()` return `Option`
so a dropped sender does not synthesize an interrupt. Pre-existing; not caused by
the recent Ctrl+C/Esc split, but adjacent to it.

`input_buffer.rs` — every method uses `if let Ok(..) = self.inner.lock()` /
`.ok()?` (lines 107,127,155,182,195,212,232,257,282,306,319). After any panic
under the lock, all `push_event`/`clear`/`pop` become silent no-ops and
`is_empty()` returns `true`. This also makes `RawInputGuard::drop`
(`interrupt.rs:364-374`) disable raw mode during the canonical-mode gap it warns
against (P0.3). Inconsistent with `interrupt.rs`/`terminal_session.rs`, which use
`unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())`.
**Fix:** adopt `unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())` everywhere in
`InputBuffer` so state stays usable after an unrelated panic.

`interrupt.rs:364-374` calls `buf.is_empty()`, which returns `true` on poison
(P0.2). A poisoned buffer still holding queued items reports empty, so raw mode
is disabled mid-turn. Resolved by fixing P0.2.

`backend.rs`: `mark_enqueued` runs once per write (`enqueue_admitted_command`,
:936), but every write arm in `flush_output_batch` calls `mark_dequeued`
*before* the defer check then `continue`s to re-queue the command
(:3234-3243, :3266-3273, :3280-3305, :3318-3326). When
`mark_dequeued`s the same bytes again. `pending_bytes` under-counts, so
`is_backpressured` (:1675-1682) under-reports and producers under-throttle under
sustained prompt-active output → latent unbounded queue growth.
**Fix:** move each `mark_dequeued` to *after* the defer check — count deferred
bytes as still-queued until they are actually written.

`ui/mod.rs:623-682`. `AUTO_USER_BOUNDARY_NEEDLES` matches `"insufficient quota"`
and `"quota exceeded"` (prose), but a provider that returns only a machine code
(`insufficient_quota`) with no prose falls through to `AutoErrorPolicy::Retry`
and retries forever. Also substring matching of `"forbidden"`/`"unauthorized"`
against the whole error chain could misclassify a transient error whose body
incidentally contains those tokens (errs safe — parks vs spins).
**Fix:** add underscore/code variants (normalize `_`→space before matching), and
prefer matching the downcast `builder_domain::Error` before string needles.

`ui/mod.rs:1188-1219` + `:1263`. `current_auto_completion_signal` does
`pending_auto_completion.take()` at :1263, but `try_auto_continue_command` can
still bail at the post-read (:1200) or commit (:1213) queue guard after the
in-memory reply was taken. Low impact (next cycle re-fetches), but it mutates
state on a path that drops the value.
**Fix:** peek instead of `take()`, or only `take()` once dispatch is guaranteed.

---


Traced full chain: `ui_turn.rs:87` → `turn_runtime.rs:95-101` →
`status_row_runtime.rs:52,74` → `turn/status_row.rs:47` →
`status_row_renderer.rs:15,49-63,104` (humanize) →
`render_backend.rs:19-25` (trait `show_status_row` `usage` param) →
`backend.rs:332,371` (`state.usage`). It dead-ends — no widget renderer reads
`usage` (the footer comment `status_row.rs:240-242` says token numbers were
removed as inaccurate). Worse, each `UsageUpdate` flips the humanized bucket →
`redraw_required` → a full bottom-area repaint producing byte-identical output.
`only_usage_changed` (`backend.rs:364-375`) exists solely to babysit this dead
value.
**Fix:** delete the `usage` param/field chain across the 8 sites above (trait
signature + mock impls in `render_coordinator.rs:155`, `status_row_renderer`
mock :161, and `builder_main` `terminal_session`/`ui_turn`/`turn_runtime`), drop
`humanize_number`, and delete `only_usage_changed` — with `usage` gone a usage
update no longer changes `render`, so the stall clock is naturally preserved.
`builder_domain::Usage` stays (used by context/html).

`terminal_session.rs:370` → `backend.rs:621-633` stores `state.queued_count`;
nothing renders it. The live queued indicator is a separate path —
`queued_prompt_prefix` renders `❯ (+N)` into the input row
(`terminal_session.rs:374,414-419`).
**Fix:** remove the field (`status_row.rs:134`, default :159), `set_queued_count`
(`backend.rs:620-633` + trait default `render_backend.rs:64` + mock impls), and
the caller at `terminal_session.rs:370`.

- `spinner_char` (`status_row.rs:185`): **zero callers, incl. tests** — remove.
- `format_status_row_frame` (`status_row.rs:~487`, `pub`, exported at
  `lib.rs:28`): zero production callers workspace-wide — remove fn + export + its
  ~5 tests.
- `render_processing_line` / `render_hint_line`: only test callers (production
  uses the `_widget_line` variants) — remove or demote to `#[cfg(test)]`.

- `status_row_renderer.rs:35-38`: `render_status_row_snapshot` never uses
  `_interrupt_hint`; drop the param (keep the runtime field that drives
  `hint_changed`).
- `interrupt.rs:248-273`: `RuntimeInterruptListener::new()` / `with_buffer()` —
  no production callers, carry `#[allow(dead_code)]`; remove or `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `interrupt.rs:336-378`: `RawInputGuard::enabled_by_us` is always `true`; drop
  the field and the dead `if` branch.
- `interrupt.rs:93`: stale `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `TurnOutcome` (it is widely
  used) — drop the attribute.
- `input_buffer.rs:202-205`: `queued_count()` only used by one test — gate
  `#[cfg(test)]`.

---


Largest source files (LOC): `builder_ratatui/backend.rs` **6700**,
`builder_main/ui/mod.rs` **2842**, `builder_main/turn_runtime.rs` 2645,
`builder_app/operation.rs` 3288, `builder_domain/tools/catalog.rs` 3151.

`ui/mod.rs` mixes the auto-loop (constants/types/pure logic 43-730, methods
1163-1447), the REPL `run` loop, MCP formatting, conversation CRUD, `on_dump`,
and zsh rprompt. **Fix:** move the pure auto surface (constants, `AutoCompletionSignal`/
`AutoContinuationDecision`/`AutoGoalProgress`/`AutoErrorPolicy`, all `parse_*`/
`decide_*`/`classify_*`/`escalated_*`/`auto_error_*`, and the state helpers
`arm`/`invalidate`/`reset_auto_run_state`/`set_active_goal`/`set_auto_mode`) into
`ui/auto_loop.rs` carrying their ~30 tests; move the auto `impl UI` methods into a
second `impl` block in `ui/auto_loop_run.rs`. Cuts mod.rs by ~600 lines and
isolates the most-changed logic.

`backend.rs:2520-2728`, invoked 6+ times. Extract `draw_minimal_input_echo`,
`repaint_transcript_on_resize`, and `draw_bottom_chrome`; promote the actor's
long-lived `Cell` locals (`last_terminal_size`, `transcript_scroll_offset`) into a
small `OutputActorState` struct so call sites take `&mut self` instead of a
10-tuple. Removes the `too_many_arguments` pressure.

`input_buffer.rs:557-633`. `char_width` maintains a partial width table by hand
while `unicode-width = "0.2"` is already a dependency (Cargo.toml:43). It omits
CJK ext-B, emoji, and combining supplements, so cursor-column preview drifts.
**Fix:** use `unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar::width(c).unwrap_or(0)` (keep tab
and control handling). Deletes ~75 lines.

- `input_buffer.rs`: `clear_all` (:178-192) and `clear` (:318-326) are
  near-duplicates — make `clear()` call `clear_all(None)`; extract `touch`
  (revision+timestamp) and `resync_events` helpers used by the four queue
  mutators.
- `ui/mod.rs:588` `command_manages_interrupt_internally` and
  `turn_execution.rs:793` `queued_command_starts_chat_turn` match the identical
  `Message|Custom|Retry` set — collapse to one predicate.
- `ui/mod.rs:1355-1368` `record_turn_outcome_for_auto` disables auto two ways
  (`set_auto_mode` vs hand-written); unify (document the consistency-gate need
  once).
- `ui/mod.rs:1851-1927` `on_dump` duplicates html/json subtitle/path logic —
  compute subtitle once.

---


`interrupt.rs:504-613` hardcodes `CrosstermEventSource`, so decision dispatch,
buffer-clear, paste, palette, and scroll paths are untestable. Extract the loop
*body* into a function over `&dyn TerminalEventSource` + buffer/catalog/callbacks
so a `FixtureEventSource` stream can drive Ctrl+C-clear, Esc-interrupt, paste, and
scroll deterministically; only the `thread::spawn` wrapper stays untested.

`ui/mod.rs:1163-1250` `try_auto_continue_command` holds the three-snapshot queue
guard + `pending.take()` + arm/dispatch ordering inside an `async` method no test
exercises. Extract `fn plan_auto_continuation(...) -> AutoDispatchPlan
{ Dispatch | Yield | Stop(signal) | ContinueAfterClaim(kind) }`; the method then
only does I/O and applies the plan. Makes the TOCTOU guard unit-testable.

`command_helpers.rs:25` + the four handlers ending in `unreachable!`. A
mis-assignment in `slash_command_route` only fails at runtime; the existing test
spot-checks 6 variants. Add a test iterating every `SlashCommand` variant
asserting it routes to the handler that actually covers it.

---


- Auto-loop state hygiene: every goal/auto/session/`/new` path funnels through
  `set_active_goal`/`set_auto_mode`/`reset_auto_run_state`; leak-tested.
- Queue/interrupt/auto linearization: biased `select!`, `QueueSuperseded` vs
  `next_repl_command` — correct and well-commented.
- Bounded exponential backoff (overflow-safe, ceiling-clamped) and the
  compaction one-shot guard.
- Backend shutdown lifecycle/fallback machine, enqueue-rollback paths,
  barrier-after-work ordering, single-actor FIFO, ANSI/scrollback wrapping, and
  the tiny-terminal fallback.
- Interrupt pause-coordinator nested-pause accounting and the `sender`-as-`Option`
  keep-alive after a buffer-clearing Ctrl+C.

## Suggested sequencing

1. P0.2/P0.3 (lock poisoning) and P0.1 (reader-death cancel) — smallest, highest
   safety payoff.
2. P0.4 (backpressure) — contained, correctness.
3. P1.1–P1.4 (dead plumbing removal) — one PR per item; P1.1 also deletes
   `only_usage_changed`.
5. P2.1 (auto_loop split) then P3.2 (pure linearization) — structural.
6. P2.2 (redraw_bottom_area) and P3.1 (reader testability) — larger refactors.


Docker wrappers only: `fmt --check`, `clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -D
warnings`, focused `test -p <crate> <filter>`, then full `--lib` for touched
crates, and `dverify refactor-stability` for anything touching the output actor
or interrupt reader.


A separate report during this session — `hi` producing repeated
`Retrying … POST https://api.minimax.io/...` then an Esc interrupt — is a network
connection failure reaching the provider (the retry cause is just the URL, the
signature of a reqwest connection error), not an app-plumbing bug. None of the
recent commits touch the HTTP/provider/retry path (verified via
`git diff --name-only`), and the Esc interrupt behaved correctly. Diagnose at the
Docker network / provider-config layer (reachability + endpoint/key), not in this
codebase.

title: Flow Wiring Cleanup — Post-Review Loose Ends (2026-07-19)
text:
Date: 2026-07-19
Status: **In progress**
Baseline: `main` @ `21d1ce68`
Scope: eliminate every wiring loose end surfaced by the 2026-07-19 final full
inspection of the deep-review series (`dde9d650~1..HEAD`). Four independent
reviewers confirmed the series is behavior-preserving with **zero defects**; the
items below are the residual wiring/consistency observations they flagged. Goal:
every flow's plumbing is symmetric, carries no vestigial parameters, and every
completeness guard is airtight.

+ the owning crate's `--lib` tests; full `dbuild test` at the end. (`nverify` /
`dverify` remain gated by the pre-existing user-owned `README.md` WIP — see the
2026-07-18 plan's verification note; functional gates are run directly.)

---

## Items

`crates/builder_ratatui/src/status_row.rs:494` — `format_status_row_frame` still
left behind by the P1.1/P1.2 plumbing removal. They are `#[cfg(test)]`-only dead
weight: every caller now feeds `None` / `0` / a hint literal.
- [x] Drop the three params; update the five test call sites.
- [x] Re-title/retarget `test_format_status_row_frame_omits_usage_and_queue_badge`
      so it asserts the *current* copy contract instead of removed params.

`crates/builder_ratatui/src/backend.rs:2469` — `draw_minimal_input_echo` writes
to the printer itself, while its two siblings (`repaint_transcript_on_resize`,
the single `write_bytes`. The asymmetry was inherited faithfully from the old
closure; unify it.
- [x] Change `draw_minimal_input_echo` to append to `out: &mut Vec<u8>` and
      return `Option<u16>` (the drawn row); the caller writes the buffer and
      records `previous_bottom_top_row`. Emitted byte sequence must be
      identical (same bytes, same single write, no write when nothing drawn).

`crates/builder_main/src/ui/command_helpers.rs:141` — the `EnumIter` count guard
catches a *missing* table row but a duplicate row could mask one (36 rows with a
dup + an omission still passes the length check).
- [x] Assert uniqueness via `std::mem::discriminant` collected into a set and
      compared against `SlashCommand::iter().count()`, alongside the length
      check.

`crates/builder_main/src/ui/auto_loop.rs:388` — `plan_auto_continuation`
currently receives the commit-point queue snapshot sampled *before* the (pure)
continuation decision; pre-refactor code sampled it *after*. Harmless today, but
the guard's contract should not depend on "the decision is fast/pure" reasoning.
- [x] Take the commit sample lazily: `commit_sample: impl FnOnce() -> (u64,
      bool)` invoked after `decide_auto_continuation`, restoring the original
      observation window while keeping the planner pure and unit-testable.
- [x] Update the call site in `ui/mod.rs` (`try_auto_continue_command`) and the

## Non-goals
- Underscore-prefixed params on trait impls and test mocks across the workspace
  (`_run_id`, `_writer`, …) — required by trait signatures, not vestigial wiring.
- Promoting the output actor's `Cell` locals into a state struct — explicitly
  deferred by the 2026-07-18 plan (P2.2 note).
- `README.md` / `public/README.md` sync — user-owned WIP.

## Execution status
- [x] W1 — landed
- [x] W2 — landed
- [x] W3 — landed
- [x] W4 — landed
- [x] Final gate: full `dbuild test` green

title: Active-Turn Input Transcript Plumbing Review (2026-07-21)
text:
> 상태: 완료; 제한형 전체 빌드·테스트·Clippy·스키마·Node·PTY 안정성 게이트 통과
> 범위: 활성 턴 입력의 키 이벤트부터 큐, interrupt, 재생, transcript scrollback까지

## 증상과 원인

일반 프롬프트 입력은 `Console::prompt`가 실행 직전에 `❯ <input>` 줄을 transcript에 남긴다. 반면 모델 응답이 진행 중일 때 받은 입력은 interrupt reader가 `InputBuffer`에 넣고 하단 고정 입력 행에만 잠시 표시했다. Esc는 이 큐를 정상 보존하고 다음 턴으로 재생했지만, 이 경로는 `Console::prompt`를 지나지 않으므로 사용자가 입력한 내용만 transcript에서 사라졌다.

즉 실행/큐잉 오류가 아니라, 활성 턴 입력 생산자와 transcript 소비자 사이의 누락된 UI 배선이었다.


1. 활성 턴에서 Enter로 확정한 비어 있지 않은 입력은 일반 프롬프트와 같은 `❯ <input>` 형식으로 transcript에 남는다.
2. 입력 확정 이벤트는 한 번만 생성한다. 큐 acknowledgement, Esc 재생, editor fallback은 이를 반복하지 않는다.
3. 모델이 부분 줄을 스트리밍 중이면 그 줄을 지우거나 끊지 않고, 출력 액터가 안전한 줄 경계에 도달할 때까지 입력 줄을 보류한다.
4. Esc는 큐와 transcript 기록을 보존하고 FIFO 재생한다. Ctrl+C의 기존 draft/queue 삭제 의미는 바꾸지 않는다.
5. 긴 입력, 여러 줄 입력, 제어문자 처리는 일반 프롬프트와 동일한 sanitizer/truncation 함수를 사용한다. 탭은 한 칸으로 가시화하고 나머지 Unicode 제어문자는 제거해 transcript 커서와 레이아웃을 바꿀 수 없다.

## 플럼빙 전수조사

| 경계 | 코드 경로 | 확인 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| 키 입력 생산 | `interrupt::process_interrupt_event` | active-turn 키를 단일 interrupt reader가 처리한다. Esc는 interrupt로 선형화되고, Enter/CR/Ctrl+J/Ctrl+M은 semantic buffer로 전달된다. |
| 입력 확정 | `InputBuffer::push_event_internal` | 큐 길이가 증가한 바로 그 revision에만 `submitted_input` edge를 붙인다. 빈 Enter, palette 선택 Enter, 이후 snapshot에는 edge가 없다. |
| 하단 입력 UI | `TerminalSession::render_buffer_snapshot` | revision 순서를 지키며 draft와 `(+N)` 큐 개수를 계속 표시한다. transcript 기록과 고정 입력 행 갱신은 별도 책임이다. |
| transcript 전달 | `TerminalSession::render_input_update` | edge가 있으면 공통 `render_prompt_submission_echo`를 호출하고, 출력 액터의 idle-safe 경로에 정확히 한 번 전달한다. |
| 출력 안전성 | `StatusRowBackend::write_output_line_when_idle` → `RatatuiBackend` output actor | prompt/status 소유 중이거나 raw output이 부분 줄이면 보류한다. 안전해지면 scrollback에 committed line으로 추가하고 하단 UI를 다시 그린다. |
| 명시적 중단 | `TerminalSession::handle_explicit_interrupt` | Esc와 queue supersede는 큐를 보존한다. Ctrl+C/signal fallback의 기존 clear 동작은 유지한다. |
| FIFO 소비 | `replay_queued_inputs_after_turn` | acknowledgement 후 정규화·파싱·실행한다. 입력 edge는 acknowledgement snapshot에서 다시 생성되지 않는다. |
| 즉시 명령 | `take_next_immediate_queued_command` | 동일 큐 항목을 꺼내 기존 interrupt/resource 경계를 거쳐 실행한다. 실패나 interrupt로 복원돼도 transcript edge는 반복되지 않는다. |
| prompt 경합 fallback | `EditorPromptSession::prefill_from_replayed_input` | 턴 종료 직후 들어온 큐가 editor로 넘어가도 `ReadResult::Replayed`로 구분해 일반 prompt echo를 두 번 쓰지 않는다. |
| modal 격리 | `TerminalSession::begin_modal_prompt` replay hooks | selector/modal이 기존 FIFO tail을 훔치지 않으며, 복원 snapshot도 새 submission edge를 만들지 않는다. |
| transcript 재표시 | output actor `recent_lines` | committed 입력 줄은 PageUp/PageDown 및 하단 영역 redraw의 기존 scrollback 원천에 포함된다. |

Bracketed paste의 개행은 Shift-modified multiline 문자로 재인코딩되므로 중간 개행이 여러 개의 제출 edge로 오인되지 않는 것도 확인했다.


- 활성 턴 callback에서 일반 `write_output_line`을 바로 호출하면 아직 끝나지 않은 Markdown/raw 줄을 clear하고 입력 줄로 덮을 수 있었다. 전용 idle-safe 계약을 통해 부분 줄이 끝날 때까지 보류하도록 했다.
- 턴 종료와 prompt ownership 전환이 경합하면 이미 보인 큐 입력이 editor replay를 거쳐 일반 prompt echo로 한 번 더 출력될 수 있었다. `ReadResult::Replayed`를 명시해 tracking/history는 유지하되 두 번째 UI echo만 생략했다.
- 실제 PTY의 원시 바이트에는 scrollback redraw 때문에 같은 committed 줄이 여러 번 전송될 수 있다. 논리적 1회 생성은 buffer/callback 단위 테스트로, 실제 화면 존재와 응답 전 순서는 PTY 테스트로 각각 검증한다.


- transcript echo는 실행 권한이나 요청 payload가 아니며, 기존 큐 항목의 실행 순서와 내용에 영향을 주지 않는다.

## 검증 기록

다음 게이트를 저장소 계약에 따라 순차 실행했으며 모두 통과했다.

- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 fmt --all -- --check`
- 입력 buffer/interrupt/terminal-session 단위 테스트와 tool snapshot 테스트
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_main --test pty_smoke -- --nocapture`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 build --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_config --test schema -- --nocapture`
- `scripts/nverify.ps1` (68개 중 65개 통과, 플랫폼 조건 3개 skip)
- `scripts/dverify.ps1 refactor-stability`
- 메인 저장소와 public submodule의 `git diff --check`

`npm run check`는 Docker image를 빌드하고 대화형 TUI를 시작하는 명령 계약이므로
비대화형 릴리스 게이트로 실행하지 않았다. Cargo 검증은 모두 메모리/CPU 제한이
적용된 Docker wrapper 안에서만 실행했다.

title: Agent PTY and Terminal-Control Plumbing Audit (2026-07-21)
text:
> Status: complete; all capped pre-release validation gates passed
> Scope: model tool contract through local PTY/pipe processes, incoming listeners,
> incremental observation, mutation, evidence, lifecycle, and cleanup

## Executive verdict

The primary Builder agent can operate long-running terminals without leaving the
registered tool boundary. It has both the high-level `process` interface and the
full 26-operation `session_control` interface. The operator and the CTF agents
that need direct terminal control also receive both tools; coordinator,
investigator, and verifier receive the safer high-level process interface.

The audit found no remaining critical or high-severity break in the terminal
control path after the fixes below. Local processes, concurrent incoming
callbacks, incremental observation, line/raw input, secret-reference injection,
literal and regex waits, terminal resize/signals, adaptive PTY upgrade, evidence
replay, and deterministic cleanup are all connected end to end. “Free control”
here means flexible control inside explicit authorization, resource, protocol,
and platform boundaries; it does not mean an unbounded or unaudited byte tunnel.


```mermaid
flowchart LR
    model["Agent tool call"] --> schema["Registered schema\n+ agent tool profile"]
    schema --> gate["Shared hook / policy /\nresource / audit gates"]
    gate --> exec["Tool executor\nprocess or session_control"]
    exec --> service["Session-control service\ndefault-spawn autostart"]
    service --> socket["Versioned JSONL Unix socket\nrequest id + size/deadline caps"]
    socket --> registry["Listener registry\nselectors + per-session lease"]
    registry --> actor["TCP / local PTY / local pipe\nsession actor"]
    actor --> evidence["Display + raw log + transcript\nledger + replay + lifecycle"]
```

Every built-in call, including `process` and `session_control`, traverses the
same registered-contract validation and outer hook/policy/resource/audit path.
The service then converts the typed request into protocol v1 JSONL and validates
the correlating response before returning model-visible JSON.

## Capability coverage

| Capability | Producer-to-consumer result |
|---|---|
| Discovery and authorization | `process` is a normal registered tool; the lower-level `session_control` remains cataloged and tool-search discoverable when deferred. Mutating operations produce structured policy operations and audit records. |
| Local terminals | `spawn` creates a PTY by default or an explicit stdin/stdout/stderr pipe. The first default-socket spawn safely auto-starts the local no-TUI listener; read-only calls and custom sockets do not silently create processes. |
| Incoming listeners | A managed nested `pentesting shell-listener` can bind one chosen port plus up to 31 additional unique ports, publish its successfully bound endpoints, accept independent sessions, and expose a dedicated workspace-relative control socket. Loopback is the default; non-loopback requires `--allow-remote`. |
| Multi-session selection | Numeric id, active/latest/open selectors, tagging, attach/detach, session info/listing, and per-session command ids preserve identity across handoff and delegation. Independent session actors continue concurrently. Adaptive upgrade takes an exclusive same-session pending-operation lease; ordinary blocking operations rely on the model boundary's sequential admission and must remain sequential per fragile session. |
| Incremental observation | `observe` and `attach` return a committed-line cursor. An unterminated prompt returns `output_partial=true` without advancing it, so consumers replace the mutable line rather than skip or duplicate it. Tail, transcript, history, and replay provide bounded retrospective views. |
| Waiting and command completion | Low-level `expect` performs a listener-side, cross-read, sticky match for one future literal. `run` uses framed sentinels and a bounded deadline. High-level `process expect` supports up to 32 literal/regex alternatives by polling a bounded current tail, detects process exit/control failure, and caps timeout and pattern size. |
| Input | `send` adds exactly one newline and rejects an existing trailing CR/LF. `raw` adds no newline and preserves exact UTF-8 text/control characters. `send_secret` consumes a policy-gated secret reference only after successful injection. |
| Terminal operations | Local PTY resize uses terminal ioctl; verified remote PTY resize synchronizes `stty`. Local PTY/pipe sessions accept the documented `int`, `term`, `hup`, and `kill` signals. Close and revoke have explicit lifecycle/audit reasons. |
| PTY upgrade | Explicit `upgrade technique=auto` performs bounded framed reconnaissance, allowlisted shell/helper selection, ACT→VERIFY retry, and probe-backed PTY state. Concrete helper and custom-text paths remain available without a silent default. |
| Evidence and recovery | Raw logs, sanitized transcripts, command ledgers, history, command-scoped replay, snapshots, PTY state, exit status, FD statistics, lifecycle state, archive, GC, and revoke are all addressable through the same session id. |
| Resource control | Requests/responses, timeout, expect pattern/count, retained line length/count, per-session raw logs, active FDs, listener ports, closed sessions, and archived sessions have explicit caps. |


| Agent profile | `process` | `session_control` | Intended terminal level |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| builder | yes | yes | Full primary-agent control |
| operator, pwn, recon, rev, web, crypto, forensics | yes | yes | Full execution/specialist control |
| coordinator, investigator, verifier | yes | no | Structured process control without the low-level listener surface |
| planner, researcher, reviewer, report-writer | no | no | Non-execution role boundary |

This is an intentional least-privilege split, not a missing plumbing path. A
role that owns terminal execution has a direct tool; planning/reporting roles do
not silently acquire one.


1. Default local PTY auto-start existed only in one shell-service adapter, so a
   first model `process spawn` or low-level `session_control spawn` could fail.
   Auto-start now lives in the shared session-control service and applies only
   to a default-socket spawn. Its exact executable allowlist covers the Cargo
   binary, npm's managed `vendor/builder` filename, and the direct release asset;
   the consistency graph derives the distributed filenames from
   `lib/runtime.mjs` so packaging cannot silently break first-spawn startup. A
   dedicated reaper also owns the spawned child so failed listeners cannot
   accumulate zombies while the parent remains alive.
2. Listener readiness accepted an uncorrelated `ok` JSON and could block on a
   silent socket. It now uses read/write deadlines, the response-size cap, and
   the normal version/request-id decoder.
3. Agent instructions described `send_line` as text plus a newline even though
   `send` already appended one. The listener now rejects trailing CR/LF and the
   schema/docs state the exactly-one-newline contract.
4. `process send_input` accepted `echo_policy=masked` even though plaintext was
   already present in model-visible arguments. It now accepts only truthful
   visible input; masked/hidden values must use a `secret_ref`.
5. Low-level `expect` matched only within one reader event. It now keeps a
   bounded cross-event window, remembers a match before tail trimming, rejects
   empty/oversized patterns, cannot lose a maximum-size match followed by bytes
   in the same read, and retains the matched line in the completed response
   instead of filtering it as though it were a command sentinel.
6. High-level `process expect` could wait up to two hours, accumulate output
   continue after process exit. It now refreshes a 64 KiB tail, accepts at most
   32 bounded patterns and five minutes, and stops on control failure or exit.
7. Display cursors advanced past an unterminated prompt, so `Pass` followed by
   `word:` at the same logical line could be skipped. Cursors now advance only
   over committed lines and expose mutable-tail state explicitly. Blocking
   operations also retain and subtract only the exact pre-existing partial
   prefix, preserving both no-echo results appended to a prompt and carriage-
   return replacements.
8. The local PTY backend appended repeated mutable snapshots, producing
   `PassPassword:`. It now replaces the partial suffix and commits it once.
9. A no-newline peer could grow one in-memory display line without a bound.
   Both stored complete lines and the mutable tail are now capped at 16 KiB
   while preserving a valid UTF-8 suffix.
10. Inserting a listener status line while remote output was partial allowed a
    later chunk to overwrite the status row. Registry lines now finalize the
    old mutable display line before insertion.
11. An explicitly empty or fully telemetry-filtered environment could fall
    through to full listener-environment inheritance. Explicit selection now
    remains explicit, including an empty environment.
12. Tool prose claimed arbitrary raw bytes although the JSON/Rust string path is
    UTF-8. The contract now accurately distinguishes exact UTF-8 text from an
    arbitrary-binary transport and documents the managed chosen-port workflow.
13. Listener auto-start handed the child to its reaper before readiness was
    known, which made a never-ready child impossible to terminate through its
    owned handle. Readiness is now established first; failure kills and waits
    the child, success transfers it to the reaper, and reaper-thread creation
    failure also kills and waits it.
14. The real shell-session fixture inferred blocked helper framing from whether
    a sentinel happened to share one TCP `read()`. It now models shell line
    order, with a deterministic segmented-read regression, so packet coalescing
    cannot make PTY verification flaky.
15. Normal `run`/`probe` sentinel detection itself was reader-event-local, so a
    framing token split by the kernel across two reads could leave complete
    probe output buffered until timeout. The session actor now owns a bounded
    streaming detector that retains only one possible token suffix and reports
    a cross-read sentinel exactly once.


- Custom control sockets are canonicalized, must exist inside the current
  workspace, and must be Unix sockets. The default socket is the only auto-start
  target.
  encoded request at 1 MiB and response at 4 MiB, and bounds connect/read waits.
- Callback listeners bind loopback unless both a non-loopback address and the
  explicit authorization flag are supplied. Successfully bound endpoints are
- Secrets travel as one-shot references through a sensitive control request.
  Redaction applies before new display/log/transcript records, but is correctly
  documented as non-retroactive.
- The listener reserves FD headroom, caps active sessions from the measured FD
  budget, caps raw logs at 64 MiB per session, retains at most 500 display lines
  of 16 KiB each, and bounds closed/archive retention.
- Timeout, disconnect, lifecycle cancellation, writer failure, and adaptive
  upgrade failure have distinct terminal paths; no blind retry follows an
  ambiguous write.


- The local PTY and control socket implementation is Unix-only. Native Windows
  uses the repository's supported Docker/Git-Bash flow; the published
  application image remains Linux AMD64 only.
- `raw` is exact UTF-8 text without an added newline, not arbitrary binary. For
  NUL-rich/binary protocols, spawn a program such as Python/pwntools in a managed
  session or exchange a workspace file; do not force bytes through JSON text.
- Low-level `session_control expect` is the lossless future-output primitive for
  one literal. High-level `process expect` intentionally polls a bounded current
  tail for buffered/multiple/regex matching and can miss data that completely
  rolls out between polls.
- Supported signals are the four documented common signals, not an arbitrary
  platform signal number.
- A custom/chosen-port listener is explicit: start it as a managed process,
  wait for its listening evidence, and then use its dedicated socket. Read-only
  probing never creates a listener behind the agent's back.
- Top-level model tool calls are admitted sequentially through the orchestration
  boundary, while long-lived session actors and listeners run concurrently.
  The adaptive controller rejects overlapping same-session pending work. Direct
  custom-socket clients are outside model admission and must not overlap
  ordinary blocking mutations on one fragile session.


- The public website no longer contains the architecture section, anchor, or
  its now-unused capability-grid styling. Its public README contains no
  architecture-document reference.
- The npm allowlist and staging script no longer include the internal root
  `ARCHITECTURE.md`; dry-pack validation enforces the exact public file set.
- The internal root architecture and main-flow documents remain private
  engineering records in the source repository and are not copied into the
  public submodule or npm package.

## Validation record

The following focused and repository-wide gates passed sequentially through the
sanctioned capped Docker/Node wrappers:

- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 fmt --all -- --check`
- listener-side match retention and `send` newline rejection tests
- bounded listener-readiness and explicit-empty-environment tests
- distributed-runtime filename and listener-auto-start consistency checks
- visible-only `process send_input` echo-policy test
- mutable-line cursor, status-line finalization, and local-backend replacement tests
- tool-description snapshot tests and real `shell_session_e2e` coverage
- bounded streaming-sentinel split-read tests and the segmented fake-peer test
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 build --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test --workspace`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_config --test schema -- --nocapture`
- `scripts/nverify.ps1` (68 tests: 65 passed, 3 platform skips)
- `scripts/dverify.ps1 refactor-stability`
- main and public-submodule `git diff --check`

The final `refactor-stability` report completed every gate with exit code 0 at
`.build-safe/windows/dverify-runs/20260721T161103Z-29128-7934/resource-report.json`.

`npm run check` was intentionally not used as a non-interactive gate because its
repository contract builds an image and launches the interactive TUI. All Cargo
compilation, tests, and linting ran only inside the capped Docker wrappers.

title: Auto-Compaction Hard-Cut — "compress and continue" instead of stopping (2026-07-27)
text:
Date: 2026-07-27
Status: **Complete** — F1+F2 landed (`6aded385`), Docker-verified
Baseline branch: `sweep/major-2026-07-27` (or `main`)

## Problem

When the conversation approaches the model's context limit, the agent **just
stops** instead of compacting and continuing. Reported symptom: "컨텍스트 초과
될 것 같으면 압축해서 진행돼야 하는데 지금은 그냥 멈춰버립니다."


1. **The compaction threshold is inert by default.**
   `builder_domain::Compact::default().token_threshold == None`
   (`compact/compact_config.rs:88`), and the agent's threshold is populated
   *only* from `config.compact.token_threshold` (`agent.rs:140-154`), which also
   defaults to `None` (`builder_config/src/compact.rs:101`). It is **never
   derived from the model's `context_length`** (`builder_domain/src/model.rs:28`).
   (`orch.rs::context_window_warning_state`) and `should_compact` are dead:
   `should_compact_due_to_tokens` returns `false` whenever `token_threshold` is
   `None` (`compact_config.rs:107-112`).

2. **There is no runtime hard-cut.** `Compact::should_compact()` has **zero
   production callers** (only tests). Nothing force-compacts before a request.
   The whole design leans on the model voluntarily calling the `compact` tool
   after seeing the warning — the warning that (per #1) is usually never shown.
   The reminder text even promises "Runtime hard-cut compaction is fallback
   only" (`orch.rs:1251`), but that fallback was never implemented.

3. **Overflow ends the turn.** `prepare_request_iteration` only *prunes stale
   tool results* (`orch.rs:461`) and injects the (usually-absent) warning, then
   sends. If the request exceeds the provider's window, `request_chat_message`
   retries the same over-limit context, fails, and the error propagates. The
   interactive turn does not — it prints the error and stops.


Design decision (user, confirmed): **no runtime hard-cut** — the model decides to
compact. The reason it doesn't today is the warning never fires, because the
compaction threshold (`token_threshold`) is `None` and is never tied to the
model's **context window**. Two distinct values, both per-model:

- **Output max_tokens** — `/model`'s existing "tokens" field → `config.max_tokens`
  → response-length cap. Keep as-is.
- **Context window** (`context_length`) — the model's total token budget. This is
  what compaction needs and what is currently missing for custom models. The
  threshold must track it, per current model, never hardcoded, and update when the
  model changes.

Rule everywhere: **effective compaction threshold = context_window × 0.80**
(warning fires at ~70% of that ≈ 56% of the window — an early nudge with ample
head-room). Sources of the context window, in priority:
1. Explicit `config.compact.token_threshold` (persisted by `/model`, see F2) —
   already stored pre-multiplied, used directly.
2. Current provider model's `Model.context_length` (auto, for listed models).
3. Otherwise `None` → no warning (can't know the window; unchanged behavior).

In `refresh_context_window_warning` (`orch.rs`), each request:
- If the user configured `config.compact.token_threshold` → use it (don't touch).
- Else recompute from the **current** model's `context_length`
  `self.agent.compact.token_threshold` — **recomputed every call, not cached**, so
  switching models mid-session updates it. (Fixes the cache bug in the first cut.)
`context_window_warning_state` then fires and injects the "call `compact` …"
reminder; the model compacts via the existing `apply_model_requested_compaction`.

`ui/model_select.rs`:
- Add a **"context window"** input to the custom form. New order:
  URL → model → key → **context window** → output max_tokens.
  effective threshold orch reads via source #1). Output max_tokens stays; if the
  user leaves it blank, default it from the context window
  (`min(window / 4, sane_cap)`).
- Update the form copy to clearly distinguish the two values.
- Provider-model (listed) selection: leave `config.compact.token_threshold`
  unset so orch auto-derives from the model's known `context_length` (source #2),
  keeping switches fresh.

- **No runtime hard-cut** / forced `should_compact`-triggered compaction.
  `should_compact` stays model-advisory only.
- No forced compact-on-overflow retry.

## Files

- `crates/builder_app/src/orch.rs` — F1: per-request threshold derivation in
  `refresh_context_window_warning` (+ `default_compact_token_threshold` helper +
  tests). **(first cut already landed; needs the no-cache/per-model fix.)**
- `crates/builder_main/src/ui/model_select.rs` — F2: context-window form field,
  persistence to `config.compact.token_threshold`, output-max-tokens default,
  copy.
- `crates/builder_config/src/compact.rs` — confirm `token_threshold` persists.


- `dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_app orch -- --nocapture` + new unit test:
  - `default_compact_token_threshold(context_length)` maps to ~80% (and floors).
  - after `refresh_context_window_warning` with a model that has `context_length`
    and no configured threshold, `agent.compact.token_threshold` is populated and
    the warning reminder is injected once the context crosses ~70% of it.
- `dbuild.ps1 clippy -p builder_app --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `dbuild.ps1 test --workspace` at the end.
  the window edge, and the model compacts and keeps going instead of stopping.

## Non-goals
- **No runtime hard-cut / forced compaction** — model-driven only (user
  decision).
- Changing the summary/compaction algorithm itself (`Compactor`) — only making
  the *warning* engage.
- Touching `README.md` / `docs/linkedin/`.

title: Major Sweep — Code Review · TUI UX · Plumbing · Tidy (2026-07-27)
text:
Date: 2026-07-27 Status: **Complete** — full-workspace test green (2131 tests, 0 failed) Baseline: `main` @ `e002dbb3` (v0.101.9) Working branch: `sweep/major-2026-07-27` ## Context `main` is green at `v0.101.9`. The 2026-07-18 DeepCodeReview (P0–P3) and 2026-07-19 FlowWiringCleanup (W1–W4) series have all landed. Since v0.101.9, three TUI fixes landed (single interrupt event per cancellation `384d4fd3`, shared active-turn input history `52415956`, PTY control hardening `05db7c32`) but no integrated full-pass sweep has run against the current tree. This sweep does, in one coordinated series: (A) fresh defect-hunt review, (B) TUI UX — robustness + visual balance, (C) plumbing/refactor of the oversized files, (D) tech-debt triage. Constraints (auto-memory + `AGENTS.md`): - **Verification is Docker-only** via `scripts/dbuild.{sh,ps1}` — host `.claude/settings.json`. Windows uses the `.ps1` wrappers. - `README.md` / `docs/linkedin/` are user-owned — untouched. - One commit per item; `main` stays green at each step. ## Workstreams - **A — Code review (defect hunt).** interrupt/input/active-turn share, PTY / shell listener, output actor / backpressure, auto-loop / completion obligation. Findings logged in `REVIEW_Sweep_2026-07-27.md` as CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE. Only CONFIRMED gets an immediate fix + regression test. - **B — TUI UX.** B1 robustness (resize/scroll/cursor boundaries, status-row clarity, interrupt responsiveness). B2 visual (spinner cadence/frames, theme palette contrast, prompt chrome) with intentional snapshot updates. - **C — Plumbing.** C1 split `builder_ratatui/src/backend.rs` (~3.7k LoC) into `backend/{wrap,scrollback,bottom_chrome,actor,finalize}.rs`, byte-identical. C2 move residual inline logic out of `builder_main/src/ui/mod.rs`. C3 (`operation.rs`) is watch-only unless A4 requires it. - **D — Tidy.** Triage 30 `allow(dead_code)` + TODO/FIXME across 12 files; remove only genuinely dead code, reinforce reserved ones with reasons. 1. A review → ledger, fix CONFIRMED. 2. B1 robustness regression tests + fixes. 3. C1 backend split, per-seam commits, byte-identical gate. 4. B2 visual + D tidy in parallel. 5. C2 ui/mod.rs residuals; C3 decision. Per-commit gate (Docker): ``` scripts/dbuild.ps1 fmt scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p --lib ``` Series end: `scripts/dbuild.ps1 test --workspace` + `nverify.ps1` green. - **A — review: DONE.** `REVIEW_Sweep_2026-07-27.md` ledger complete. A1/A3/A4 CLEAR (no actionable defect); A2 deferred to the 2026-07-21 PTY audit. - **D1 — tidy: APPLIED.** Removed dead `RuntimeInterruptListener::new` / `with_buffer` + their `allow(dead_code)`. D2 reserved allows kept (documented), D3 TODOs are backlog (no code change). - **C1 — backend split: IN PROGRESS.** - C1.1 `backend/wrap.rs` — DONE (`4cd97b23`). Moved pure width/ANSI line layout (wrap/transcript-page/visible-rows + cfg-test width helpers). backend.rs −391 LoC. builder_ratatui 236 lib tests + clippy green. - C1.2 `backend/scrollback.rs` — DONE (`e8ec490b`). Moved `committed_scrollback_lines`, `append_committed_scrollback_lines`, `append_scrollback_text`; narrowed `use text_width::*` to `#[cfg(test)]`. backend.rs −166 LoC. fmt/236 tests/clippy green. - backend.rs: 6774 → 6223 LoC so far (−551). - C1.3 `backend/geometry.rs` — DONE (`1ed9638b`). Pure bottom-chrome row/viewport math + actor redraw/flush predicates + reset_session_surface_state. backend.rs −161 LoC. - C1.4 `backend/paint.rs` — DONE (`e209b578`). title: Review Ledger — Major Sweep (2026-07-27)
text:
Date: 2026-07-27
Baseline: `main` @ `e002dbb3` (v0.101.9)
Reviewer pass: direct read of each subsystem below.

test required. **PLAUSIBLE** = suspicious but unverified; kept as backlog with
rationale. **CLEAR** = inspected, no defect found.

---


Scope: `builder_main/src/interrupt.rs`, `ui/mod.rs` input path,
`builder_ratatui` input buffer. Focus: TOCTOU, lock ordering, event
duplication/loss after `384d4fd3` / `52415956`.

Traced:
- **Single-event-per-cancellation** holds. `wait()` awaits `&mut receiver`;
  `stop_and_take_pending_interrupt()` publishes `stop`, **joins the reader**,
  then `try_recv()`. Post-join the one-shot is either already consumed by
  `wait()` (→ `Closed` → `None`) or holds the boundary interrupt (→ `Some`).
  The two paths cannot both yield a source. (`interrupt.rs:302-364`,
  `485-499`.)
- **Ctrl+C-clears vs Esc-interrupts**: `process_interrupt_event` consumes the
  one-shot only on `Interrupt`; a buffer-clearing Ctrl+C keeps `sender` for a
  later Esc. Covered by
  `test_process_ctrl_c_clears_buffer_without_consuming_interrupt`.
- **Pause coordinator** (`InputReaderPauseCoordinator`): `pause_depth` is
  balanced on every path (success guard drop, timeout bail, reader-ended bail);
  all locks are poison-recovering. No lost-wakeup found.

No defect. **Tidy applied** (see D1): removed the two dead constructors
`RuntimeInterruptListener::new` / `with_buffer`.


Independently audited 2026-07-21 (`RESULT_AgentPtyControlAudit_2026-07-21.md`)
plus the `05db7c32` hardening. Not re-audited line-by-line this pass; the FD
lifetime / partial-write surface was the direct subject of that audit. Re-open
only if a concrete symptom surfaces.


Scope: `builder_ratatui/src/backend.rs` — `run_output_actor`,
`flush_output_batch`, `SharedOutputBackpressureState`.

Traced:
- `mark_enqueued`/`mark_dequeued`/`rollback_enqueued` keep `enqueued_at`
  (push_back / pop_front / pop_back) and `pending_bytes` (saturating add/sub)
  symmetric; consistent with the P0.4 double-decrement fix. `saturating_sub`
  makes an over-decrement a no-op rather than a panic.
- `wait_until_below` uses `wait_timeout_while` and re-checks the predicate on
  return — no spurious-wakeup escape. All locks poison-recovering.

No defect.


Scope: `builder_app/src/orch*.rs`, `ui/auto_loop.rs`, `completion_obligation/`.

Traced:
  tokens fall through to reason text (cosmetic only, not a defect).
- `decide_auto_continuation`: Blocked → continue-after-claim; Complete with
  `current < target` → continue-after-claim; else Complete. Model stays the
  completion authority with a self-consistency guard. Matches the
  goal-visibility intent of `ea05ea1f`.
- `auto_queue_allows_dispatch` gates on `current_revision == previous_revision`

No defect.

---

## Summary

| ID | Subsystem | CONFIRMED | PLAUSIBLE | CLEAR |
|----|-----------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| A1 | interrupt/input | 0 | 0 | ✅ (+ D1 tidy) |
| A2 | PTY/shell | — | — | deferred to 2026-07-21 audit |
| A3 | output actor | 0 | 0 | ✅ |
| A4 | auto-loop | 0 | 0 | ✅ |

consistent with the three independent zero-defect reviews of the prior series.
The sweep's value therefore lands in **D (tidy)**, **C (plumbing split)**, and
**B (UX)** rather than defect fixes.

---


`interrupt.rs` `RuntimeInterruptListener::new()` and `with_buffer()` had **no
callers workspace-wide** (only `with_buffer_and_callback` is live, via
`terminal_session.rs:344`). Removed both + their two `#[allow(dead_code)]`.

- `porcelain.rs` `into_body` / `into_rows`: used **only** by `#[cfg(test)]`
