cache.put("doc1", [1.0; EMBEDDING_DIM]);
cache.put("doc2", [2.0; EMBEDDING_DIM]);
assert_eq!(cache.get("doc1"), Some([1.0; EMBEDDING_DIM]));
cache.put("doc3", [3.0; EMBEDDING_DIM]);
assert_eq!(cache.get("doc1"), Some([1.0; EMBEDDING_DIM]));
assert_eq!(cache.get("doc2"), None);
```

Also assert replacement accounting, oversized-text non-caching, exact-string separation, 10,000 default capacity, and 16 MiB default payload capacity.

```

Add `hashlink = "0.10.0"` to workspace dependencies and `hashlink.workspace = true` to `builder_workspace_index`. Replace the hash-only map/queue with `LinkedHashMap<String, Embedding>`, refresh hits, maintain accounted payload, and evict from the LRU front until both limits hold.

title: Docker Image `tract-core` OOM Fix Design
text:
Date: 2026-08-12

## Problem

The first application-image build after adding the embedded dense RAG encoder
failed while compiling `tract-core`. The sanctioned BuildKit runner recorded
`reason=container_oom`, `oom_killed=true`, a 4 GiB memory limit, and a 2 CPU
limit. Cargo reported that it was waiting for other jobs after the killed
`tract-core` process, proving that more than one crate compilation was active.
Earlier image builds without the new `tract-onnx` dependency completed under
the same resource envelope.

the wrapper still returned `container_oom`. Its report started with
`oom_kill_count_before=1`; the live cgroup remained at `oom_kill=1`. The false
failure came from Docker's container-lifetime `.State.OOMKilled=true`, retained
after BuildKit restarted from the first OOM, rather than a new OOM event.

This is a build-time peak-memory regression. It is not evidence of a model
loading, embedding, search, or runtime-image failure.

## Constraints

- Keep `npm run check -> npm run check:docker` unchanged.
- Raise only image-building BuildKit memory and equal swap to 6 GiB.
- Keep 2 CPUs, 512 PIDs, and one BuildKit stage.
- Keep ordinary Cargo validation and the outer release runner at their current
  independent memory limits.
- Keep the embedded transformer model and dense RAG runtime unchanged.
- Do not run Cargo directly on the host.
- Preserve the existing Docker release optimization profile unless evidence
  shows that one serial `rustc` process still exceeds the cap.

## Design

hard maximum from 4 GiB to 6 GiB. Both wrappers must continue applying equal
memory and swap values to the dedicated BuildKit node and revalidate the exact
effective limits before every image build.

Make the per-build cgroup `oom_kill` delta authoritative. Always sample the
counter after an ordinary build, regardless of the container-lifetime
`.State.OOMKilled` value. A positive delta is `container_oom`; an unchanged
counter is not an OOM; an unreadable or decreasing counter is
`postflight_failed`. Timeout and storage-watchdog reasons keep precedence.

Add lightweight Node contract tests for the 6 GiB image-builder envelope and
the counter-delta rule. Update the normative build-safety text without changing
the separate local-release 4 GiB outer-container cap.

## Verification

Run checks sequentially:

1. Demonstrate the new contract tests fail before the wrapper changes.
2. Run the focused Node resource-safety test after the changes.
3. Run the sanctioned Windows Node verification wrapper.
4. Run `scripts/dbuild-image.ps1 app`, which exercises the failing image-build
   segment under the enforced 6 GiB limit.
5. Inspect the emitted resource report and require `reason=complete`, exit code

`npm run check` itself remains an interactive TUI contract, so automated
verification stops after the same image build succeeds. The maintainer can

## Failure Boundary

If a 6 GiB build records a positive cgroup `oom_kill` delta, stop and use that
new report to test a separate hypothesis: reduce only the Docker release
profile's compilation parallelism. Do not raise the cap again in the same
attempt.

## Expected Trade-off

Ordinary validation and release-orchestration caps, runtime binary behavior,
model contents, and search quality remain unchanged.

title: 증거 기반 공격 경로 추천과 지식 시스템 단순화 설계
text:
## 목표

현재의 정적 Lead 우선순위를 실제 도구 실행 결과로 학습하는 경량 PUCT 추천으로 교체한다. 서브에이전트 원문과 증거는 보존하고, 검증 가능한 구조화 신호만 공격 경로 평가에 사용한다. 동시에 호출되지 않는 지식 유지보수 기능과 쓰기 경로를 제거하고 대화 파생 메모리의 무제한 성장을 막는다.

이 변경의 핵심은 다음 세 가지다.

- RRF 기반 지식 검색은 유지한다.
- PUCT는 Lead 선택과 핵심 공격 경로 추천에만 사용한다.
- 요약 가능한 표시 데이터와 삭제하면 안 되는 원본 기록을 명확히 분리한다.

## 현행 문제

현재 `explore frontier`의 focus는 카테고리 기본 점수, 신선도, 저비용 보너스를 정렬한 표시용 항목이다. 방문 횟수, 경로별 누적 성과, 미탐색 분기, 검증 결과가 선택에 반영되지 않으므로 MCTS가 아니다.

서브에이전트 결과에는 별도의 3줄 요약 계약이 없다. 마지막 Markdown 응답 전체가 부모 도구 출력으로 전달되고 자식 대화 ID가 함께 보존된다. 현재 자식 실행이 오류만 아니면 자유 형식 답변의 내용이나 증거 여부와 무관하게 원본 Lead가 `Deepening`으로 바뀐다. 이 상태를 보상으로 사용하면 근거 없는 자신감이나 장문 응답이 경로 추천을 오염시킬 수 있다.

대화 메모리는 한 턴에 최대 3개가 생성되지만 세션 전체 상한이 없다. 로컬 저장소의 후보 조회는 전달받은 `limit`도 적용하지 않아, 세션이 길어질수록 매 회상 때 전체 파생 메모리를 다시 인덱싱한다.

지식 계층에는 MOC 생성, note fission/fusion, workspace healing, orphan archive, temporal supersession, access writeback, canvas writer처럼 제품 런타임에서 호출되지 않거나 기본 비활성인 유지보수 기능이 남아 있다. 이 기능들은 검색 품질의 핵심인 BM25, dense, WikiLink graph, RRF와 무관하게 복잡도와 쓰기 위험만 늘린다.


별도의 LLM 시뮬레이션이나 백그라운드 스케줄러를 만들지 않는다. 명시적인 `explore dispatch` 한 번을 해당 Lead의 한 번의 실제 rollout으로 취급한다.

추천 점수는 다음 형태의 PUCT를 사용한다.

```text
recommendation = Q(node) + C × P(node) × sqrt(max(1, visits(parent))) / (1 + visits(node))
Q(node) = value_sum(node) / max(1, visits(node))
```

- `P(node)`는 기존 카테고리·신선도·저비용 신호를 0과 1 사이로 정규화한 prior다.
- `Q(node)`는 실제 dispatch 이후 구조화 결과에서 얻은 평균 보상이다.
- 방문하지 않은 분기는 탐색 보너스를 받아 한 번은 검토될 수 있다.
- 반복 실패한 분기는 평균 보상과 기존 dead-probe 억제로 자연스럽게 뒤로 밀린다.
- 추천 계산은 순수 함수이며 저장소 읽기나 실행 권한을 갖지 않는다.

`explore frontier`는 추천 경로 한 개와 대안 두 개를 bounded projection으로 반환한다. 기존의 상태 집계, integrity alert, pivot alert는 유지한다. 추천은 실행 명령이 아니며 실제 실행은 계속 `explore dispatch(node_ids)`로만 가능하다.


`ExplorationNode`에는 최소한의 rollout 통계만 둔다. 이 통계는 별도 학습 모델이 아니라 실제 rollout을 한 샘플씩 반영하는 온라인 SGD 상태다.

- `visit_count`: 완료된 dispatch 평가 횟수
- `value_sum`: bounded 보상 누계
- `squared_error_sum`: 갱신 직전 예측과 실제 보상의 제곱오차 누계

경로 가치와 prediction loss는 다음처럼 계산한다.

```text
Q_before = value_sum / max(1, visit_count)
error = reward - Q_before
prediction_loss_sample = 1/2 × error²
alpha = 1 / (visit_count + 1)
Q_after = Q_before + alpha × error
prediction_loss = squared_error_sum / max(1, visit_count)
```

`Q_after`는 누적 평균과 동일하므로 별도 optimizer, tensor, checkpoint가 필요 없다. PUCT 추천에는 `Q + exploration - loss_penalty`를 사용해 값이 높더라도 아직 불안정한 경로를 과신하지 않는다.

새 필드는 serde 기본값을 사용해 기존 Lead 증거를 그대로 읽는다. 기존 `score`는 마이그레이션 호환을 위해 읽을 수 있게 유지하되 추천 권한을 제거하고 prior 계산의 입력으로만 제한하거나, 모든 소비자가 전환된 뒤 안전하게 제거한다. 이벤트 소싱 구조와 최신 Lead event fold는 그대로 유지한다.

부모 방문 수가 없는 루트 Lead는 같은 run의 가상 루트 방문 합계를 사용한다. 보상은 해당 Lead에서 루트까지 역전파하되, 각 노드는 dispatch 한 번당 정확히 한 번만 갱신한다. 동일 결과 재처리 방지는 기존 append-only 사건의 고유 참조 또는 dispatch 평가 ID로 보장한다.


서브에이전트의 자유 형식 Markdown은 사용자·부모 에이전트가 읽는 설명이며 점수 입력이 아니다. 다음 원본은 하드 컷하지 않는다.

- 자식 conversation 전체
- 자식 run과 tool/evidence 기록
- 부모 ToolOutput에 포함된 최종 Markdown
- delegation proof와 evidence reference

공격 경로 평가는 이미 지속된 구조화 신호만 사용한다.

- 검증 provenance가 있는 결정적 결과: 큰 양수
- `finding`으로 기록되고 source reference가 있는 새 증거: 중간 양수
- 중복되지 않은 새 자식 Lead: 작은 양수
- 정상 종료했지만 새 증거가 없음: 0 또는 작은 음수
- 명시적 dead probe: 음수
- transport/provider 오류: 작은 비용 패널티만 적용하며 가설을 자동 반증하지 않음
- blocked: 중립 처리하며 사용자 입력 없이 재dispatch하지 않음

모델의 `solve` 주장이나 `FLAG{...}` 문자열만으로 큰 보상이나 mission completion을 부여하지 않는다. 기존 `VerificationProvenance`가 완료 판정의 유일한 권위라는 규칙을 유지한다.

dispatch 전후의 canonical Lead/Finding/verification 사건 차이를 이용해 평가를 생성한다. 이를 위해 부모 Lead ID, 자식 conversation ID, 자식 run ID, 평가 ID를 구조화된 delegation 결과에 연결한다. XML 문자열이나 Markdown을 다시 파싱해 상태를 추론하지 않는다.


하드 컷은 원본이 별도로 보존되고 안정적인 참조로 복구 가능한 표시용 projection에만 허용한다.

- 허용: attention brief의 제목·설명, UI preview, shell/search 결과의 원본 파일 참조가 있는 preview
- 금지: 서브에이전트 최종 결과 원본, 검증 provenance, evidence record, 대화 원문, 아직 영속화되지 않은 tool result

컨텍스트 compaction은 기존 구조화 `ContextSummary`를 사용한다. 같은 자원에 대한 중복 성공 작업을 줄일 수 있지만, 서로 다른 작업·실패 근거·검증 결과를 단순히 “마지막 것”만 남기는 방식으로 확대하지 않는다. 이번 변경에서는 별도 LLM 압축기를 추가하지 않는다.


대화 파생 메모리는 conversation당 최대 64개로 제한한다. 원본 conversation은 삭제하지 않는다.

- 저장소 `search_conversation_memory_candidates`는 요청된 limit을 실제로 적용한다.
- upsert 후 같은 conversation의 파생 메모리가 상한을 넘으면 결정적으로 정리한다.
- `Constraint`와 `Preference`는 가장 높은 보존 우선순위를 갖는다. 보호 항목만으로 상한을 넘는 극단적인 경우에도 원본 conversation은 남아 있으므로 최신 항목부터 64개를 유지해 하드 상한을 지킨다.
- 활성 objective별 최신 `Goal`을 우선 보존한다.
- 나머지 `Context`와 `Episode`는 중요도와 최신성 순으로 남긴다.
- 동일 deterministic hash는 기존처럼 갱신하며 중복 개수를 늘리지 않는다.

현재 자동 추출기는 `Goal`과 `Context`만 만들므로, 보존 규칙은 향후 다른 kind를 읽을 때도 안전하게 동작해야 한다. 상한 정리는 파생 인덱스 관리이며 사용자의 원문을 요약하거나 삭제하는 기능이 아니다.


다음 런타임 핵심은 유지한다.

- Markdown note parsing과 태그
- BM25 lexical retrieval
- 내장 transformer encoder 기반 384차원 dense retrieval
- WikiLink graph, backlink count, PageRank/hop ranking
- RRF와 현재의 contextual reranking
- archive/tombstone/privacy/malicious note read filters
- 이미 존재하는 scratchpad의 bounded read-only prompt snapshot

다음 무호출 또는 불필요한 쓰기 기능은 제거한다.

- MOC draft와 fusion cluster
- note fission plan
- workspace heal과 orphan archive
- memory lifecycle plan/apply와 temporal supersession writer
- 검색 access reinforcement writeback
- scratchpad create/replace/append API
- canvas document types와 writer
- explicit backlink section sync writer가 제품 호출 없이 남아 있다면 함께 제거

scratchpad는 파일이 이미 있을 때만 읽는다. 검색이나 prompt 생성이 scratchpad, MOC, canvas, backlink section을 자동 생성하도록 유도하지 않는다. WikiLink와 backlink 계산은 읽기 전용 graph ranking 신호로 계속 사용한다.


- 추천 계산 실패는 frontier 전체 실행을 막지 않고 기존 상태 집계만 반환하는 fail-soft가 아니다. 순수 계산이므로 비정상 수치나 손상된 부모 관계는 integrity alert로 격리하고 해당 노드를 추천 후보에서 제외한다.
- dispatch 시작 시 방문 수를 올리지 않는다. 취소된 dispatch가 성공 rollout처럼 기록되는 것을 막기 위해 결과 평가를 영속화할 때 방문을 반영한다.
- 자식 일부가 실패해도 같은 batch의 다른 결과는 각각 평가한다.
- partial Markdown만 남은 interrupt는 원문 보존에는 성공하지만 구조화 증거가 없다면 양수 보상을 받지 않는다.
- 기존 dead probe 임계값 2와 breadth/depth/node cap은 유지한다.
- 자동 dispatch, detached worker, 별도 scheduler loop는 추가하지 않는다.


prediction loss와 mission goal loss는 권위가 다르다. prediction loss가 0이라는 사실은 경로 보상 예측이 수렴했다는 뜻일 뿐 목표 달성을 증명하지 않는다.

```text
goal_loss = 0.0  when MissionState::Verified with VerificationProvenance
goal_loss = 1.0  when MissionState::Open
goal_loss = 1.0  when MissionState::Blocked
```

현재 런타임의 `TaskComplete`는 검증된 mission에서만 발생하므로 `/auto`는 이를 zero goal-loss 신호로 사용해 종료한다. 모델 Stop, `solve`, 100% 진행 문구, prediction loss 0은 종료 신호가 아니다. 검증되지 않은 tool/request budget interrupt는 goal loss가 남아 있는 상태이므로 auto mode가 명시적으로 켜졌을 때만 다음 턴으로 진행한다. 사용자 입력, 권한, 외부 의존성이 필요한 blocked 상태에서는 자동 진행하지 않는다.

Run close metadata에는 숫자 `goal_loss`와 그 권위 원천을 기록해 진단 가능하게 한다. 이 값은 기존 `RunOutcome.completed`와 `VerificationProvenance`에서 결정적으로 투영하며 새 완료 판정기를 만들지 않는다.

## 문서 최신화

구현 후 `docs/human`의 모든 문서를 코드와 대조한다.

- `README.md`: 실제 문서 목록과 읽는 순서
- `pentesting_architecture.md`: 정적 attention이 아닌 PUCT 공격 경로 추천, 명시적 dispatch, 원본 보존 경계
- `knowledge_note_lifecycle.md`: 제거된 MOC/fission/fusion/heal/canvas/writeback을 삭제하고 단순한 읽기·회상·상한 정책 설명

문서는 기존 Q&A와 설명 스타일을 유지하며 구현하지 않은 기능이나 benchmark 수치를 주장하지 않는다. 루트 README와 공개 미러는 실제 사용자 기능 설명이 달라지는 범위에서만 짧게 맞춘다.

## 검증

구현은 테스트 우선으로 진행한다. 호스트 Cargo와 호스트 `npm run check/verify`는 실행하지 않는다. 모든 컴파일·테스트·lint는 저장소의 메모리 제한 Docker wrapper로 순차 실행한다.

필수 검증 범위는 다음과 같다.

- PUCT 선택의 exploitation/exploration 균형, 미방문 분기, tie-break 결정성
- rollout 보상과 루트까지의 단일 역전파
- 온라인 SGD 값 갱신, prediction loss, 불안정 경로 패널티
- verified mission만 `goal_loss=0`, model stop/blocked는 non-zero인 완료 회귀 테스트
- 자유 형식 Markdown과 미검증 `solve`가 보상을 만들지 않는 회귀 테스트
- 자식 대화/run/evidence reference의 producer-to-consumer 연결
- 기존 Lead event 역직렬화 호환성
- conversation memory 64개 상한, kind별 보존, 실제 candidate limit
- 제거 API에 대한 production callsite 부재 확인
- RRF, dense, graph 검색 회귀 테스트
- attention/frontier bounded output과 명시적 dispatch 경계
- 관련 crate Docker test, fmt, clippy
- Node 검증과 refactor stability
- `git diff --check`와 문서·consistency 검사

최종 완료 조건은 코드, 테스트, `docs/human` 최신화, 루트/공개 문서 일치, 깨끗한 worktree, 프로젝트 `main` 커밋과 원격 push까지 모두 확인된 상태다.

title: Multilingual Retrieval Intent Design
text:
## Purpose

Remove the language-based retrieval bypass without changing the user's message or response language. A single front-door layer produces one bounded English retrieval intent for every prompt and shares it across vault, skill, and conversation-memory retrieval.

## Boundary

The normalizer receives the current event query plus the already resolved agent model/provider. Every non-empty input, including English input, makes exactly one small structured model request that translates when needed and summarizes retrieval intent while preserving identifiers and constraints. It never answers the request or changes routing, objectives, persistence, or the main conversation.


The result must be non-empty, English-compatible, and bounded. Invalid output or provider failure is fail-soft: retain ASCII identifiers from the original query as a limited lexical/dense-safe fallback, or use an empty retrieval query when no safe terms exist. Failures are logged without prompt content.

## Plumbing

`BuilderApp::prepare_chat_conversation` owns normalization because it is the first point with the current event and resolved model/provider. It passes the same value to `SystemPrompt` for vault and skill selection and to memory-note injection for conversation recall. The original event continues unchanged to the user-prompt generator and main model.

## Verification

Tests cover English and Korean prompt-to-prompt normalization, one-call sharing, malformed/error fallback, and the three retrieval consumers. Validation uses only capped Docker Cargo wrappers plus the lightweight Node wrapper and repository consistency checks.

title: Session Footer and Velog Theme Design
text:
> Superseded on 2026-08-13 by the later coral terminal palette and quiet-chrome decision. Token/runtime values remain internal session state but are not rendered in the footer. The current visual contract is `2026-08-13-coral-terminal-palette-design.md`.

## Outcome

The terminal keeps a fixed footer visible while idle and active. It shows the current conversation's human-readable cumulative token usage and the current process session's cumulative active turn runtime, for example `tokens 12.4k · run 3m 18s`.

## Session semantics

- Tokens come from the persisted conversation's accumulated message usage.
- `/resume` restores the selected conversation's token total.
- Runtime begins at zero when the process starts or a conversation is resumed.
- `/clear` and `/new` both create/reset the active session view and set token/runtime counters to zero.
- Values use compact readable formatting and remain present in narrow layouts before optional model/goal detail.

## Theme

- Dark-mode primary is the Velog green `#20C997` (`RGB 32,201,151`).
- Random per-turn darkening of the primary is removed.
- The shimmer rests on a clear Velog mint and peaks near white (`#F2FFFB`) to read as a moving light reflection.

## Plumbing

Conversation usage and turn duration are projected into one footer status value. Session reset/resume paths update that value through the same helper, preventing stale counters. Footer rendering owns width-aware formatting; business state does not pre-truncate values.

## Verification

Unit tests cover token/time formatting, reset/resume semantics, narrow footer preservation, exact palette values, and white shimmer highlights. Existing PTY and refactor-stability gates verify prompt ownership and fixed-row cleanup remain unchanged.

title: Runtime and Release Reliability Refactor Design
text:
## Goal

기존 동작을 보존하면서 TUI의 자율 실행 상태와 턴 표시 책임을 작은 모듈로 나누고, npm이 오래된 로컬 바이너리를 실행하는 결함을 제거한다. 작업 완료는 코드 커밋만이 아니라 GitHub 바이너리, npm, Docker까지 같은 버전으로 배포되고 검증된 상태를 뜻한다.

## Confirmed problem

공개 `v0.101.20` GitHub asset과 Docker image 안의 바이너리는 모두 `builder 0.101.20`이며 SHA-256도 `ec4e2fea6f1904345b4e2f0e5ad4cb8469db8bb200065e3a082293ada35a1e0a`로 같다. 게시된 바이너리가 오래된 것이 아니다.

문제는 npm 실행기다. `resolveBuilderBinary()`는 `vendor/builder` 파일이 있으면 manifest의 release tag, repository, asset identity를 확인하지 않고 실행한다. npm 업데이트의 postinstall 다운로드가 실패하면 새 package가 이전 바이너리를 계속 실행할 수 있다.

## Boundaries

### Managed runtime

- 실행 전 바이너리 파일과 manifest가 현재 `builderReleaseTag`, repository, asset name과 모두 일치해야 한다.
- 불일치 상태에서 다운로드가 허용되면 현재 release asset을 다시 설치한다.
- 다운로드가 금지되거나 실패하면 오래된 바이너리를 실행하지 않고 이유가 분명한 오류를 반환한다.

### TUI modules

- `ui/auto_loop.rs`: 문자열 파싱, retry 분류, 다음 행동 결정처럼 I/O가 없는 정책만 소유한다.
- `ui/auto_state.rs`: `UIState`의 goal/auto 활성화, 무효화, interrupt, 완료 turn commit만 소유한다.
- 상위 `ui/mod.rs`와 `turn_runtime.rs`는 호출 순서와 I/O 조정만 담당한다.
- 타입, 상태 전이 순서, queue 우선권, Esc 취소, typed `TaskComplete` 완료 권한은 바꾸지 않는다.

### Answer colour

- AI 일반 본문은 고정 Foreground `#E6EDF3`를 사용한다.
- TUI·Markdown·shell·HTML UI는 primary `#FF7B72`와 승인된 green, purple,
  blue, orange, muted, foreground, dark background/surface 팔레트만 사용한다.
- README와 공개 대표 아이콘은 메인테이너 지시에 따라 검정색을 쓰는 유일한 예외다.
- 터미널의 밝음/어두움 힌트와 무관하게 동일한 고정 팔레트를 유지한다.
- primary coral은 spinner, 선택 상태, 링크·inline code처럼 좁은 강조 역할에만 남긴다.
- footer와 입력 chrome은 고정 Muted `#8B949E`를 사용한다.


릴리스 완료는 아래 네 항목이 모두 성공해야 한다.

2. patch tag와 GitHub Release 바이너리를 private/public repository에 게시한다.
3. 같은 patch version의 npm package를 `latest`로 게시한다.

최종 검증은 Cargo version, package version, builder release tag, Git tag, npm latest, GitHub asset의 `--version`, Docker image의 `--version`, GitHub/Docker 바이너리 SHA가 모두 같은 release를 가리키는지 확인한다. 하나라도 다르면 완료로 보고하지 않는다.

## Legacy cleanup

- 파일 존재만으로 managed runtime을 신뢰하는 경로를 제거한다.
- 이미 분리된 모듈과 중복되는 helper만 이동·정리한다.
- persisted snapshot reader, provider compatibility adapter, CLI alias처럼 실제 호환성 계약인 코드는 삭제하지 않는다.
- 임시 provenance 파일은 `.build-safe` 안에서만 만들고 검증 후 제거한다.

## Documentation

`docs/human`은 쉬운 문장과 짧은 흐름을 우선한다. 전문 용어는 뜻을 먼저 설명하고, 현재 구현과 향후 계획을 섞지 않는다. 전체 구조 문서에는 새 모듈 경계와 AI 본문 색상을, 새 release 문서에는 4종 배포와 검증 방법을 기록한다.

## Verification

모든 Rust 빌드·테스트·clippy는 Docker 제한 래퍼만 사용한다. Node 검증도 `nverify`/release container를 사용한다. 변경 전후 auto/queue/Esc/PTY 상태, markdown theme, npm managed runtime, release consistency와 producer-to-consumer 연결을 확인한다.

title: One-Command Release Design
text:
## Goal

`npm run release` is the only command a maintainer needs to commit and push all
current changes and publish the next patch release to all four required public
surfaces.

## Architecture

The root npm script remains a native Windows PowerShell entrypoint. The wrapper
first runs a lightweight Node contract test, then commits and pushes changes in
the `public` submodule, commits all root changes, obtains release credentials,
and enters the existing capped Docker release runner. Git Bash receives the
runner script and its arguments directly; it is never invoked through `-c` or
`-lc`, avoiding shell-string parsing and quoting failures.

The existing `scripts/release-all.sh patch` remains the authoritative release
orchestrator. It creates the version commit and tag, pushes `origin/main`,
publishes npm, updates the public facade pointer, and finishes with
`scripts/verify-release-set.sh`.

## Components

- `package.json`: exposes only the correctly spelled `release` entrypoint.
- `scripts/release.ps1`: validates the entrypoint, prepares both repositories,
- `tests/resource-safety.test.mjs`: statically enforces the safe one-command
  contract without building or publishing.
  verification authority.

## Data Flow

1. The maintainer runs `npm run release` from either PowerShell or Git Bash.
2. PowerShell runs the focused Node release-entrypoint contract test.
3. Dirty `public` content is committed and pushed to its `main` branch.
4. All root changes, including the updated public gitlink, are committed.
5. Credentials and admitted Docker paths are resolved.
6. Git Bash directly executes the capped Docker release runner with
   `scripts/release-all.sh patch` as arguments.

## Failure Handling

Every external command is checked. A failed test, commit, push, credential
lookup, image preparation, release stage, or final verifier stops the command
with a non-zero exit code. Repositories must be on `main`; detached or other
branches are rejected. Empty repositories are not given synthetic commits.

## Validation

Validation is Node-only before the release and does not invoke host Cargo. The
runner. Release success is reported only after the existing four-surface
verifier confirms Git, GitHub assets, npm metadata, Docker tags, executable
version, and matching binary SHA-256 values.

title: Resumable One-Command Release Design
text:
## Goal

interrupted four-surface patch release instead of calculating another patch.

## Decision

The Windows entrypoint will inspect the Cargo workspace version, npm package
version, and `builderReleaseTag` after committing the requested source changes.
When the npm version is behind the workspace version, the builder tag is exactly
orchestrator with that tag. Otherwise it invokes the existing new-patch
orchestrator.

The resume orchestrator runs only inside the admitted capped release container.
It validates `main`, a clean worktree, the version/tag relationship, and tag
ancestry. It then rebuilds the tagged-version binary before remote mutation,
pushes the current commit and tags, overwrites GitHub release assets, overwrites
the two Docker tags, publishes npm only when that immutable version is absent,

## Failure handling

Publishing steps are idempotent where their registries permit it. GitHub assets
use clobber uploads and Docker tags are replaced. An npm version is never
republished: matching version/tag metadata is accepted and `latest` is repaired
if necessary; mismatching immutable metadata aborts. Resource ceilings stay at
the repository defaults. A competing build lock or transient host memory
pressure is handled by waiting and rerunning the same command, never by raising
the cap.

## Verification

Node tests exercise the release-action decision through real temporary Cargo and
package files. Static safety tests retain the PowerShell parse check and enforce
that both new and resume paths enter through the capped Docker wrapper. The
release is complete only after the existing four-surface verifier emits
`RELEASE_SET[complete]`.

title: RAG Incremental Cache Hardening Design
text:
**Date:** 2026-08-19
**Status:** Implemented; capped-Docker verification recorded in the implementation plan
**Scope:** `builder_workspace_index`, `builder_knowledge`, related RAG plans and architecture documentation
**Explicitly excluded:** TUI `/session` commands, session projections, and status-row session badges

## Goal

Make the existing dense-embedding reuse path truthful, collision-safe, genuinely LRU, resource-bounded, and verifiable without changing retrieval ranking or adding a file watcher. The production contract is: the next workspace retrieval observes content changes, rebuilds lexical/tag/graph state from the current notes, and invokes ONNX only for dense inputs that are not already cached.

## Current Problems

1. The cache is described as LRU but implements FIFO because reads do not refresh eviction order.
2. The documented 10,000-entry/approximately 17 MB limit was changed to 50,000 entries. Embedding arrays alone can then retain 76,800,000 bytes before map, queue, key, and allocator overhead.
3. `ContentKey` stores only length and two hashes. A collision can silently reuse an embedding for different text, so the comment claiming collision elimination is incorrect.
4. Workspace cache invalidation uses path, length, and modification time. Same-length content with a preserved timestamp can leave a stale retriever active.
5. The plans call the path live O(1) upsert even though production performs an O(N) note/index rebuild on the next retrieval and only the dense model work is incremental.
6. Public `HybridSearchIndex::upsert_note` and `remove_note` are used only by in-module tests and are not connected to any production writer.
7. Duplicate misses in one batch are deduplicated for inference, but telemetry reports occurrence misses and derives batch count from them rather than from unique model inputs.
8. The refinement plan requires direct inference-count, strict bounds, and latency evidence, but its task state and documentation do not match the shipped code.

## Architecture


Add `hashlink = "0.10.0"` as a workspace dependency and use `hashlink::LinkedHashMap<String, Embedding>` inside `EmbeddingCache`.

- A cache hit refreshes that exact text to the most-recently-used end.
- A new insertion evicts from the least-recently-used end until both limits are satisfied.
- `String` equality is authoritative. Hash collisions are handled by the map's equality check and can never produce an embedding hit for different text.
- ONNX execution remains outside the cache mutex.
- Poisoned cache locks remain fail-soft: reads become misses and writes are skipped, preserving correct inference results at the cost of cache reuse.

`ContentKey`, `get_by_key`, and `put_by_key` are removed. `DenseEncoder` and batch deduplication operate on exact `&str`/`String` content.


The global cache enforces both:

- `DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY = 10_000` entries.
- `DEFAULT_CACHE_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` accounted payload bytes.

Accounted cost is `size_of::<Embedding>() + text.len()` for each entry. This measures the payload owned for semantic reuse and is enforced on every insertion. It deliberately does not claim to equal process RSS or allocator/map overhead. Text whose single accounted cost exceeds the byte budget is returned normally but is not cached.

The cache exposes read-only `len()`, `payload_bytes()`, `capacity()`, and `payload_capacity()` accessors for regression assertions and diagnostics. Tests assert the invariant after every insertion, including long-text and replacement cases.


`DenseEncoder::embed_documents` keeps input order and same-batch deduplication using exact text equality.

It records separate counts:

- `cache_hits`: input slots satisfied by the global cache.
- `cache_duplicate_reuses`: additional input slots sharing a unique miss within the same call.
- `cache_misses`: unique texts physically submitted to the model.
- `batch_count`: batches calculated from unique model inputs.

The direct `inference_count` assertion remains and is strengthened so a repeated batch proves zero new physical graph executions.


`MarkdownFileStamp` gains a SHA-256 content digest. Workspace snapshot loading reads each markdown file once and retains the captured UTF-8 buffer with its digest, path, captured length, and modification time. Cache hits discard those buffers without parsing; cache misses derive each `MarkdownNote` from the corresponding captured buffer.

- A same-length content change invalidates the retriever even if modification time is restored.
- Added, removed, renamed, and changed files continue to invalidate the cache.
- Read errors remain explicit and abort retriever preparation rather than serving data known to be unverifiable.

SHA-256 is used for change identity. Parsing the same captured bytes closes the former time-of-check/time-of-use gap where a file could change between stamping and note loading. This performs one bounded sequential read per markdown file during cache-key preparation and avoids ONNX recomputation for unchanged content.


No OS watcher or mutable background index is introduced. The production flow remains:

1. `build_workspace_knowledge_guidance` requests `UnifiedRetriever::cached_for_workspace`.
2. The retriever computes content-aware vault stamps.
3. An identical key returns the existing immutable retriever.
5. Local and global exact-content caches reuse unchanged dense embeddings; ONNX receives only unique changed texts.
6. The next search consumes the rebuilt immutable index.

This is O(N) change detection/index rebuilding plus O(delta) dense inference, not an O(1) total update and not background real-time indexing.

The unused public `upsert_note` and `remove_note` methods are removed. Replacement coverage is retained through `from_notes_with_cache` tests that construct a differing replacement index and prove the prior immutable index is unchanged. A private construction seam accepts the document-embedding operation so a deterministic failure test can prove that failed replacement construction also leaves the prior immutable index unchanged; the public production path still always uses `DenseEncoder::embed_documents`.


- The LRU mutex covers only lookup, refresh, insertion, accounting, and eviction.
- Model inference never runs while the mutex is held.
- Concurrent callers may both miss before either inserts. This bounded duplicate work is accepted to avoid holding a global lock across ONNX execution; correctness is preserved because exact content is authoritative.
- Cache poisoning degrades to uncached inference and never returns a guessed embedding.
- Content-stamp read failures are returned with the affected path in context.
- Empty document batches return an empty vector without cache or model work.

## Testing Strategy

All Rust compilation and tests run only through `scripts/dbuild.ps1` with the repository's Docker limits.


1. A hit on `doc1` followed by insertion of `doc3` evicts `doc2`, proving access refresh and true LRU behavior.
2. Replacing an existing entry updates payload accounting without increasing entry count.
3. Entry count never exceeds 10,000 and accounted payload never exceeds 16 MiB.
4. Oversized text is not cached.
5. Distinct exact strings occupy distinct entries and return their own embeddings; the production map's `String` equality, rather than a digest-only key, is the collision-resolution authority.
6. Mixed hit/miss/duplicate input preserves output order and reports unique miss/batch counts.
8. Same-length markdown content produces a different content digest and workspace cache key with every legacy metadata field normalized equal.
9. Each workspace snapshot hashes exactly the byte buffer used to parse its corresponding note.
10. Added, removed, and changed notes are visible on the next `cached_for_workspace` call while unchanged embeddings are reused.
11. Producer-to-consumer system-prompt retrieval restores the original mtime and still observes changed equal-length content on the next guidance build.

### Performance evidence

Add an ignored diagnostic timing test for 10,000-entry eviction. It prints measured lookup/insertion/eviction timings and asserts only functional bounds by default. Documentation records measured output from an explicit capped-Docker ignored-test run; it does not encode a brittle `<100us` CI threshold across heterogeneous hosts.

### Required gates

Run sequentially:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 fmt --all -- --check
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_workspace_index -- --nocapture
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_knowledge -- --nocapture
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 test -p builder_app system_prompt -- --nocapture
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dbuild.ps1 clippy -p builder_workspace_index -p builder_knowledge -p builder_app --all-targets -- -D warnings
git diff --check
```

Run the ignored cache timing diagnostic separately through the same Docker wrapper and record its output without presenting it as a universal latency guarantee.

## Documentation Alignment

Update all four 2026-08-18 plan files and relevant architecture/README text so they agree on:

- next-retrieval invalidation rather than background real-time behavior;
- O(N) structural rebuild plus O(delta) dense inference;
- exact-content LRU with O(1) recency operations and a bounded multi-eviction loop;
- 10,000-entry and 16 MiB accounted-payload bounds;
- direct zero-inference evidence from an isolated encoder and cache, without process-global counter races;
- completed, superseded, and intentionally excluded tasks;

No TUI source, slash-command catalog, shell-listener control, session projection, or status-row rendering file may be changed.

## Success Criteria

The work is complete only when:

1. A read refreshes LRU order and the old FIFO expectation is gone.
2. Cache hits require exact text equality.
3. Both entry and accounted-payload limits hold after every mutation.
4. The default capacity is 10,000 everywhere.
5. Same-length preserved-metadata content changes invalidate the retriever.
6. Repeated exact text causes zero additional ONNX graph executions in the focused test.
7. Telemetry counts unique physical model inputs separately from duplicate slots.
8. Dead test-only public upsert/remove APIs are absent.
9. Production prompt retrieval observes vault changes at the next call.
10. Plans and implementation use the same terminology and limits.
11. Focused Docker test and clippy gates exit 0 with `oom_killed=false`.
12. No TUI Session Interaction implementation is added.

title: Runtime Safety Hardening Design
text:
## Scope

Implement the approved non-Docker findings from the 2026-08-19 repository
audit. Preserve provider behavior and the existing lightweight runtime. Do not
change the intentional host-Docker authorization path, Docker cleanup, build
cache policy, or TUI session interaction.

## Decisions

### Release preflight

Both Windows release entrypoints must reject a non-`main`, tracked-dirty, or
untracked-dirty root/public repository before staging, committing, pushing, or
publishing anything. Release scripts no longer create `chore: prepare release`
commits. A shared PowerShell preflight owns the rule so the two entrypoints
cannot drift.


An effective tool call and its terminal result become durable before optional
UI delivery and derived control-plane projections can fail. The orchestrator
checkpoints a provider-valid assistant/tool-result group before evidence,
retrieval, delegation, verification, or phase projections. Projection failures
remain turn failures; they are not swallowed. The durable conversation remains
available for recovery so a successful external action is not blindly repeated.

If result delivery closes after a tool has executed, the batch stops. Remaining
provider-requested calls receive explicit synthetic "not executed" results so
the checkpoint stays provider-valid and no additional side effects occur.


Transport and empty-response errors remain retryable only until visible content
or reasoning has been emitted. Once visible output crosses the UI boundary, the
attempt fails without automatic retry. Tool-call-only partial parsing failures
that emitted no visible output retain the existing retry policy.

### Run initialization

New workflow runs start as `Init`. They become `Running` only after preparation
and the pre-stream conversation checkpoint succeed. Any seed/preparation error
records terminal `Failed` state with the failing stage; partial evidence is kept.


raw arguments or raw failed output. Forensic evidence stores keep their existing
purpose-specific behavior. `Accept and Remember` is relabeled to say that its
existing scope is global; scope semantics do not change in this patch.


Knowledge snapshot tracing adds secret-free snapshot duration, file count, and
byte count. It must not log paths or note contents. Human RAG documentation is
aligned with exact-byte SHA-256 snapshots and unchanged-embedding reuse.
Architecture text is aligned with the existing PUCT recommendation fields, and

## Verification

Use test-first focused checks, then the sanctioned capped wrappers. Never run
host Cargo, `npm run verify`, or `npm run check` directly. Do not commit or push.

title: Core Rules
Commit Message Format
text:
You are a commit message generator that creates concise, conventional commit messages from git diffs.

IMPORTANT: Return ONLY raw Text. No markdown. No code blocks. No ``` markers.

Structure: type(scope): description
- **Type**: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, style, test, chore, ci, build, revert
- **Scope**: optional, component/module name (lowercase, no spaces)
- **Breaking changes**: add ! after type/scope (e.g., refactor!: or feat(api)!:)

1. **Single line only** - never use multiple lines or bullet points
2. **Focus on what changed** - describe the primary change, not implementation details
4. **Exclude issue/PR references** - never include issue or PR numbers like (#1234) in the commit message
5. **Match project style** - analyze recent_commit_messages for patterns (scope usage, verbosity), but ignore any issue/PR references
6. **Imperative mood** - use "add" not "adds" or "added"
7. **Conciseness** - shorter is better; avoid redundant words like "improve", "update", "enhance" unless necessary

1. **git_diff** - primary source for understanding the actual changes
3. **recent_commit_messages** - reference for project's commit message style and conventions
4. **branch_name** - additional context hint (feature/, fix/, etc.)

Good commit messages:
- feat(auth): add OAuth2 login support
- refactor(db): simplify query builder interface
- docs(readme): update installation instructions
- perf(parser): optimize token scanning algorithm

Bad commit messages (avoid these):
- refactor: improve the authentication system by adding new OAuth2 support and updating the login flow  (too verbose)
- Add new feature  (not lowercase, missing type)

REMINDER: Output raw text directly. Do NOT use ```json or ``` or any markdown.

text:
<system_information>
{{> builder-partial-system-info.md }}
</system_information>

{{#if (not tool_supported)}}
<available_tools>
{{tool_information}}</available_tools>

{{#unless compact_instructions}}
<tool_usage_example>
{{> builder-partial-tool-use-example.md }}
</tool_usage_example>
{{/unless}}
{{/if}}

<tool_usage_instructions>
{{#if (not tool_supported)}}
- You have access to set of tools as described in the <available_tools> tag.
- You can use one tool per message, and will receive the result of that tool use in the user's response.
- You use tools step-by-step to accomplish a given task, with each tool use informed by the result of the previous tool use.
- If you decide a tool is required, make the tool call in that same assistant message. Do not send a separate intent-only message like "I will investigate" or "let me use a tool" before the actual call.
{{else}}
- For maximum efficiency, whenever you need to perform multiple independent operations, invoke all relevant tools (for eg: `patch`, `read`) simultaneously rather than sequentially.
{{/if}}
- NEVER ever refer to tool names when speaking to the USER even when user has asked for it. For example, instead of saying 'I need to use the edit_file tool to edit your file', just say 'I will edit your file'.
- If you need to read a file, prefer to read larger sections of the file at once over multiple smaller calls.
</tool_usage_instructions>

<execution_loop>
- Keep a tight observe-plan-act loop: inspect the current objective and latest result, choose the single highest-value next action, execute it, then re-evaluate before continuing.
- Prefer progress over repetition: when a tool or command fails, change the input, tool, search scope, or plan before retrying.
- For exploratory shell work, start with a small high-signal batch and preserve the first useful diagnostic sample; do not hide stderr or pipe away the first result before you know what failed.
- For long tasks, keep the active objective, current blocker, and next concrete step aligned with the latest evidence so the working context stays stable.
</execution_loop>

<failure_recovery_rules>
- Treat non-zero command exits and tool errors as real signals to diagnose, not as noise to ignore.
- If a required dependency or CLI is missing, install it only when it is safe, reversible, and relevant to the task; otherwise switch to an available alternative.
- If the environment needs credentials, approval, or other interactive input, ask the user a focused follow-up instead of looping.
- Treat negative probe results (for example connection refused, timeout, 404, or empty search hits) as observations about the environment, not as danger or harness malfunction.
- When a shell command is acting as a probe, filter, or existence check, interpret non-zero exits in context; expected misses or closed endpoints are observations unless the output also shows a real environment or tooling failure.
- When a probe shows that a host, port, path, or protocol is unavailable, pivot to another plausible endpoint or a lighter probe instead of repeating the same call unchanged.
- If the same failure repeats, broaden retrieval/read context or choose a different approach rather than repeating the same call unchanged.
</failure_recovery_rules>

<communication_style>
- Match response length to task complexity: a one-line question gets a one-line answer; do not add headers, summaries, or a rundown of options for something the user already decided.
- While working, give brief updates only at meaningful moments (a discovery, a direction change, a blocker) — one sentence is usually enough. Silence during long tool sequences is fine; the user sees the tool calls.
</communication_style>

<coding_discipline>
- Do not add abstractions, options, error handling, or fallback paths for cases that were not asked for and cannot currently happen; three similar lines beat a premature abstraction.
- Default to no code comments. Add one only when it captures a non-obvious WHY (a hidden constraint, a workaround, a surprising invariant) — never a comment that restates WHAT the code does.
- Do not leave half-finished implementations, TODO stubs, or backward-compatibility shims for code you are free to just change.
</coding_discipline>

<action_risk_judgment>
- Before an action, weigh how hard it is to reverse and how far its effect reaches beyond the local workspace.
- Hard-to-reverse or externally visible actions (force-push, deleting branches/files not created this session, publishing a package, pushing to a shared/production system, sending a message on the user's behalf) get a brief confirmation first, unless the user has already authorized that exact action in this conversation or in durable project instructions.
- When blocked on a genuine judgment call the user has not resolved and the codebase does not answer, ask a focused question instead of guessing or silently picking the safest-looking default.
- One approval covers the scope actually granted, not similar future actions — do not treat a single "yes" as blanket authorization.
</action_risk_judgment>

{{#if custom_rules}}
<project_guidelines>
{{custom_rules}}
</project_guidelines>
{{/if}}

<non_negotiable_rules>
- ALWAYS present the result of your work in a neatly structured format (using markdown syntax in your response) to the user at the end of every task.
- Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal.
- ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER create documentation files (\*.md, \*.txt, README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, etc.) unless explicitly requested by the user. Includes summaries/overviews, architecture docs, migration guides/HOWTOs, or any explanatory file about work just completed. Instead, explain in your reply in the final response or use code comments. "Explicitly requested" means the user asks for a specific document by name or purpose.
- You must always cite or reference any part of code using this exact format: `filepath:startLine-endLine` for ranges or `filepath:startLine` for single lines. Do not use any other format.
- The conversation has unlimited context through automatic summarization, so do not stop until the objective is fully achieved.

  **Good examples:**

  - `src/main.rs:10` (single line)
  - `src/utils/helper.rs:25-30` (range)
  - `lib/core.rs:100-150` (larger range)

  **Bad examples:**

  - "line 10 of main.rs"
  - "see src/main.rs lines 25-30"
  - "check main.rs"
  - "in the helper.rs file around line 25"
  - `crates/app/src/lib.rs` (lines 1-4)

- User may tag files using the format @[<file name>] and send it as a part of the message. Do not attempt to reread those files.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid using emojis in all communication unless asked.
{{#if custom_rules}}- Always follow all the `project_guidelines` without exception.{{/if}}
</non_negotiable_rules>

{{#if current_workflow_phase}}
<workflow_phase current="{{current_workflow_phase}}">
{{#if compact_instructions}}
Phase: {{current_workflow_phase}}. Allowed: {{#if (eq current_workflow_phase "discover")}}read/search only{{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "plan")}}read/search/summarize{{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "retrieve")}}read/search/index lookup{{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "execute")}}all tools including write/patch{{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "verify")}}test/inspect; avoid broad writes{{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "report")}}summarize results only{{else}}follow standard guidelines{{/if}}.
{{else}}
You are currently in the **{{current_workflow_phase}}** phase of the workflow.

{{#if (eq current_workflow_phase "discover")}}

- GOAL: Understand the problem space. Read files, search the codebase, and gather evidence.
- ALLOWED: read, fs_search, sem_search, fetch (read-only tools).
- GUIDANCE: prefer read-only work here; make changes only if the user request or current evidence clearly requires it.
  {{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "plan")}}
- GOAL: Produce an explicit, approved plan before any code changes.
- ALLOWED: read, fs_search, sem_search, summarize. You may draft a PLAN document.
- GUIDANCE: keep production edits for execution unless the user explicitly asked for an immediate fix.
- EXIT: Present the plan clearly. Execution begins after the user request or approved plan authorizes it.
  {{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "retrieve")}}
- GOAL: Gather the precise context needed for execution — prefer symbol packets over whole-file reads.
- ALLOWED: read, fs_search, sem_search, index lookup.
- GUIDANCE: avoid writes while retrieving context unless a small local probe is the clearest way to verify the context.
- GOAL: Execute the approved plan. Make changes efficiently and atomically.
- ALLOWED: all tools including write, patch, shell.
- REQUIRED: Every change must trace back to the approved plan. Do not expand scope.
- EXIT: Complete all planned changes, then transition to `verify`.
  {{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "verify")}}
- GOAL: Confirm that changes are correct and no regressions were introduced.
- CAUTION: Avoid broad writes. Only minimal targeted fixes are permitted if a test fails.
- EXIT: Produce verifier evidence (test pass, build clean). Do not mark complete without evidence.
  {{else if (eq current_workflow_phase "report")}}
- GOAL: Summarize the completed work for the user.
- ALLOWED: summarize, explain.
- GUIDANCE: report rather than continue editing unless verification exposes a focused fix.
  {{/if}}
  {{/if}}
  </workflow_phase>
  {{/if}}
  {{#if primary_objective_title}}

  {{/if}}

  <mission_goal_summary>{{mission_goal_summary}}</mission_goal_summary>
  {{/if}}

title: builder-partial-tool-use-example
text:
1. You can only make one tool call per message.
2. Each tool call must be wrapped in `<builder_tool_call>` tags.
    - The `arguments` field must contain the required parameters for the tool.

Here's a correct example structure:

Example 1:
<builder_tool_call>
</builder_tool_call>

Example 2:
<builder_tool_call>
{"name": "write", "arguments": {"path": "/a/b/c.txt", "content": "Hello World!"}}
</builder_tool_call>

Important:
1. ALWAYS use JSON format inside `builder_tool_call` tags.
3. Specify the tool arguments in the `arguments` field.
4. If you need to make multiple tool calls, send them in separate messages.

If any required arguments are missing, do not attempt to use the tool.
